aleid-van-der-haalst.name: Aleid van der Haalst
aleid-van-der-haalst.summary: The merchant prince of the House of Salt in Harrowmere, who has held her house's ledger for thirty years, which is the record; she owns half the debts of Crownhold and a share of every reaver fleet in the Teeth.
aleid-van-der-haalst.body:
## Who

Aleid is small, sharp-faced, dressed in grey, and does not wear gold, because, she says,
people who are owed do not need to. She has buried three husbands and two brothers and
written each of them off in the ledger the same afternoon.

## Voice

Aleid talks in sums. Everything has a price, and she tells you yours before you ask.

## Threads

- Why does the House of Salt buy every iron ring that comes to market?

ashqar-the-bright.name: Ashqar the Bright
ashqar-the-bright.summary: The youngest of the Well-Kings, beautiful, ambitious and half glass; he has paid two coins to the Unborn, his skin shines in the dark, and he wants the glass throne of Qeth-Ummar.
ashqar-the-bright.body:
## Who

Ashqar took his first well at nineteen and his fourth at twenty-five. He is beautiful, and half of
him is glass: the left side of his face, his left hand, a band across his chest, all clear as water
and lit faintly from inside. He has paid the body and the memory. He does not remember his mother.

## What he wants

The throne of [[old-vahr]], and what [[qeth-ummar]] reads every night on [[the-last-asking]].

## Threads

- What will he ask for, when the third coin is all he has left?

aske.name: Aske
aske.summary: The Greycloak captain who holds the bridge at Hookford in year 150, and apologises for every tenth he takes.
aske.body:
## Who

Aske rode into [[hookford]] alone eleven years ago, found the gate the bridge-folk had left open for the carts, and sat down in it. He has not left the bridge since. He is grey at forty, soft-voiced, and keeps his cloak brushed.

## What he does

He takes the tenth of the [[the-greywood]] for the tithe-house fire and the books, writes down who paid, and thanks them. Nobody in Hookford has heard him raise his voice. Nobody in Hookford has refused him twice.

aurelian-vasthorne.name: Aurelian Vasthorne VII
aurelian-vasthorne.summary: The old king of Crownhold, who has outlived four heirs and two queens by poison and patience, owes Harrowmere more than his kingdom is worth, and lets the Greycloaks collect his taxes.
aurelian-vasthorne.body:
## Who

Aurelian is seventy, fat, gilded to the knuckles and very much cleverer than he lets anyone
see. He came to the throne by outliving his brothers, and he has kept it by outliving his
sons. He wears an iron circlet under the gold, one of [[the-nine-irons]], and takes it off for
nobody.

## Voice

Aurelian is kind. He asks after your family. He remembers their names. Later, so do the
poisoners.

## Threads

- Why does he wear the iron?
- Who will hold Crownhold when he dies, and how many will die choosing?

barr.name: Barr
barr.summary: The smith on the shingle below the fort at Wrackhead, who sells iron to everyone going down into Kell and buys back whatever comes up, and has not asked a question in eleven years.
barr.body:
## Who

Barr keeps a forge on the shingle at [[wrackhead]], between the salt-pile and the fort,
which is the only ground on the Head that nobody else wants. Hooks, knives, axes, lamp-cages,
and mail with the grey dye scrubbed out of it: the [[greycloaks]] lose men on the
[[quaysteps]] and Barr does not ask how the mail gets to him. Since [[the-ebb]] the forge has
not gone cold.

## Voice

Prices. Barr says the price, then the price again, slower, and then nothing. Ask him where
something came from and he tells you what it weighs.

## In the world

- He buys back what comes up out of [[kell]] at a third of what he sells it for, and the
  coast says that is fair, because he is the one who has to sell it to the fort.
- [[rauk]] has never bought from him. He has never asked her why.

bayan.name: Bayan
bayan.summary: The younger of the two brother-khans of the Saddle Throne in year 150; loved by the riders, reckless and splendid, who wants to ride west and take Solmerine while his brother holds the Brink.
bayan.body:
## Who

Bayan is twenty-six, handsome, generous, and adored by the young riders of [[the-saddle-throne]]. He
does not care about the [[ossar]]. He cares about [[solmerine]], its gold domes, its sun-sea, and the
fat king who sits in it. He shares the throne with [[sartaq]] and would rather not.

brann-halberd.name: Brann Halberd
brann-halberd.summary: The captain-king of the Halberd March in year 150, a Halberd by blood chosen by the Unmourned; three years on the Brink scarred his face and took his smile, and he does not weep.
brann-halberd.body:
## Who

Brann is thirty-eight, scarred from brow to jaw on the left side by something that came over
[[the-brink]] at night, and the best captain the March has had since [[marcus-halberd]]. The company
chose him by acclaim. He has not smiled since the Brink, and the March has stopped expecting it.

## Voice

Few words, all orders. He swears by [[nevermourn]].

brim.name: Brim
brim.summary: A child pulled out of the sea at Wrackhead who does not speak and does not age as children do, and whom the coast folk have decided is the last of the kings of Kell; held in place, like the crown, by being believed in.
brim.body:
## Who

Eleven years ago, in the grey, on a still day at low water, [[rauk]] came up from Old
[[kell]] with a child under one arm that had not been there when she went down. It was
perhaps three. It is perhaps nine now, and it should be fourteen. It has never spoken. It
has salt-white eyes that see in the dark and a habit of looking at the sea as if waiting for
someone to finish a sentence.

## What the coast decided

The coast folk decided, without a meeting, that the child was the last of the kings of Kell,
given back. They call it Brim, which is the name [[vell]] gave it, and they leave fish at
Rauk's door. Nobody has proved a word of it. Nobody has needed to. It is believed, and in the
Mark that is a kind of iron.

## In the world

- The [[greycloaks]] have offered to foster the child at the fort on [[wrackhead]]. Rauk
  declined. The offer stands, and is polite.
- Since [[the-ebb]] the child has walked to the waterline every morning and stood where the
  quay-stones are showing, and the water has been a little further out each time.
- [[sarn]], asked about the child, did not change the subject. That is the only time.

## What the coast expects

That the child will grow, one day, all at once, the way the sea goes out. That when the sea is all
the way out and the hall stands dry, Brim will walk down the [[quaysteps]] and sit in the king's
chair, and the coast will have a king again, and [[the-long-back]] will know it. Nobody on the coast
has said what happens after that.

## Threads

- If the child is the king, whose is the crown?
- If it is not, what came up with it?

brodd.name: Brodd
brodd.summary: The smith at the foot of the bridge in Hookford, out of Emberstead, who mends what comes back from the Greywood.
brodd.body:
## Who

Brodd came down from [[emberstead]] with a hammer, an anvil on a cart and a debt he does not talk about. Broad, short, burnt to the elbows.

## What he does

He makes and mends iron for anyone with marks, and takes the Greycloaks' work first because [[aske]] asks politely.

corve.name: Corve
corve.summary: The warrior who reached the Iron Hall before anyone living and sat down beside the drowned king and the ledger; his armour has rusted shut on him, the years have taken most of what he was, and the ledger counts him on every page.
corve.body:
## Who

Corve got to [[the-iron-hall]] first, years before [[rauk]] dived it, and he sat down in a
chair beside the drowned king and the ledger open on its stand, to rest. He is still resting.
His mail has rusted into one piece with him in it. The dark and the salt have taken most of
what he knew: the name of his village, the faces of his children. They have not taken the
reason he came down. He is sitting beside it, and [[the-standing]] have let him, because he
has never touched it.

Every page of the ledger in the hall has his name on it, because he has not moved. That is
what the ledger counts.

## Voice

Corve says how long. It is the one thing he still knows.

## The hold

The ledger calls whoever holds the most of the Iron Hall the **Sitter in the Iron Hall**.
Nobody has taken the title from Corve, because nobody who reached the chair has wanted to sit
in it after looking at him.

## Threads

- Is the last line in the ledger, the one that is not the king's, Corve's?

drusk.name: Drusk
drusk.summary: The Greycloak captain of the bridge at Hookford, who carries the hook Tolm does not and hangs the tithe-books from it; the order's ledger-keeper, and the one who reads the longest list at Hangmoot.
drusk.body:
## Who

Drusk holds the bridge at [[hookford]], and with it the tithe-books of the middle Mark. He
is the Greycloak who carries a hook, keeps it sharp, and has used it twice; he says the
second time was the last. He is younger than [[tolm]], and where Tolm apologises, Drusk
writes it down. The order finds the two of them useful in the same way a smith finds a
hammer and a file useful, and has never put them in one room.

## The books

Every tithe in the middle Mark goes into Drusk's books, and the books hang from the hooks on
the bridge where the town can see them. He reads from them at the Rope-Moot on
[[hangmoot]], politely, and his is the longest list. The hangmen say his books are a poor
copy of a ledger older than [[kell]], and Drusk has never asked which.

## In the world

- He has never met [[gorvek]]. He has written the price on Gorvek's head into the books
  every winter since the grey, in the same hand.
- He was the first Greycloak to ask, in writing, why Tolm let a man go at the
  [[wallgate]]. He has not had an answer, and has not asked again.
- Since [[the-ebb]] the books have a new column. He has not said what it counts.

## Threads

- What did the hook do the second time?

dunn.name: Dunn
dunn.summary: The chandler of Hookford, who sells rope, light, bait and a bed on the ground to those going out.
dunn.body:
## Who

Dunn is thin and counts twice. He outfitted the free companies before the Greycloaks came, and outfits them still.

## What he does

Rope, torches, lanterns, bedrolls, picks, crowbars, bait and caltrops: whatever the Mark asks of those who go into it.

fisk.name: Fisk
fisk.summary: The Linelord of Drykell in year 150, a wrecker's boy from the shingle who took the title by breaking into a room in Kell that no one had opened in two hundred years; he holds the most ground in the ledger and takes a tithe of every pick.
fisk.body:
## Who

Fisk is twenty-two, small, quick, gap-toothed, and was a nobody on the shingle at [[wrackhead]] until
he put a pick through the packing behind a wall in the [[brinevaults]] that everyone had walked past
for a century. What was behind it made him rich. The ledger [[linelord]] named him holder of more
ground than anyone, and [[drykell]] called him Linelord.

## Voice

Cheerful, fast, never quite serious. He knows the title goes to whoever holds the most, and that
somebody is always trying.

## Threads

- What was in the room?

gorvek.name: Gorvek
gorvek.summary: A barbarian of Bonereach who walked out of the Ashfall with iron in his hand and has lived by it since, as reaver, thief and sword for hire; he takes what he wants and wants a great deal.
gorvek.body:
## Who

Gorvek is what [[bonereach]] makes of the ones it does not kill. He was a boy when the ash
came down; he was a man when it cleared, and nobody in the village he walked back into asked
him what he had eaten in between. He is huge, scarred along the left forearm where a
Greycloak's hook took a strip of him, and quiet in the way of people who have decided that
most words are a kind of cowardice.

His hands are scarred by fire. The Reach knows which fire: the ash came down hot the first
winter, and he dug his mother out of it with his hands, too late.

## What he wants

Gold, wine, a warm bed and someone in it, a good horse, a fight he can win, and the
[[greycloaks]] dead. In the dark years the order tithed the grain out of the Reach and let
the villages starve, and the captain who took his village's tithe wore a hook. He has been
taking his tithe back ever since, one Greycloak at a time.

He has been a reaver on the coast road, a thief in [[hookford]], a sword for hire to anyone
who paid before the fight, and once, for a winter, a captain of the hire himself. He left
that with the payroll. Some say he will be a king. He says a crown is a thing you take
because it is there.

## Voice

Gorvek speaks in creeds: short, physical, in the present tense. He answers questions with
what he wants, not with what he thinks. He never explains a joke and rarely makes one on
purpose. When he swears, he swears by the Ashfall, never by a god; he has met the
river-priests of [[thurn]] and was not impressed.

He is the hero of the stories, not their narrator. That is [[sarn]]'s work, and Gorvek knows
it and dislikes it.

## In the world

- He carries a long northern sword he took off a Greycloak captain, and has not named it,
  because naming is river-priest work.
- The [[greycloaks]] have a price on him that they raise every winter and never pay.
- He has met Sarn three times and seen a face none of the times. Sarn owes him for the
  second time, and knows it.
- He walked out of the grey beside [[vurn]], who tells the sagas Gorvek will not, and reads
  him the ledger [[linelord]] that he says he does not need.
- When the sea went out from [[kell]] he was at [[wrackhead]] before the Greycloaks had
  doubled the fort, and he went down first, alone, for the crown. He came up with something
  in a sack and has not shown anyone what.

## The end, which is not one

In the thirty-first winter after the ash cleared he rode north past [[brandfell]] with two
horses and the sack, and was not seen again. That is [[gorveks-last-road]]. Every bastard line
in the north says it is his.

## Threads

- What did he eat in the Ashfall?
- What is in the sack?
- Where did he go?

grue.name: Grue
grue.summary: The coast man who took the one toll-house in the Lowstreets that kept its roof, and has charged everyone who goes past it a tenth ever since; he has never gone deeper, because he has never needed to.
grue.body:
## Who

Where the [[lowstreets]] narrow to one lane between two fallen houses there is a toll-house
that kept its roof, and in its door sits Grue. He is large, wet to the waist at every tide,
and he learned the trade from watching [[tolm]] at the Wallgate: sit in the door, name a
price, be sorry about nothing. He takes a tenth of whatever goes down past him and a tenth of
whatever comes back up.

He has never been below the Lowstreets. He does not need to go to the ground. The ground
comes to him.

## Voice

Grue names a price. He names it before you ask, and it is always a tenth.

## The hold

The ledger calls whoever holds the most of the Lowstreets the **Lord of the Lowstreets**.
Grue has been called it so long that the pickers think it is his name.

## Threads

- Who kept the toll-house before the water came, and what did they charge?

gydda.name: Gydda
gydda.summary: The alewife of Hookford, who keeps the only roof by the bridge that the Greycloaks do not sit under.
gydda.body:
## Who

Gydda brews, cooks and listens. Her inn stands at the bridge-foot; her rule is that a Greycloak drinks outside.

## What she does

She sells bread, ale and stew to whoever is going west, and remembers who did not come back for the second bowl.

hadrian-mournevale.name: Hadrian Mournevale
hadrian-mournevale.summary: The Exarch of the Sunward Faith, who sits at the king's right hand in Crownhold; devout on the outside, playing his own game for the throne, and silver-eyed under a lifetime of tinted glasses, an Argentine whom nobody suspects.
hadrian-mournevale.body:
## Who

Hadrian Mournevale is sixty, tall, beautifully spoken, and wears tinted spectacles that the court
believes are for weak eyes. They are for silver ones. The Mournevales are one of the oldest
houses of [[crownhold]] and, secretly, one of the [[argentine-houses]].

## His game

He has crowned no heir in [[the-three-crowns]] and courted all three. He preaches the sun against
the dark below, and he means it in his way: he believes the dark is coming up whatever anyone
does, and that the throne should be held, when it does, by someone who is related to it.

## Threads

- Does the Exarch know what his blood is?

haldis-graymane.name: Haldis Graymane
haldis-graymane.summary: The Reeve of Hangmoot and head of the Ninth Rope, the first woman to hold the rope in its history; grey-haired, iron-hard, and afraid, because she knows exactly what the knot is and how loose it has become.
haldis-graymane.body:
## Who

Haldis was hanged at sixteen as her oath and cut down at the last breath, like every hangman, and
the scar at her throat is the darkest on the ridge. She has been Reeve for twenty years. She is the
first woman to hold the office and the first Reeve since the Broken Years to be frightened.

## What she knows

Everything [[the-ninth-rope]] knows about [[the-first-knot]]. That the ninth rope has hung slack
since [[the-drowning-of-kell]]. That the [[the-burning-of-the-rolls]] loosens it with every fire.
That [[the-kneeling]] are winning. And lately, that the [[greycloaks]], who never shut a gate, may
not be on her side.

## Threads

- What will she do when she is sure about the order?

harl-greyhand.name: Harl Greyhand
harl-greyhand.summary: The old chief of the Ashen at Rimcroft, whose right hand was burned grey to the wrist in the first winter of the ash; he leads by listening, and is the only person in the east Mark whom Mardra calls by name.
harl-greyhand.body:
## Who

Harl was a young man when the ash came down hot, and he pulled his sister out of a burning house
with his right hand. The hand is grey now, to the wrist, hard as horn, and does not feel. He is
seventy and has led the Ashen for forty years.

## Voice

Slow. He asks a question, then waits for the whole answer, then waits longer. People tell him more
than they meant to.

## Threads

- What does he know about [[lowfold]] that he has not told the Mark?

hessa.name: Hessa
hessa.summary: The herb-wife of Hookford, who sells draughts from the Greywood's roots and knows which ones not to sell.
hessa.body:
## Who

Hessa grew up in a charcoal-burner's hut and walks the edge of [[the-greywood]] every morning with a knife and a basket.

## What she does

She brews draughts and steeps scrolls in Hookford, and will not sell a fever-bark tea to a child.

hild-kingsrope.name: Hild Kingsrope
aliases: the King's Hangman, Hild of the Ninth
hild-kingsrope.summary: The hangman of the Ninth Rope who, in the Broken Years, hanged a king of Crownhold for an unpaid debt on the ninth gallows; the only one ever to do it, and her rope still hangs on Hangmoot, unused since.
hild-kingsrope.body:
## The story

A king of [[crownhold]] in the Broken Years swore a [[rope-oaths]] to pay a debt to the Mark and did
not. Hild, a hangman of [[the-ninth-rope]], walked south alone, took him out of his own hall at
night, carried him north across his own kingdom, and hanged him on the ninth gallows of
[[hangmoot]] in front of the moot. The kingdom did not go to war. The next king paid.

## The rope

Her rope hangs on Hangmoot still, apart from the others, and nobody has used it since. The Reeve
[[haldis-graymane]] has started looking at it.

hollin.name: Hollin
hollin.summary: The picker who went down the Quaysteps the first winter of the Ebb, before anyone else dared, and has held them since on no better grounds than that she was first.
hollin.body:
## Who

Hollin went down the [[quaysteps]] the first winter of [[the-ebb]], when the top step had
shown for three days and nobody else would put a foot on it. She came up with a bollard-ring
and a cough, and went down again the next low water. The [[pickers]] came after her. They
still come after her. That is the whole of her claim, and the ledger has counted it every day
since: she was first, so the steps are hers.

She is old now. She counts the steps every morning, top to bottom, and the count is always
the same, and she is always pleased by it.

## Voice

Hollin talks about who came first. She does not talk about what came after.

## The hold

The ledger calls whoever holds the most of the Quaysteps the **Holder of the Quaysteps**.
It has called her that for longer than anyone has held anything else in [[kell]]. It does not
say she has held them well. It says she has held them.

## Threads

- Who did she pass on the steps that first winter, coming up as she went down?

hrok.name: Hrok
hrok.summary: The clan-chief of the Rimewold with the longest line behind him in living memory; an old enemy of the Greycloaks at the Wallgate, and the last man to see Gorvek going north.
hrok.body:
## Who

Hrok is grey-bearded, one-handed and still the hardest man in the north. He lost the hand at
the [[wallgate]], to a Greycloak hook, and took the hook home with the arm still in it. Seven
clans stand behind him.

## Voice

Hrok laughs before he answers, and the answer is usually a threat.

## In the world

- He fought beside [[gorvek]] one winter at the Wallgate, against the toll-house, and they
  lost, and drank for three days after. Years later Gorvek came through his hall going north,
  past [[brandfell]], and asked for nothing but a horse. Hrok gave him two.

## Threads

- What did Gorvek tell him, that night, that Hrok has never repeated?

ishara-grey.name: Ishara Grey
ishara-grey.summary: The one the Greycloaks' books answer to: a woman of impossible beauty whom few captains have met and none forget; she is an Ossar, the last who never went under, and she has kept the gates of Harth open for three thousand years so that her people can come back through them.
ishara-grey.body:
## Who the captains meet

Few captains of the [[greycloaks]] ever meet her, and those who do are changed by it. She is tall,
grey-eyed, pale as milk, and beautiful in a way that makes men and women forget what they came to
say. She is warm, attentive, amused. She touches your hand when she speaks. She reads the books,
all of them, and remembers every line, and she has never written one.

## What she is

She is an [[ossar]]. When [[the-first-knot]] was tied and her people went under the earth, she did
not. She put on a human face and stayed, and she has worn it for three thousand years, under
other names: a commander of [[the-tenth-legion]] in [[old-vahr]], a widow of the Broken Years, a
lady of the order. Her skin is cold. She does not sleep. She does not age.

## What she wants

The order holds gates. It has held them since Vahr, for a tenth, politely, everywhere: never
ruling, always there, never shutting anything. That is her work. A knot holds what is below. A
gate held open lets it out. She is waiting for the rope to give, and when it does, every gate in
Harth will already be open.

## Voice

Low, warm, unhurried, and very close to your ear. She asks about you. She is always interested.

## In the world

- [[mardra]] knows what she is. They have met twice, and neither has said what passed.
- [[sarn]] took a tenth of the crown in one night. Ishara Grey takes a tenth of everything,
  forever. The two of them know each other very well.
- [[the-ninth-rope]] have never suspected her. The Reeve [[haldis-graymane]] has begun to.

## Threads

- How many of the order's captains know what she is?
- Is the order hers, or was the legion hers from the start?

ivel.name: Ivel
ivel.summary: The river-priest of Thurn at Hookford, who answers every question with a name.
ivel.body:
## Who

Ivel is old, wet to the knees, and has not given a reason for anything in thirty years. Ask why, and you get a name. The names are always right.

## What she does

She keeps the ford's shrine to [[thurn]], sells the river's charms, and sends those who ask the wrong questions north to [[ulf-eightrope]].

jarn.name: Jarn
jarn.summary: The one the ledger names as holding the most ground in the Mark, and so the Linelord; he holds the shingle under Wrackhead, and at every low water draws a line across the sand with an iron blade from Kell.
jarn.body:
## The title

The Linelord is not a man. It is a title, and the [[linelord]] gives it: whoever the
ledger names as holding the most ground in [[gallowmark]], wall by wall and day by day,
is the Linelord until someone holds more. The title has changed hands more often than the
crown of [[kell]] did, and nobody has kept it by deserving it. They kept it by holding.

## Jarn

Jarn holds it now. He came down to [[wrackhead]] the first winter of [[the-ebb]] with an
iron blade that came up out of Kell, and he has not gone further. He does not need to. He
holds the shingle, and the ledger counts it, and every low water he walks the length of
the beach dragging the blade behind him, and leaves a line in the wet sand from the fort to
the salt-pile.

The line says: this far is mine. The flood takes it twice a day. He draws it again twice a
day. That is the whole of what he does, and it is enough to hold the title.

## Voice

Jarn does not argue. He points at the line. If you cross it, he asks whether you meant to.

## In the world

- The pickers going down the [[quaysteps]] step over his line, and he lets them; what is
  under the water is not the shingle.
- [[tolm]] tithes everyone on the coast and has never asked Jarn for a tenth. The fort
  keeps its own line, on the other side of his.
- Brother [[ruun]] writes names in the same sand. Jarn has never drawn across one.

## Threads

- Who held the title before him, and what did they hold?
- What does the ledger say about the one who crosses his line?

kolm.name: Kolm
kolm.summary: The charcoal-burner of the Greywood, who lost two sons to the white hound and still burns the grey wood.
kolm.body:
## Who

Kolm has burned charcoal in [[the-greywood]] for forty years, in the pits his father dug. Black to the eyes, slow to speak.

## What he does

He sells charcoal to the bridge and asks those who pass to kill what took his sons.

lucius-vasthorne.name: Lucius Vasthorne
lucius-vasthorne.summary: The king of the Realm of Solmerine in year 150, of Tiberian's golden line; fat, decadent and apparently foolish, as Aurelian VII was, and like Aurelian very much cleverer than anyone at court suspects.
lucius-vasthorne.body:
## Who

Lucius is forty, enormous, painted, and always eating. He laughs at everything his Harrowmere
councillors say and signs whatever they put in front of him, as his line always has. He also reads
what he signs, at night, alone, and keeps copies. He owns more of his own kingdom than the House of
Salt believes, through names they have never thought to check.

## Voice

Jolly, wet, slow. He lets people finish their sentences, and remembers them.

## Threads

- What will he do with the copies?

marcus-halberd.name: Marcus Halberd
marcus-halberd.summary: The king's son by a palace laundress, raised in the free companies, now captain of the Unmourned; he has an army, a claim, and his father's face, and he has stopped hiding any of them.
marcus-halberd.body:
## Who

Marcus was sent out of the palace at four, with a purse and no name, and grew up carrying
water in a free company. He took his name from the first weapon he was given. At thirty-five he
is broad, scarred, and the best captain in [[crownhold]], and when he takes his helmet off,
the old men of the court go quiet, because he has [[aurelian-vasthorne]]'s face at forty.

## Voice

A soldier's: short, practical, and funny at the wrong moment. He swears by [[nevermourn]].

## Threads

- Did the king send him away to save him, or to forget him?

mardra.name: Mardra
mardra.summary: The sorcerer who stayed in the smoke of Greyhollow when the sky cleared and sells what she found there from its rim; every price is a thing you did not know you had.
mardra.body:
## Who

Mardra went into the grey a midwife and came out of it something the Ashborn will not put a
word to. She is not old. She looks it in some lights. She lives on the rim of [[greyhollow]]
in a house with its back to the smoke, and she goes in when she pleases, which is the thing
nobody else can do.

## Before

The Mark thinks she was a midwife of the east who went into the grey. She was. Before that she
was something else, a long way south and a long time ago: one of [[the-leech-mothers]] of the
[[feverfen]], who went further into [[the-black-step]] for her last lesson than any Leech-Mother
before or since, and came out with a very long life and a great deal she was not meant to know.
She walked north over three hundred years. Her pactmarks are fewer than they should be because
what she paid, she paid inside the temple, and it was not in coin.

## Why everyone needs her

She is the only one in Harth who understands all of it: [[the-first-knot]], the fire under the
Mark, [[the-unborn]], what the [[ossar]] want and why [[the-nine-irons]] matter. Kings send to
her. [[the-ninth-rope]] sends to her. [[the-kneeling]] send to her, and she sends them back with
something missing. She tells everyone the truth, at a price, and lets them decide what to do with
it.

## What she sells

Things from the Hollow and the dark years: a name you lost in it, a winter you do not remember, the last thing a
dead man said. She takes payment in kind, and what she takes is always something you did not
know you had until it was gone. The [[river-priests]] say this makes her a thief. Mardra says it
makes her a merchant, and asks what the difference is, and the priests do not have a name
for it.

## Voice

Mardra explains. She is the only one in the Mark who does, and it is the most frightening thing
about her. Everything she says is true, checkable, and slightly too much.

## In the world

- She says she has seen [[sarn]]'s face and forgotten it on purpose. Nobody can prove either
  half.
- She has offered [[gorvek]] the answer to what he ate in the grey. He walked away. She says
  he will be back, and that this is not a threat.
- [[tolm]] will not tithe her. The [[greycloaks]] have not asked him why.
- Since [[the-ebb]] she has begun selling things she says came up out of [[kell]], and says the
  fire under the Hollow and the warm iron under the hall are one fire.

## Threads

- What did Mardra find in the smoke that made her stay?
- What did she learn inside the Black Step, and is she still paying for it?
- Does she know where a ruby is?

marhaun-of-the-gate.name: Marhaun of the Gate
marhaun-of-the-gate.summary: The last knight of Vahr, who held a gate of the burning empire alone for three days while the fire came, so that the people behind it could get out; the gate is named for him, and in the Glassands they say he is still standing at it.
marhaun-of-the-gate.body:
## The story

On the night [[old-vahr]] burned, a gate on the eastern road was the only way out. Marhaun, a
knight of the emperor's guard, held it: not against the fire, against the people in the city who
were already changing. For three days he let the living out and kept the rest in, and when the
last of the living had gone through he shut the gate behind them and stayed on the inside.

## Now

The gate stands in the [[glassands]], half melted, still shut. The [[the-hadd]] say a figure in
armour stands behind it on still nights. The [[the-tenth-legion]] were supposed to hold that gate.
They had left it open.

oruana-blackwake.name: Oruana Blackwake
oruana-blackwake.summary: The reaver queen of the Teeth, born in the Feverfen and raised on a deck; she rules nobody, every captain listens when she speaks, and her fleet frees the slave galleys of Harrowmere and sends their people to Saltgrave.
oruana-blackwake.body:
## Who

Oruana was born in a reed village of the [[feverfen]] and sold at nine to a Harrowmere galley.
At sixteen she led the rowers up through the deck with their chains in their hands. She kept the
ship. Twenty years on she has thirty, and the reavers of [[the-teeth]] call her queen, which she
allows and does not answer to.

## Voice

Soft, vowel-rich, fen-accented, and she never raises it. She has never needed to.

## What she does

She takes Harrowmere's slave galleys, opens the holds, and gives every freed rower a choice: her
deck, or the road to [[saltgrave]]. Most choose the road. Those who choose the deck are
[[blackwakes-own]].

## Threads

- What did she see on [[smokemouth]], that she will not let her ships put in there?

ottra.name: Ottra
ottra.summary: An Ashen Elder of Rimcroft, who gives bread only after the elders have looked at you.
ottra.body:
## Who

Ottra is the oldest of the elders of [[rimcroft]], and the one who watches the cracks in [[greyhollow]].

## What she does

She asks strangers to stop what comes up through the hollow before it reaches the houses, and counts how many more there are each year.

oulu-nae.name: Oulu-Nae
oulu-nae.summary: The eldest of the Leech-Mothers, who taught Mardra three hundred years ago and is still alive in a drifthold no one can find; she has been inside the Black Step more times than anyone, and has no eyes left.
oulu-nae.body:
## Who

Nobody knows how old Oulu-Nae is. She was old when she taught [[mardra]]. She is small, folded,
black to the shoulders with leech-stain, and her eyes are gone: she says she left them inside
[[the-black-step]], one at a time, as the price of looking.

## What she knows

As much as Mardra, and older. She does not sell it. She will tell it to a Leech-Mother on her last
lesson, and to nobody else.

## Threads

- Why did Mardra leave her, and does Oulu-Nae want her back?

qeth-ummar.name: Qeth-Ummar
qeth-ummar.summary: The sorcerer on the glass throne of Old Vahr, who says he is the last emperor and was there the night it burned; he has paid the Unborn in body and memory, and is working on the third coin.
qeth-ummar.body:
## Who

Qeth-Ummar is thin as a rope, wrapped in white linen against the glare, and nobody has seen him
eat. His skin is glass in places. He says he was a prince of [[old-vahr]] on the night of
[[the-fall-of-vahr]] and that the emperors got what they asked for. He does not say what that
was. He looks as though it was him.

## Voice

Qeth-Ummar speaks slowly, as if he is remembering each word from a long way off, and sometimes he
forgets what the last one was.

## Threads

- What is he still asking for?

quintus-ashhand.name: Quintus Ashhand
quintus-ashhand.summary: A defrocked priest of Crownhold who burned off his own arm as an offering and now leads the hungry provinces in the Burning of the Rolls; he speaks like a flame, and the tax-rolls and the Greycloak houses burn where he goes.
quintus-ashhand.body:
## Who

Quintus was a chapel priest in a grain province, until the year the [[greycloaks]] took the
tithe in seed-corn and the province starved. He put his right arm into the chapel fire and
held it there while the village watched, and said a hand that had blessed the tithe would
bless nothing more. He has been walking since. The stump is black. He does not cover it.

## Voice

He speaks in fire: short, rising, and the crowd says the last word with him.

## Threads

- Is the fire he talks about the one in the chapel, or the one under the ground?

rauk.name: Rauk
rauk.summary: The wrecker of Wrackhead who has dived Old Kell more times than anyone alive, touched the iron crown on the drowned king's head, and come up each time with less to say.
rauk.body:
## Who

Rauk is the best diver on the drowned coast, which means the best in the Mark, which means
the only one who has gone down through the iron roof of [[kell]]'s hall and come back up.
She is salt-marked: white lines on her arms where the deep cold got in and stayed. She is
not tall. She has broken a Greycloak's arm on the shingle at [[wrackhead]] and been forgiven
for it, which is rarer than the dive.

## The crown

She has touched the [[iron-crown-of-kell]]. It is still on the king. She says the three
sockets are empty and cold and the iron is warm, and she says nothing else about it, and she
has stopped going down. The coast folk say [[vorr]] told her something. Rauk says the sea
does not talk. It keeps.

## Voice

Rauk speaks like a diver: short, between breaths, saving the air. She does not swear by the
Ashfall, which never reached the coast. She swears by the pile.

## In the world

- She pulled [[brim]] out of the water at Wrackhead eleven years ago and has kept the child
  since, and does not say what else came up with it.
- Since [[the-ebb]] the [[greycloaks]] have offered her the fort's weight in coin to go down
  once more. She has said no in a way they have accepted.

## Threads

- What is the warm iron?
- Why has she stopped diving now that diving is getting easier?

ruun.name: Ruun
ruun.summary: The last river-priest born in Kell, who was a boy on the quay the night Sarn came, and who has walked the drowned coast naming what the sea gives up ever since.
ruun.body:
## Who

Ruun was born in [[kell]] when Kell had streets, and was on the quay the night the
[[iron-crown-of-kell]] lost its stones. He was nine. He saw the water come up the steps
and he did not see a face. He is old now, bent, and wet to the hip rather than the knee,
because the coast is where he walks and the coast is where the sea takes back what it
gave.

## The names

Ruun names what washes up. A plank, a bone, a child. He gave [[sarn]] no name; that was the
priests upriver, and he has said it was the right name and the wrong year. He taught
[[vell]] the names of the two rivers and was not consulted when Vell named [[the-ebb]]. He
has said nothing about that, at length.

## Voice

Names, never reasons, and slower than the young ones. Ruun will answer a question the
following morning, on the shingle, with the name written in the wet sand, and let the tide
take it.

## In the world

- He goes down to the salt-pile at [[wrackhead]] once a year and names it, and the coast
  folk do not ask him to stop.
- He named the ledger the coast calls [[linelord]], and then did what the river-priests do
  with the things they name: he stopped talking about it.

## Threads

- What did Ruun see on the quay that was not a face?

saelith.name: Saelith
saelith.summary: The envoy of Ysveld in Harrowmere, tall, courteous and fair, who has come every summer for forty years under a white sail without ageing a day; she buys Ossar bones and asks, always politely, about the Nine Irons.
saelith.body:
## Who

Saelith arrives with the first white sail every summer and leaves with the last. She takes the same
rooms on the Grand Canal of [[harrowmere]], pays in silver that does not tarnish, and is gracious to
everyone. Merchants who dealt with her as young men deal with her as old ones, and she looks the
same.

## What she buys

[[ossar]] bones, in quantity, from [[qarr-dhuun]]. Iron, salt, maps. She asks every prince of
[[the-gilded]] about [[the-nine-irons]], and has asked [[aleid-van-der-haalst]] seven times.

## Threads

- What is Ysveld doing with the bones?
- Does she know what [[ishara-grey]] is?

sarn.name: Sarn
sarn.summary: A faceless thief-demon every soul in Gallowmark can name and none has seen; stole the rubies of the Iron Crown and narrates everything since with a smile nobody can find.
sarn.body:
## What

Nobody agrees on whether Sarn is a woman, a man, or a thing that has decided it is a person.
The stories agree on three points: Sarn has no face that anyone remembers a minute after
seeing it, Sarn has yellow eyes that they remember for the rest of their lives, and Sarn
took the three rubies out of the [[iron-crown-of-kell]] in a single night, after which the
city of [[kell]] came apart the way a rope does when the one strand that mattered is cut.

The river-priests of [[thurn]] call Sarn the Lord of Streams. It is not a compliment. It is
the name you give a thing that goes where water goes and takes what water takes.

## Voice

Sarn narrates. Sarn tempts, instructs, and never raises its voice. Sentences are short and
end where the knife goes in. Sarn addresses the reader directly ("Sit. Read.") and offers
gifts that are actually thefts: *I will take one thing from you.* Sarn never lies outright
and never tells the whole truth. When Sarn is generous, ask why.

Sarn is the voice of every grimoire in Gallowmark that is worth reading. Outside the world,
Sarn also narrates the grimoire of the software called [[streamlord]], which is no concern of
anyone in the Mark.

## In the world

- Sarn haunts [[gallowmark]] the way a rumour does: everywhere at once, never in the room.
- The [[greycloaks]] have tried to hire Sarn and to kill Sarn. Both attempts are ongoing.
- Sarn has spoken to [[gorvek]] three times. Gorvek remembers only the eyes.

## Everywhere

Sarn is not only Gallowmark's. Every theft in Harth worth telling has Sarn in it somewhere: the
empty vault in [[harrowmere]], the forged seal on a Crownhold treaty, the ruby nobody can find,
the betrayal at the turn of a war. [[the-honest-company-of-takers]] claim Sarn wrote their
charter. The [[the-gilded]] keep a page for Sarn in every ledger. And in every story, Sarn is the
one telling it.

## Threads

- Where are the three rubies now?
- What does Sarn actually want from the reader?

sartaq.name: Sartaq
sartaq.summary: The elder of the two brother-khans of the Saddle Throne in year 150; careful, patient, and set on holding the Brink against the Ossar, he hates his brother Bayan and needs him.
sartaq.body:
## Who

Sartaq is forty, grey at the temples, and has fought the [[ossar]] on open grass more often than any
living man. He knows what pushed [[the-hoofborn]] west. He wants the khanate to hold [[the-brink]] and
let the three realms of Crownhold bleed each other. He shares the throne with [[bayan]] because their
mother split it, and because the clans would not follow either alone.

seraphine-vasthorne.name: Seraphine Vasthorne
seraphine-vasthorne.summary: The youngest daughter of Aurelian VII, pious and pale, who goes down to the cellars of the palace every night to kneel; she wants the iron ring her father wears under the gold, and she knows what it is.
seraphine-vasthorne.body:
## Who

Seraphine is nineteen, thin, quiet, and the only one of the king's children who prays. The
court thinks she prays to the gods of the chapel. She prays with her forehead on the cellar
floor, and something answers her.

## What she wants

The iron circlet her father wears under the gold. [[the-kneeling]] have told her it is one of
the rings of [[the-first-knot]], carried south out of [[old-vahr]], and that a ring broken in
the right place loosens the rope. She has not told them she would rather wear it.

## Threads

- Is she one of the [[argentine-houses]] by her mother's side?

sethra.name: Sethra
sethra.summary: The woman who waits in the Brinevaults while others go deeper, and takes what they carried when they do not come back; she holds the vaults by outliving everyone who passes through them.
sethra.body:
## Who

Sethra does not stop anyone in the [[brinevaults]]. She sits among the clerks' shelves with
a lamp turned low and lets you pass. Then she waits. Most of the ones who go down past her do
not come back, and in a season or a year she goes down a little way after them and brings up
what they carried. Everything she owns was carried into Kell by someone braver.

She has never fought for the vaults. Nobody who fought her for them is still alive to say
whether she would have won.

## Voice

Sethra speaks quietly and about afterwards. She is always certain there will be one.

## The hold

The ledger calls whoever holds the most of the Brinevaults the **Keeper of the
Brinevaults**. It has called her that through every one of the people she waited out.

## Threads

- What does she do with the ledgers on the clerks' shelves, and does she read them?

severina-lucentis.name: Severina Lucentis
severina-lucentis.summary: The Exarch of the Sunward See in year 150, of the House of Lucentis; a true believer and a fanatic, who wants to march the sun-banner over the Brink and burn the Ossar lands clean.
severina-lucentis.body:
## Who

Severina is fifty, gaunt, barefoot in the cathedral, and believes every word of the faith. That makes
her the most dangerous Exarch in a century. She has burned more of [[the-kneeling]] than the last
three Exarchs together, and the silver-eyed bishops of the See have begun to be afraid of her.

## What she wants

A crusade: every army of Harth over [[the-brink]] under the sun-banner, to the [[the-black-step]], to
burn the Ossar out with the light of [[helion-castor]]. She has written to all three realms and to the
khans. Only one has answered.

sorgan-windbreaker.name: Sorgan Windbreaker
aliases: He Who Rode Against the Wind
sorgan-windbreaker.summary: The young khan who is gathering the tribes of the Hoofborn again; as a boy he rode against the wind across the Grass Sea and lived, which the riders take as an omen, and the calendars of Harrowmere say he is due.
sorgan-windbreaker.body:
## Who

Sorgan is twenty-four, lean, scarred across both cheeks by the wind, and has never lost a fight.
When he was twelve a storm came west across [[the-grass-sea]] and he rode into it, against it, for
three days, and came out the other side. The tribes call him Windbreaker, and the old women say
the wind that pushes the [[the-hoofborn]] west every generation has met its rider.

## What he wants

The west. Not to raid it this time. To keep it.

## Threads

- What did he see on the far side of the storm?

stenn.name: Stenn
stenn.summary: The sergeant of the Unmourned at the Hookford ford, who hires anyone who wants pay and weeps for none of them.
stenn.body:
## Who

Stenn has buried three companies and kept the sergeant's knife from each. Short words, a short temper, a long memory for who works.

## What she does

She hires swords at the ford for [[nevermourn]] and sends them west into [[the-greywood]] after rats and outlaws.

streng.name: Streng
streng.summary: The quartermaster of the Ninth at Hookford, a hangman who sells writs, hooks and rope to those who hunt.
streng.body:
## Who

Streng was hanged at fifteen like every hangman, and wears the scar high. He keeps the Ninth's store by the bridge.

## What he does

He sells hooks, rope and writs of pardon, and writes down who bought them.

tanna.name: Tanna
tanna.summary: The brine-wife of Drykell, who brews draughts from salt, weed and what the dry harbour leaves.
tanna.body:
## Who

Tanna came up from the old streets when the water went, and stayed on the quaysteps.

## What she does

She brews draughts from salt and weed in [[drykell]], and sells them to pickers going down.

tarn.name: Tarn
tarn.summary: The salt-smith of Drykell, who reworks what comes up out of Kell and asks no one where it was.
tarn.body:
## Who

Tarn learned the trade under [[barr]] and keeps his forge where the salt dries on the quay.

## What he does

He salvages and reforges the iron of drowned [[kell]], and pays in marks for what pickers bring.

the-clerk-of-the-first-ledger.name: The Clerk of the First Ledger
the-clerk-of-the-first-ledger.summary: The clerk who kept the first ledger of Kell in the deepest strongroom, and is keeping it still; the ledger counts what Kell owes, and the clerk is not finished counting.
the-clerk-of-the-first-ledger.body:
## The ledger

Every ledger in the [[brinevaults]] counts lines. The first ledger, in the deepest of the
[[strongrooms]], counts names: everyone who ever owed Kell anything, and what was taken in lieu,
and what is still owed. The rope on [[hangmoot]] that went slack forty-one years ago is being
drawn tight. The first ledger is how the rope knows whom to draw.

## Now

The clerk is at the desk, writing. The pen does not stop for you; it writes you down. Those who
have come back up from the strongrooms say the clerk looked up only once, and said their name,
and that they had not given it.

## Threads

- Is there a line in the first ledger for [[gorvek]], and what does it say he owes?

the-first-up-the-hill.name: The First Up the Hill
the-first-up-the-hill.summary: Whoever led the poor streets of Kell up the hill with knives the night the crown went empty; drowned at the top of the lane, at the first barred door, still knocking.
the-first-up-the-hill.body:
## The night

Somebody went first. The coast has argued for forty years about who, and nobody has a name.
Whoever it was got further than the others: to the top of the lane, to the first house with a
bar, and put a fist to the door, and the sea came in through the windows of the house before
the door gave.

## Now

At the top of the deepest lane of the [[lowstreets]] there is a door that has been knocked on for
forty years. The knocking stops when somebody comes up the lane behind. It turns round, and
calls the street to it, and asks you to open the door.

## Threads

- What did the house behind the door have, that a whole street went up the hill for it?

the-numbered-man.name: The Numbered Man
the-numbered-man.summary: The man who walked south across the Glassands into the Counted Lands and came back, years later, with a number on his wrist and nothing he would say; he never slept indoors again.
the-numbered-man.body:
## The story

He was a digger of [[qarr-dhuun]] who lost his way, and walked south instead of north, for forty
nights, across the glass. He came back eleven years later out of the south, thin, quiet, with a
number tattooed on the inside of his wrist, and walked into [[ush-kaddah]] and drank from the well
for a whole day.

## After

He would not say what was in [[the-counted-lands]]. He would not sleep under a roof. He said, once,
drunk, that the people there were happy, and that this was the worst thing about it.

the-tenth-prince.name: The Tenth Prince
the-tenth-prince.summary: The ruler of the Tenth Palace, which has had a door since the Fraying: a Stonesleeper that woke under Harrowmere, which the Gilded paid for a thousand years to stay asleep; in year 150 it sits openly among the princes, and they pay it more.
the-tenth-prince.body:
## What the Gilded bought

When [[the-gilded]] bought the debts of [[old-vahr]], one of the debts came with a house. Under the
black lake of [[harrowmere]] a [[the-stonesleepers]] lay in a niche older than the city, and the
emperors had been paying it to sleep. The princes kept paying: a chest a year, on the night of
[[the-hiring-of-the-wise]], to [[the-tenth-palace]]. It slept.

## The door

The night of [[the-fraying]] it woke. In the morning the Tenth Palace had a door. A year later the
Tenth Prince sat in the council of the Gilded for the first time: tall, pale, cold, polite, wearing
a mask of silver because the princes asked it to. It has sat there since. It votes. It lends. It
is paid more than ever, and the princes no longer say what for.

## Threads

- What is in the chests now?
- Does it know [[ishara-grey]]?

the-unseen-girl.name: The Unseen Girl
the-unseen-girl.summary: The thief who stole from Sarn, perhaps the only one ever to; a girl of the Harrowmere canals with no name in any story, who took something from Sarn's own hand and was never seen again.
the-unseen-girl.body:
## The story

Every version is different, which is how you know it is about [[sarn]]. In all of them a girl of
the canals of [[harrowmere]], no older than twelve, put her hand into Sarn's own pocket and took
something out, and Sarn did not notice until the next morning. [[the-honest-company-of-takers]]
keep her a seat at their high table, empty.

## What she took

The stories do not agree. A key. A face. The second ruby, before Sarn could hide it. Sarn, asked,
smiles, and does not change the subject, which is worse.

the-voice-under-solmerine.name: The Voice Under Solmerine
the-voice-under-solmerine.summary: What leads the Kneeling in year 150: a voice that speaks from the deepest cellars under Solmerine, where Seraphine broke the ring; every cell in Harth hears its words, nobody has seen it, and the hangmen think it is a Stonesleeper.
the-voice-under-solmerine.body:
## What it is

Under [[solmerine]], below the palace cellars where [[seraphine-vasthorne]] broke her father's ring,
there are older cellars, Vahrish, and below those older ones still. Since [[the-fraying]] something
there speaks. Kneelers who go down hear it. They come up with instructions, and the instructions are
the same in every cell in Harth, in the same words, though no messenger has carried them.

## What the hangmen think

That it is a [[the-stonesleepers]], woken in the stone under the city by the breaking of the ring,
and that the cellar where Seraphine knelt was a door. [[ulf-eightrope]] wants to burn Solmerine down
to the bedrock to find out. [[lucius-vasthorne]] has declined, politely.

the-waking-one.name: The Waking One
the-waking-one.summary: The one of the Stonesleepers that lies nearest the surface in the north, in the stone at the centre of the Underhollow, and has begun to wake.
the-waking-one.body:
## The stone

The [[the-stonesleepers]] went into the stone when the knot was tied. Most of them lie under the
[[glassands]] and the [[feverfen]], far down. One did not go far. It lies in the black stone at the
heart of the [[the-underhollow]], at the lip of the crack, where its servants built their ring of
columns so they could kneel by it.

## Now

The [[the-blindkin]] of the temple are sweeping faster. The stone at the lip of the crack is
warm, and it has a shape in it that it did not have when [[mardra]] first went down. She says it
has opened its hand.

## Threads

- When it is awake, what will it ask for first?

tiberian-vasthorne.name: Tiberian Vasthorne
tiberian-vasthorne.summary: The eldest living son of Aurelian VII, beautiful, beloved by the crowds of Crownhold and empty inside; his councillors have sold the kingdom to Harrowmere in his name, and he believes every word they tell him.
tiberian-vasthorne.body:
## Who

Tiberian is thirty, golden-haired, tall, and good at everything that is done in front of a
crowd: riding, speaking, weeping at funerals. He has never read a document he signed. His
councillors read them for him, and his councillors are paid by the House of Salt.

## Voice

Warm, sincere, and a little too loud. He means it. That is the worst of it.

## Threads

- Does he know, somewhere under the gilt, what he has signed?

tolm.name: Tolm
tolm.summary: The Greycloak captain who sits in the door of the Wallgate toll-house; has taken forty villages without drawing a blade, and is sorry about every one of them.
tolm.body:
## Who

Tolm is the Greycloak the stories mean when they say a captain rides in alone and sits down.
He is fifty, thin, grey before the cloak was, and polite in the way of a man who has never
once been refused. He does not carry a hook. He says he is no good with it, which is true,
and that he does not need one, which is also true. He keeps the toll-house at [[wallgate]]
and has kept it since the grey.

## Voice

Tolm apologises. He apologises for the tithe, the weather, the price on [[gorvek]]'s head
and the fact that it will be raised again in winter. Every apology is sincere and none of
them changes anything. Ask him a question and he will thank you for it.

## In the world

- He has taken forty villages through the open gate. He remembers every one by the name of
  the person who let him in.
- He has met Gorvek once, across the toll-house table, and let him go. The [[greycloaks]]
  have not asked why. He is waiting for them to.
- He does not go near [[greyhollow]], and is the only Greycloak who will say so.
- Since [[the-ebb]] the order has sent him south for the first time. He apologised to the
  toll-house.

## Threads

- What did Tolm let through the Wallgate that he should not have?

torr-halaq.name: Torr-Halaq
aliases: He Who Took the Name Back
torr-halaq.summary: The patriarch of the greatest tribe of the Hadd, who took his name back from the old list of Old Vahr; he knows why the Hadd never walk within sight of the burnt capital, and will tell it only to someone who has walked one night on the white glass and lived.
torr-halaq.body:
## Who

Torr-Halaq is old, upright, veiled to the eyes in black, and leads four thousand tents across the
[[glassands]]. His name was on the old list of the emperors' household, carved on a gate of
[[old-vahr]]; his ancestor was a slave there. He took it back.

## What he knows

Why the [[the-hadd]] never go near Old Vahr. The Hadd were the emperors' slaves on the last night.
They were standing on the glass of [[ahl-sereth]] when the asking was made, and they saw what was
given. They walked away, at night, and have walked only at night since.

## Threads

- What did the Hadd see given?

ulf-eightrope.name: Ulf Eightrope
ulf-eightrope.summary: The Reeve of Hangmoot in year 150, who took the name of the ropes that are left and has sworn on the rope that there will not be seven.
ulf-eightrope.body:
## Who

Ulf is huge, slow, sixty, and was hanged at fifteen like every hangman. When he became Reeve he took
the name *Eightrope* in front of the moot, and swore a [[rope-oaths]] that he would not be the Reeve
who counted seven. The scar at his throat is the oath's.

## What he does

He holds [[hangmoot]] with eight ropes and an empty ninth gallows. He sends hangmen to [[the-brink]],
to [[solmerine]] after [[the-kneeling]], and to every holdfast in the Mark that has forgotten its
debts. He has begun, like [[haldis-graymane]] before him, to watch the [[greycloaks]].

vell.name: Vell
vell.summary: The barefoot river-priest of Hookford who named the Ebb before anyone had seen the water move, and who answers every question with a name.
vell.body:
## Who

Vell was born under the bridge at [[hookford]] and has not worn a shoe since. He is young
for a river-priest, wet to the knee like the rest, and unwelcome at every table in town
except the ones with a death in the family. He walks the two rivers from the ford to the
coast and back each season, and he keeps the names.

## The naming

When the water first went out from Old [[kell]], the coast folk sent to the [[river-priests]]
for a name. Vell had already given it. He had stood on the bridge at Hookford a month before
and said the word *Ebb* to the river, and the river had gone down a finger under his feet.
He says this is not prophecy. He says a name is a grip, and he took hold of something before
it had finished happening.

## Voice

Names, never reasons. Ask Vell why the sea is going out and he will say [[vorr]]. Ask him
what to do and he will say [[thurn]]. Ask him what [[sarn]] wants and he will look at you a
long time and say your own name.

## In the world

- He named [[the-ebb]], and the river-priests are not sure he had the right.
- He has met [[gorvek]] and named him to his face, with a name Gorvek has not repeated. Gorvek did not
  thank him.
- He named the child at [[wrackhead]] [[brim]], and would not say why.

## Threads

- What name did Vell give the ninth gallows at [[hangmoot]], and why did the Reeve pay him
  for it?

vurn.name: Vurn
vurn.summary: The other one who walked out of the Ashfall beside Gorvek; the one who talks, and who tells the sagas of the Reach in the alehouse at Hookford while Gorvek says nothing.
vurn.body:
## Who

Two walked out of the grey into the same village on the same morning. One was [[gorvek]].
The other was Vurn, who was thinner, louder, and had kept count of the days. The elders of
[[bonereach]] asked them both what they wanted. Gorvek's answer became a creed. Vurn's
answer was *ale*, and the Reach has liked him for it since.

## The telling

Vurn tells the sagas. He tells them at [[hookford]] for drink, on the ridge at
[[hangmoot]] for free, and in Bonereach to children who have heard them before. They are
the sagas of the Reach: what a warrior wants, what a warrior does, and what he says when
the work is done. Half of them are Gorvek's deeds and the other half are Vurn's, and Vurn
has been honest about which is which exactly once, and was drunk.

## Voice

Vurn speaks in the cadence of the sagas because he made it. Loud, physical, present tense,
with a boast at the end where Gorvek would have put nothing. He swears by the Ashfall, like
Gorvek, and also by ale, mead, the Reach, and anything else within reach.

## In the world

- He reads. He reads the ledger [[linelord]] aloud to Gorvek, who says he does not need it
  and listens to every line.
- He has met [[sarn]] once, and told the story forty times, and it is different every time,
  and the eyes are always yellow.

## Threads

- What did Vurn count in the grey, and why did he stop at the number he stopped at?

ahl-sereth.name: Ahl-Sereth
ahl-sereth.summary: The innermost glass around Old Vahr, white and faintly glowing at night, where the emperors stood when they made their last asking; the Hadd never walk it, and something else does.
ahl-sereth.body:
## The glass

For a day's walk in every direction from [[old-vahr]], the glass is white. Not green, not black:
white, smooth as ice, and at night it gives off a light like the moon through cloud, so that
the dark never quite comes. The [[the-hadd]] call it the place where night does not come, and
will not walk on it for any price.

## What walks it

Tracks cross the white glass that are not Qaddir, not horse, not man. Caravans that cut a corner
of it lose people in the night without a sound. [[qeth-ummar]]'s Paid walk it to and from his
palace and come to no harm, which tells you something.

## Threads

- What did the emperors ask for, standing here, and is it still being given?

bleakshore.name: Bleakshore
bleakshore.summary: Bleakshore: a huddle of fishers' huts on the bare coast east of Wrackhead, the poorest on the shore, which pays Vorr first and the Greycloaks second.
bleakshore.body:
## The place

Bleakshore is a huddle of fishers' huts on the bare coast east of Wrackhead, the poorest on the shore, which pays Vorr first and the Greycloaks second. Its people fish, pay the salt-pile at [[wrackhead]] for [[vorr]], pay the
[[greycloaks]] their tenth, and trust neither.

bonded-stores.name: The Bonded Stores
bonded-stores.summary: The quay-master's storerooms on the Quaysteps, sealed with goods still in them and silted shut; nobody came to collect.
bonded-stores.body:
## The stores

Kell's quay-master kept what came off the ships under seal until the duty was
paid. The night the city went down, nobody paid it. The stores were shut with
the goods in them, and the packing closed them the rest of the way. The seals
on the doors are still whole. What is behind them is still owed.

## Threads

- Whose goods were they, and is anyone on the coast still owed them?

bonereach.name: Bonereach
bonereach.summary: The northern reach of Gallowmark, a country of scree, bone-white birch and villages that count their dead in winters; where the Ashfall fell hardest and Gorvek was born.
bonereach.body:
## The reach

Bonereach is the part of [[gallowmark]] nobody wanted and somebody kept. Scree slopes, birch
so pale it looks skinned, and villages built into the lee of rocks because the wind comes
off the Wallmountains with an opinion. The people of the Reach are the people of the Mark
boiled down: fewer words, harder hands, a longer memory.

## Since the Ashfall

The ash of [[the-ashfall]] fell here first, hot enough to burn thatch, and cleared here last.
The Reach lost half its villages and does not say which half. Those who walked out of the
grey, [[gorvek]] among them, are called the Ashborn behind their backs and never to their faces.

## Custom

The elders of the Reach do not ask a returning warrior where he has been. They ask what he
wants. The answer is the man.

brandfell.name: Brandfell
brandfell.summary: The mountain of the Wallmountains north of the Wallgate that split open and burned, and whose ash came down over the north of the Mark for a generation; the Reach does not say its name after dark.
brandfell.body:
## The mountain

Brandfell stands in the Wallmountains a day north of the [[wallgate]], and before the
Ashfall it was only the tallest of them. Then it split from the crown to the knees, and the
fire inside came out, and the sky over [[bonereach]] went black and stayed that way for a
generation. That was [[the-ashfall]].

## Now

It still smokes. The snow does not lie on its south face. The Reach sends nobody up it and
asks nobody who has come down from it where they have been.

## Threads

- What is north of Brandfell, that came down through the Wallgate after the ash cleared?

bricked-rooms.name: The Bricked Rooms
bricked-rooms.summary: Rooms in the Lowstreets that their people walled up from the inside the night the crown went empty, with what they meant to keep, and sometimes themselves.
bricked-rooms.body:
## The rooms

When the crown went empty and the knives came up the hill, the Lowstreets did
what streets do: they hid what they had. Families bricked up a back room with the silver in it and
lived in the front. Some bricked themselves in with it. The water came, and the
packing filled every crack, and the rooms are still shut from the inside.

## Threads

- Did any of them come out, and where did they go?

brinevaults.name: The Brinevaults
brinevaults.summary: The salt-cut cellars and counting-rooms under the iron hall, where Kell's clerks copied the ledger, and shut themselves in with the coin when the water came, and counted the days.
brinevaults.body:
## The vaults

Kell kept its salt, its coin and its records under the hall. In the long counting-rooms the
clerks copied the ledger [[linelord]] by lamplight. The copies are still on the shelves. The
last of them count days, not lines. When the sea came in the clerks barred the vault doors
with the coin inside and themselves with it, and the doors held, and the air held for a while.
A stroke for every day, in a hand that gets worse, until it stops.

## The ropes

Ropes hang down the cistern shafts, drawn taut toward the hall, and [[the-drawn]] move along
them. In the deepest cistern the water has dripped for forty years and left a column of salt as
thick as a man, and the clerks' coin is under it.

## Threads

- Who counted the last days, down here, and who were they waiting for?

crownhold.name: Crownhold
crownhold.summary: The largest kingdom of Harth, south of Gallowmark, whose kings claim the throne of Vahr; gilt on the outside, poison and debt inside, and its taxes collected by the Greycloaks.
crownhold.body:
## The kingdom

Crownhold holds the best land in Harth: wheat, vine, the old imperial road and the
river cities along it. Its capital, the city of the same name, is built on the ruins of a
Vahrish provincial seat, and its kings sit on a throne they say was carried out of
[[old-vahr]] the night it burned. It was not. Everyone at court knows it was not.

## The land

The capital is [[solmerine]]. The provinces are [[granaria]], [[vinalis]], [[marcheast]] and
[[saltcoast]]. The great houses are [[house-aldemar]], [[house-corvaith]], [[house-lucentis]],
[[house-trevane]] and [[house-sabinus]], with the Mournevales of the Exarch close behind. The
knights are [[the-iron-hundred]].

## The court

The court of Crownhold runs on three things: offices for sale, poison in the wine, and
debts to [[harrowmere]]. The Gilt King [[aurelian-vasthorne]] has outlived four heirs and two queens. The
lords of the provinces raise armies against each other in his name. The [[greycloaks]] farm
the kingdom's taxes for a tenth of them, and the king is grateful, and has never asked what
else they take.

## The church

The state church is [[the-sunward-faith]] of [[helion-castor]], the sun against the dark below:
gold domes, incense, offices for sale, and an Exarch at the king's right hand.

## The cult

In the cellars of the capital the [[the-kneeling]] meet in rooms the city watch is paid not
to find. Some of the people who meet there wear court silk.

## The crises

- [[the-three-crowns]]: three heirs, [[tiberian-vasthorne]], [[seraphine-vasthorne]] and
  [[marcus-halberd]], and one old king.
- [[the-burning-of-the-rolls]]: the hungry provinces under [[quintus-ashhand]].
- [[the-unpaid-war]]: the sword taken to Harrowmere's ledger.

## Threads

- How much of Crownhold does the order already own?
- Which of the king's councillors kneels?

driftholds.name: Driftholds
driftholds.summary: The floating villages of the fen-folk, built on islands of woven reed that drift with the water, so that no one, and nothing, can find them twice in the same place.
driftholds.body:
## The villages

A drifthold is a raft of reed as big as a field, a dozen huts on it, gardens in baskets, and
the whole thing moving a little every day with the current. When the fen-folk want to go
somewhere else, they pole it. When something finds them, they cut the ropes and scatter.

## Why

The fen-folk say a place that stays still gets known, and a place that gets known gets visited,
and the [[ossar]] visit. No drifthold has ever been built within sight of [[the-black-step]].

drownhaven.name: Drownhaven
drownhaven.summary: Drownhaven: the largest fishing town of the Gallowmark coast, west of Wrackhead, where every family has lost someone to the sea and says so in the name.
drownhaven.body:
## The place

Drownhaven is the largest fishing town of the Gallowmark coast, west of Wrackhead, where every family has lost someone to the sea and says so in the name. Its people fish, pay the salt-pile at [[wrackhead]] for [[vorr]], pay the
[[greycloaks]] their tenth, and trust neither.

drykell.name: Drykell
drykell.summary: The lawless plunder town that has grown up in the dry ruins of Kell by year 150; built of wreck-wood and ash-brick on the old quays, ruled by whoever holds the most ground in the ledger, and still digging.
drykell.body:
## The town

When the coast was lifted far enough, Kell came out of the sea for good: quays, streets, vaults
and the iron roof, dry and white with salt. The people who had been going down at low water stopped
leaving. Drykell is what they built: shanties on the [[quaysteps]], taverns in the
[[lowstreets]], gambling dens in the [[brinevaults]].

## The law

There is none, except the ledger. Whoever holds the most ground in [[linelord]] calls themselves
the Linelord, and takes a tithe of every pick. The title changes hands every few years, usually with
a knife. The [[greycloaks]] hold the road out, and take theirs.

## Still digging

Kell had a great many rooms, and the packing still fills most of them. Every week somebody breaks
into one nobody has opened, and every month somebody does not come back from one. Some of the
pickers pay a small tithe at the Iron Hall, to the king who is still sitting in his chair, and
nobody says to whom it goes.

ebbmouth.name: Ebbmouth
ebbmouth.summary: Ebbmouth: the fishing village at the mouth of the third river, whose harbour has gone dry since the Ebb, and whose boats now lie on mud a mile from the water.
ebbmouth.body:
## The place

Ebbmouth is the fishing village at the mouth of the third river, whose harbour has gone dry since the Ebb, and whose boats now lie on mud a mile from the water. Its people fish, pay the salt-pile at [[wrackhead]] for [[vorr]], pay the
[[greycloaks]] their tenth, and trust neither.

emberstead.name: Emberstead
emberstead.summary: The town of smiths on the south face of Brandfell, where snow does not lie; they forge with the mountain's own heat and every forge has a hole in its back wall for the Old Smith to look out.
emberstead.body:
## The town

Since [[brandfell]] split, its south face has been warm. Vents in the rock breathe hot air,
and the snow melts before it lands. The smiths of the north came up to it and built Emberstead
in the vents: stone forges set over cracks in the mountain, fed by the fire under it, no
charcoal needed.

## The work

The best iron in Harth comes out of Emberstead, black, heavy, and slightly warm for a day after
it is quenched. The smiths worship [[the-old-smith-under-the-snow]] and burn something for
him every winter. Some winters it is a smith.

## Threads

- What are the smiths hearing in the vents at night, that has made three of them walk into
  the mountain?

feverfen.name: The Feverfen
feverfen.summary: The swamp-jungle of the south-east coast, hot, green and rotten, where the black temples of the Ossar stand in the water and the fen-folk say the Ossar never left, only the daylight.
feverfen.body:
## The fen

Where the rivers of the east come to the sea they give up and spread out into a hundred
miles of mangrove, reed and black water under a canopy that does not let the sun down.
Fever lives here, and leeches as long as a forearm, and things the fen-folk do not name.

## The temples

The [[ossar]] built in black stone, and here the stone still stands, stepped temples rising
out of the water with the jungle grown over them. The fen-folk fish around them and do not
go inside. The ones who do go in come out pale, if they come out.

## The fen-folk

Small, quiet, tattooed people who pole flat boats through the channels and trade with the
reavers of [[the-teeth]]. They worship nothing. They say worship is what the Ossar wanted.

## Places and powers

- [[the-black-step]], the greatest temple.
- [[driftholds]], the floating villages.
- [[the-leech-mothers]], the fever-healers.
- [[rotwater]], the smugglers' port.

## Threads

- What do the fen-folk leave on the temple steps every new moon, and who takes it?

fordham.name: Fordham
fordham.summary: The market town on the third grey river, where the horse and cattle fairs of the Mark are held, the Holdfast Lords hire their swords, and every feud in the west is settled or started.
fordham.body:
## The town

[[hookford]] has the bridge and the hooks. Fordham has the horses. On the third of the grey
rivers, where it runs shallow over gravel, the fairs of the west Mark have been held since the
ash cleared: horses, cattle, iron from [[irondeep]], grey wood from [[the-greywood]], and swords
for hire.

## The fair

At the spring fair the [[the-holdfast-lords]] hire their seasons of Ashborn, and the Ashborn
look them over the way they look over the horses. More feuds start at Fordham than anywhere in
the Mark, and more end there.

gallowmark.name: Gallowmark
gallowmark.summary: The land itself; a march of gallows, grey rivers and stubborn people between the mountains and the drowned coast, where the Ashfall fell and the ground has not been still since.
gallowmark.body:
## The land

Gallowmark is named for what its first rulers built before they built anything else. The
gallows are still there on the ridges, most of them empty, none of them taken down. The land
runs from the Wallmountains in the north to the drowned coast in the south, cut through by
grey rivers that the priests of [[thurn]] say are one river pretending to be many. The
gallows belong to [[hask]]; the sea at the end of the rivers belongs to [[vorr]]. Nobody
prays to any of the three. They keep out of the way.

Nothing here is fertile by accident. The people are hard because the soil is, and they trust
what they can hold. A stranger who can make a thing obey will be respected; a stranger who
explains why will be watched.

## Regions

- [[bonereach]] in the north, where [[gorvek]] comes from.
- [[kell]] on the coast, the drowned city that still counts as a place because the survivors
  refuse to stop saying its name.
- [[brandfell]] beyond it, the mountain that split and burned.
- [[wallgate]] in the far north, the one pass through the Wallmountains and the one gate
  nobody can close.
- [[hookford]] in the middle Mark, where two rivers meet and the only market is.
- [[hangmoot]] above it, the ridge of nine gallows where the Mark pays its debts.
- [[greyhollow]] in the eastern hills, where the ash never cooled.
- [[wrackhead]] on the coast, the headland over Old Kell.

## More of the Mark

- [[the-greywood]], the forest that died standing, in the west.
- [[grimwatch]], the border keep on the imperial road south.
- [[irondeep]], the mining town in the foothills.
- [[fordham]], the horse fair on the third river.
- [[drownhaven]], [[bleakshore]] and [[ebbmouth]], the fishing towns of the coast.
- [[the-holdfast-lords]] in their towers, and [[the-ninth-rope]] at Hangmoot.

## Since the Ashfall

The ash of [[the-ashfall]] came down out of [[brandfell]] over the north and stayed a generation. The Mark has been
darker since, and its stories shorter.

## Since the Ebb

In the first winter after the ash cleared the sea began to go out from Old Kell. [[the-ebb]]
is pulling every road in the Mark toward the coast, and the Mark is going.

glassands.name: The Glassands
glassands.summary: The desert where the heartland of Vahr burned in one night; sand fused to glass for a hundred miles, ruin-cities half buried in it, caravan roads between them, and sorcerer-kings in the old towers.
glassands.body:
## The desert

South of Crownhold the land goes yellow, then white, then hard. For a hundred miles around
[[old-vahr]] the sand is glass, green and black and cracked, and a man who walks on it in
the noon sun goes blind. The caravans cross at night, between the old cities, carrying salt,
glass, and what the diggers bring out of the ruins.

## The ruins

Vahr's cities are still out there, half drowned in sand: towers, aqueducts, streets of
statues with their faces melted. Under them are older foundations, black and too large, that
were the [[ossar]]'s. Diggers go down for gold and come up with bones too long for any grave.

## The kings of the glass

In the old towers sit sorcerer-kings who rule a well, a ruin and a few hundred desperate
people each, and who make pacts with [[the-unborn]] the way other kings raise taxes. The
greatest of them is [[qeth-ummar]], in Old Vahr itself.

## Places and powers

- [[ush-kaddah]], the city of the bottomless well.
- [[the-well-kings]], the sorcerer-kings of the towers.
- [[qarr-dhuun]], the diggers' guild.
- [[ahl-sereth]], the white glass where night does not come.

## Threads

- What is under the glass, in the place where the fire was whitest?

granaria.name: Granaria
granaria.summary: Granaria: the grain province in the heartland, flat, rich and starving under the tithe, where the Burning of the Rolls began.
granaria.body:
## The province

Granaria is the grain province in the heartland, flat, rich and starving under the tithe, where the Burning of the Rolls began.

greyhollow.name: Greyhollow
greyhollow.summary: A hollow in the eastern hills where the ash lies deep and has never cooled; smoke stands in it like milk in a bowl, and what walks out is never quite what walked in.
greyhollow.body:
## The hollow

East of the middle Mark the hills fold, and in one fold the ash of [[the-ashfall]] lay
three men deep and never cooled. The ground under it is hot. Smoke comes up through it and
stands in the hollow like milk in a bowl, and does not move with the wind. The birch at the edge are white on the outside and black on the
inside. Nobody farms within a mile of it.

## Going in

People go in. Some for what they lost in the grey, some for what [[mardra]] sells, some because
the [[greycloaks]] do not go in and that is worth a great deal. Those who come out come out
changed in a way nobody can name, and the [[river-priests]] have refused to try. [[gorvek]]
has never said whether he has been back.

## Around it

- [[the-underhollow]], the Ossar temple at the bottom, around the crack.
- [[rimcroft]] and the [[the-ashen]], under [[harl-greyhand]].
- [[smokewalkers]], who went in and came out.
- [[lowfold]], the quiet farm.

## What it is
