The Ashborn say the Hollow is the last of the Ashfall. Mardra says it is the nearest the fire
under the Mark comes to the top, and that the Hollow is not cooling. It is warming.

## Threads

- Why is the Hollow warmer every winter since the sea began to go out?

grimwatch.name: Grimwatch
grimwatch.summary: The stone fortress on the southern border of Gallowmark where the old imperial road crosses into Crownhold; held by the Greycloaks for a king who has forgotten it, and the first place the Three Crowns will fight over.
grimwatch.body:
## The keep

Grimwatch is Vahrish, older than anything else in the Mark, a square of black stone where the
imperial road comes down out of the hills into Gallowmark. [[crownhold]] built it as a border
keep. The [[greycloaks]] were hired to garrison it two hundred years ago and never left.

## Now

Whichever of [[the-three-crowns]] holds Grimwatch holds the road north. All three know it.
The captain of the keep has received three letters this winter and answered all three, politely.

hangmoot.name: Hangmoot
hangmoot.summary: The ridge of nine gallows above the middle Mark where the land's first rulers hanged their god, and where once a year at the Rope-Moot every debt in Gallowmark is paid, forgiven or hanged.
hangmoot.body:
## The ridge

Nine gallows on a bare ridge, older than [[kell]], taller than anything else the first rulers
built. Eight of them are used. The ninth has never held anyone that anyone will name, and it
is the one the wind plays. This is where [[hask]] hangs, if he hangs anywhere.

## The Rope-Moot

Once a year, when the rivers are lowest, the Mark comes up the ridge. Debts are read out by
the Reeve. What can be paid is paid. What cannot is hanged or forgiven, and the Mark has
always found the first cheaper. The [[greycloaks]] attend, politely, and read the longest
list.

## The slack rope

The hangmen say one of the nine ropes has hung slack since [[the-drowning-of-kell]], and
that a slack rope is a debt nobody has collected. Since [[the-ebb]] the Reeve has had the
ninth gallows re-roped, and the Mark noticed.

## Threads

- Whose name is on the ninth gallows?
- Who was the Reeve before [[haldis-graymane]]?

harrowmere.name: Harrowmere
harrowmere.summary: The canal-city of merchant princes on a black lake east of Crownhold, the richest place in Harth; everything is for sale in it, including sorcery, people and the empire's old debts.
harrowmere.body:
## The city

Harrowmere is built on piles driven into a black lake, a thousand palaces and ten thousand
hovels joined by canals. It has no king. It has [[the-gilded]], the merchant princes, who
bought the debts of [[old-vahr]] the year after it burned and have been collecting on them
since. Every kingdom in Harth owes Harrowmere. Harrowmere owes nobody, and says so.

## What is for sale

Grain, iron, ships, slaves, poisons, offices in [[crownhold]], the names of the dead,
sorcerers by the season, and once, they say, a god's tooth. The slave market on the
Stairs of Weighing is the largest in the world. The [[greycloaks]] keep a chapterhouse on
the Grand Canal and pay no harbour tax.

## Under the water

The black lake has no bottom anyone has found. The princes sink their debtors in it. Things
come up sometimes that were not sunk.

## Places and powers

- [[the-tenth-palace]], with no doors.
- [[stillwater]], the debtors' prison on the lake.
- [[the-honest-company-of-takers]], the thieves' guild.
- [[the-hiring-of-the-wise]], the yearly auction of sorcerers.

## Threads

- Who is the Tenth Prince?

harth.name: Harth
harth.summary: The continent Gallowmark is the northern edge of; what was the empire of Vahr, broken a thousand years ago into rotten kingdoms, ruin-deserts, fens, ice and borderlands, and held together by nothing.
harth.body:
## The land

Ice in the north, glass in the south, rot in the east, and in between a thousand years of
kingdoms that are each sure they are what is left of [[old-vahr]]. Nobody calls it one
place except the people who are not from it. Harth is what the empire looked like
after [[the-fall-of-vahr]]: a plate dropped on a stone floor.

## From north to south

- [[rimewold]], beyond the Wallmountains: ice, clans and the smoke of [[brandfell]].
- [[gallowmark]], the borderland under the mountains, where the world is tied shut at
  [[hangmoot]].
- [[crownhold]], the gilt kingdom that claims Vahr's throne and is eaten from the inside.
- [[harrowmere]], the canal-city of merchant princes, the richest and rottenest place in the
  Sunder.
- [[feverfen]], the swamp-jungle of the south-east coast, over the Ossar's drowned temples.
- [[the-teeth]], the reaver islands off the fen coast.
- [[glassands]], the desert of fused sand where Vahr's heartland burned.

## What holds it together

Nothing. The roads are Vahr's and nobody mends them. The coin is Harrowmere's and nobody
trusts it. The [[greycloaks]] are in every kingdom and rule none of them. Under all of it,
the [[the-unborn]] are bound, and the binding is a rope in the north that one thief has
already loosened.

## Threads

- What is past the Glassands, to the south, where the caravans do not go?

hookford.name: Hookford
hookford.summary: The one town in the middle Mark, where two of the grey rivers meet at a ford and the Greycloaks hang their tithe-books from hooks on the bridge; market, tithe-house, and the last warm bed before anywhere.
hookford.body:
## The town

Two of the three grey rivers meet at Hookford. The ford was there before the town, and the
bridge before the [[greycloaks]]. It is the only place in the middle Mark with a market, a
smith who takes coin, and a hall where a stranger can sleep with a door between him and the
wind. The people of the Mark distrust it accordingly.

## The hooks

The Greycloaks hung their hooks on the bridge the year they came, one per span, and hang the
tithe-books from them. Nobody has ever been hanged from the bridge. Everybody knows that they
could be, and pays.

## The road

Every road in the Mark passes through Hookford: down from [[wallgate]] and [[bonereach]], up
from [[wrackhead]] and the coast, east to the rim of [[greyhollow]], and the ridge road to
[[hangmoot]]. If [[the-ebb]] pulls the Mark to the coast, it will pull it through here.

## Threads

- Who owned the bridge before the hooks?

irondeep.name: Irondeep
irondeep.summary: The mining town in the foothills of the Wallmountains, built over the deepest iron pits in the Mark; the shafts have grown warm since Brandfell split, and the miners have started hearing things.
irondeep.body:
## The town

Black houses on a black hillside, slag-heaps, and the mouths of the pits. Irondeep has dug iron
for the Mark since before [[kell]] had a quay. The miners are Ashborn, debtors and convicts, and
the [[greycloaks]] take a tenth of the ore at the pithead.

## Since Brandfell

The deep shafts have grown warm. The lowest galleries are too hot to work in summer. The miners
say they hear knocking below the deepest level, regular, like a hammer. The smiths of
[[emberstead]] say they know exactly what that is.

## Threads

- Who is knocking?

kell.name: Kell
kell.summary: The old royal city on the drowned coast, seat of the Iron Crown, which came apart the night Sarn took the rubies and has been sinking ever since.
kell.body:
## The city

Kell was the only city in [[gallowmark]] that deserved the word. Stone quays, a hall with a
roof of iron plates, and a king with a crown that held the three rivers in place: that is
how the river-priests tell it, and they tell it with their hands over their mouths.

The last king kept the ledger [[linelord]] in the iron-roofed hall and read it the winter
before the night, looking for a wall that would hold. Brother [[ruun]] was a boy on the quay.

## The night

Then [[sarn]] came, and the [[iron-crown-of-kell]] lost its three rubies in one night, and by
morning the quays were under water and the king was under the quays. Whether the crown held
the sea back or only the people's belief that it did, the result is the same: Kell is a place
you sail over.

## Now

Old Kell is a name the coast people still use for the water where the city was. The
[[greycloaks]] say they will raise it. They have said so for forty years.

## The packing

Forty years of water have packed the ash into Kell's walls. Where a doorway was
bricked up, a wall cracked, or a room shut in a hurry, the gaps are full of it:
grey, hard as clay and softer than stone. The divers call it the packing. A
pick goes through it where a pick would never go through stone, and behind it
are the rooms Kell shut and nobody opened: the [[bonded-stores]] on the
[[quaysteps]], the [[bricked-rooms]] of the [[lowstreets]], the
[[strongrooms]] of the [[brinevaults]], and in [[the-iron-hall]], the
[[kings-way]].

kings-way.name: The King's Way
kings-way.summary: A stair from the Iron Hall that the last king of Kell had built for himself and walled up behind him; nobody was meant to know about it, and it goes up.
kings-way.body:
## The stair

The last king of Kell did not trust the doors of his own hall. He had a stair
cut through the wall behind the throne, up toward the iron roof, and had it
bricked over so it looked like wall. He never used it. The night came on him in
his chair. The packing has filled the brickwork, and the stair is still there,
going up.

## Threads

- Did Corve know about it, sitting in front of it for forty years?

lowfold.name: Lowfold
lowfold.summary: A farm on the low side of Greyhollow's rim, the nearest house to the warm ground, where a cell of the Kneeling lives as farmers; no dog barks there, and its people kneel in the furrows at night.
lowfold.body:
## The farm

A long-house, barns, fields of grey barley, and the warmest soil in the Mark, because it is the
nearest to the fire. To a traveller it is a good farm, quiet, prosperous, hospitable. There are no
dogs. There are no young children. At night the family goes out into the furrows and kneels with
their foreheads on the warm earth.

## What they do

They listen. They send their own into the smoke to become [[smokewalkers]], and the hungry ones
they keep. They buy [[knotrats]] by the cage. And they are digging, slowly, under the barn, toward
[[the-underhollow]].

lowstreets.name: The Lowstreets
lowstreets.summary: The streets of drowned Kell, where every house is barred from the inside, and not against the water.
lowstreets.body:
## The streets

Below [[quaysteps]] the city is still a city, and every door in it is barred from the
inside. The coast says Kell went home that night and waited for the crown to hold. The
scratches on the doors are on the outside, low, and they are not from water.

When the crown went empty, Kell came apart before the water came in. The streets that
had nothing went up the hill to the streets that had something, with knives. Every house
that had a bar used it.

## The houses

The people inside held the doors against their neighbours, and the sea came in through the
windows instead, and they drowned with their shoulders to the wood. Some of them did not stay
drowned. Nobody has asked them what they ate.

## Threads

- Who led the streets up the hill that night, and did they get what they came for?

marcheast.name: Marcheast
marcheast.summary: Marcheast: the eastern march toward the Grass Sea, a land of burnt towns and watchtowers that remembers the Hoofborn.
marcheast.body:
## The province

Marcheast is the eastern march toward the Grass Sea, a land of burnt towns and watchtowers that remembers the Hoofborn.

old-vahr.name: Old Vahr
old-vahr.summary: The capital of the fallen empire, in the white heart of the Glassands; a city of melted towers and black Ossar foundations, where the sorcerer Qeth-Ummar sits on the glass throne and claims to be the last emperor.
old-vahr.body:
## The city

The fire that ended the empire was whitest here. The towers of Old Vahr stand bent like
candles in a hot room, their stone run into glass. The palace still stands, because it was
built on [[ossar]] foundations, and those did not melt.

## The throne

On the glass throne sits [[qeth-ummar]], who says he is the last emperor and was there on the
night. Nobody can prove he was not. The caravans pay him in water to cross his glass.

## Threads

- Is there a door in the Ossar foundations, under the throne?

ossery.name: Ossery
ossery.summary: The city in the east of Crownhold that the Kneeling took in the Broken Years and the hangmen and kings burned to the ground; nothing is built on the ash, and nothing grows there.
ossery.body:
## The city

Ossery was a river city of the old empire, rich, learned and named, the scholars said, after the
[[ossar]] who first built there. It was the first city [[the-kneeling]] took whole. It is ash now.
Nothing grows on it four hundred years on, and the Crownhold road goes round.

## Threads

- What did the Kneeling of Ossery raise, that it took a city's burning to put it down?

quaysteps.name: The Quaysteps
quaysteps.summary: The stone quays and water-stairs of drowned Kell, the first ground the Ebb gave back; the silt on them is grey, and the bones in it wear the order's cloak.
quaysteps.body:
## The steps

[[kell]] met the sea in stairs, and since [[the-ebb]] the top of them shows at low water
below [[wrackhead]]. The pickers go down them for what the sea has let go of. They come up
with iron and bollard-rings, and with grey on their boots that does not wash off, because it is ash.

## The silt

The silt on the steps is not sand. It is ash, thirty years of it, that the grey rivers carried
down out of the north and laid on the sea floor. Lamps burn grey down here, in the dust. In it lie bones in cloaks the colour of the silt, the order's first men, from
the years when the [[greycloaks]] guarded these quays from salvagers, and kept guarding them
when the ash came down the rivers and nobody came to relieve them. Some
of them are still guarding.

## Threads

- Why are the steps warm, under the silt, where the sea has only just let go of them?

realm-of-solmerine.name: The Realm of Solmerine
realm-of-solmerine.summary: The successor kingdom of Crownhold founded by Tiberian the Fair in the capital, rich, beautiful, and owned by Harrowmere; in the year 150 its kings still sign whatever the House of Salt puts in front of them.
realm-of-solmerine.body:
## The realm

When [[the-three-crowns]] were crowned, the capital crowned [[tiberian-vasthorne]], and he kept it:
[[solmerine]], the Saltcoast, Vinalis and the river cities. His line holds them still, a dynasty of
golden kings with beautiful manners and Harrowmere councillors.

## In the year 150

The richest of the three realms and the weakest. Its armies are bought. Its debts are held by
[[aleid-van-der-haalst]]'s descendants. It wants the other two crowns back, and Harrowmere lends it
the money to try, every generation, at interest.

rimcroft.name: Rimcroft
rimcroft.summary: The largest village of the Ashen, on the rim of Greyhollow, low grey houses roofed with turf and ash, where the Ashen have lived through the Ashfall and since under Old Harl Greyhand.
rimcroft.body:
## The village

Forty houses built low against the wind off the hollow, walls of stone, roofs of turf laid over
ash. The smoke of [[greyhollow]] stands a long stone's throw from the last house. The Ashen keep
goats, grow a grey barley nobody else can grow, and trade with [[mardra]], whose house is a mile
round the rim.

## Custom

Visitors are given water at the gate, never bread, until the elders have looked at them. The
dead are laid in the smoke's edge and not brought back. Every winter outlasted is a new line of
ash in the skin.

rimewold.name: The Rimewold
rimewold.summary: The frozen uplands north of the Wallmountains, where the clans fight the winter and each other, Brandfell smokes on the southern skyline, and the ice is older than anything that walks on it.
rimewold.body:
## The land

North of the [[wallgate]] the world goes white and stays white. Snowfields, black stone,
lakes frozen to the bottom, and wind that does not stop for a generation at a time. The
clans of the Rimewold live in longhouses dug into the hillsides and fight over the few
valleys where anything grows. [[brandfell]] smokes on the southern horizon, and since it
split the snow on that side melts in the middle of winter.

## The clans

The [[rimeclans]] have no king and want none. They raid south through the Wallgate when the
winters are bad, and the winters are always bad. A clan is a hall, a chief, and whoever
followed the chief home from the last fight.

## The ice

The ice is not only weather. In the deep north it stands in walls taller than any tower,
and in it, if you go far enough, there are shapes. The clans do not go that far.

## Places and powers

- [[the-icething]], the seventh-year moot on the ice.
- [[emberstead]], the smiths' town on Brandfell's warm face.
- [[the-sleepers-wall]], the ice with shapes in it.
- [[clan-skoll]], the clan that came back.

## Threads

- What is frozen in the far ice?
- Did [[gorvek]] go that far?

rotwater.name: Rotwater
aliases: the Smugglers' Port, the Fen Market
rotwater.summary: The rotten smuggling port on the Feverfen coast where the reavers of the Teeth sell their plunder; rum, poison, slaves, incense, and no questions, under lanterns that mean safe trading tonight and only tonight.
rotwater.body:
## The port

Stilt-houses over the mud at a river mouth, a quay of rotting timber, a hundred taverns and no
law. The reavers of [[the-teeth]] bring their prizes here, and the buyers of [[harrowmere]] come
masked to buy them back. Lanterns hung on the quay mean trading is safe tonight. When the
lanterns come down, it is not.

## Who is here

Everyone. Fen-folk selling fish and poison, reavers, Harrowmere factors, deserters from
[[the-unpaid-war]], [[the-honest-company-of-takers]] on a working holiday, and the
[[greycloaks]], who keep a small, polite house by the quay and tithe the lantern-oil.

## Threads

- Who pays for the lanterns?

saltcoast.name: Saltcoast
saltcoast.summary: Saltcoast: the salt-pan coast toward Harrowmere, whose pans the House of Salt owns in all but name.
saltcoast.body:
## The province

Saltcoast is the salt-pan coast toward Harrowmere, whose pans the House of Salt owns in all but name.

saltgrave.name: Saltgrave
saltgrave.summary: The mountain city of the Saltless, built in a gorge above Harrowmere by escaped slaves, where the salt they were bought for lies buried under the gate and no one owns anyone.
saltgrave.body:
## The city

A gorge in the hills above [[harrowmere]], walled at both ends, its houses cut into the rock
faces in tiers. Under the gate is the grave: a pit full of salt, a handful from every one of
[[the-saltless]] who ever came in. They walk over it every day.

## Its enemies

[[the-gilded]] have sent three armies up the gorge. The bones of the third are still in it. The
[[greycloaks]] have never been hired against Saltgrave, and the order has never said why.

## Threads

- How long can a city with no masters and no trade hold out against a city that owns everything?

smokemouth.name: Smokemouth
smokemouth.summary: The island of the Teeth that began to smoke the year Brandfell split and opened a crater last year; someone has landed on it, and is building something on the crater's lip.
smokemouth.body:
## The island

A black cone at the end of the jaw, the furthest of [[the-teeth]] from the coast. It was dead
rock for as long as the reavers remember. The year [[brandfell]] split, it began to smoke. Last
year the top fell in, and now it breathes: a long plume by day, a red glow at night, and the
sea around it warm enough to cook fish.

## The building

On the crater's lip, something is going up: black stone, laid in the old way, too large. Ships
that put in to see do not come back. [[oruana-blackwake]] has forbidden her captains to try.

## Threads

- Who is building, and in whose pattern? The stone looks like the [[ossar]]'s.

solmerine.name: Solmerine
solmerine.summary: The capital of Crownhold, built on a Vahrish provincial seat beside a wide bright lake the court calls the sun-sea; gold domes, marble stairs, poison at the banquets and beggars on every stair.
solmerine.body:
## The city

Solmerine stands on the hills above a shallow lake so bright under the summer sun that the court
calls it the sun-sea. The palace of [[aurelian-vasthorne]] is on the highest hill; the cathedral
of [[the-sunward-faith]] on the next; the great houses below; the poor everywhere else.

## Its life

Banquets, processions on [[helions-crown]], duels on the marble stairs, offices sold in the
cathedral's side-rooms, and the cellars where [[the-kneeling]] meet. It is the most beautiful city
in Harth and smells, in summer, of the lake.

stillwater.name: Stillwater
stillwater.summary: The debtors' prison on piles in the middle of the black lake of Harrowmere, where those who cannot pay live until the account is closed and they are sunk; the water around it is still, because nobody swims from it.
stillwater.body:
## The prison

A square of timber and iron on a hundred piles, a mile out on the black lake. The debtors live
in cages and work at whatever their creditors send out: rope, nets, copying ledgers. Every
month the books are balanced. A debtor whose account will never close is taken to the edge
with a stone and given to the lake.

## The water

It is still around Stillwater. Nobody swims from it, and not because of the distance. The
canal-lurkers of the lake have learned where the food comes from.

## Threads

- What comes up the piles at night, that the guards will not talk about?

strongrooms.name: The Strongrooms
strongrooms.summary: The clerks' strongrooms in the Brinevaults, where the first ledgers were kept under lock; the ledgers in them counted something other than lines.
strongrooms.body:
## The rooms

Every vault of the clerks had its strongroom, behind a door with two locks and a
clerk's seal on each. The first ledgers were kept there, and the clerks' own
pay, and the things the clerks took in lieu. The doors held when the water came
in. The packing has made them part of the wall.

## Threads

- What did the strongroom ledgers count, if not lines?

the-black-step.name: The Black Step
the-black-step.summary: The greatest of the Ossar temples, a black stepped pyramid in the heart of the Feverfen where lights burn on the top at night that nobody has lit; the fen-folk leave offerings on its lowest step.
the-black-step.body:
## The temple

In the middle of the [[feverfen]], where the water is deepest and the trees tallest, a black
pyramid stands up out of the swamp in steps, each one the height of a man. Vines cover the lower
steps. The upper ones are clean. Nothing grows on them, and nothing has been seen to clean them.

## The lights

On some nights there are lights at the top: pale, steady, not fire. The fen-folk leave fish,
reed-cloth and sometimes worse on the lowest step at new moon, and in the morning it is gone.
[[the-leech-mothers]] say the [[ossar]] are inside, and that the warmth coming out of the
temple has been rising every year since [[brandfell]] split.

## Threads

- How many steps are there below the water?

the-brink.name: The Brink
the-brink.summary: The front against the Ossar lands in year 150: a ragged line of forts, ruins and burned villages from the fen coast to the southern glass, held by every power in Harth in turn and by none for long; everything beyond it is lost.
the-brink.body:
## The line

Since [[the-fraying]] the [[feverfen]] and the south of the [[glassands]] are Ossar country. The
Brink is where that country ends, for now: watchtowers on the hills above the fen, Vahrish forts
reoccupied on the edge of the glass, villages that are burned every few summers by one side or the
other. Soldiers say *going to the Brink* the way the Mark says *going under*.

## Who holds it

Everyone, in turns. [[the-sunward-see]] marches south every summer under the sun-banner. Free
companies of [[the-halberd-march]] hold forts for pay. [[the-saddle-throne]] rides along it and
kills what comes out. [[harrowmere]] pays for it, at interest. The [[greycloaks]] hold its gates,
and the gates are always open.

## What comes over it

[[the-blindkin]] in the night, [[the-paid]] in columns, [[seepers]] through the ground, and once or
twice a year a [[the-stonesleepers]] walking upright, and then a fort is gone.

the-counted-lands.name: The Counted Lands
the-counted-lands.summary: The land south of the Glassands, where the caravans do not go; the Hadd say the Ossar still rule there, and that men there are still kept, fed and counted.
the-counted-lands.body:
## What is said

South of the [[glassands]] the maps stop. The [[the-hadd]] say the land goes on, green, rich and
ordered, and that the [[ossar]] never went under there, because the knot was tied in the north and
did not reach so far. Men live there, the Hadd say, in neat villages, fed, counted, and taken.

## What is known

Nothing. Once in a generation someone walks out of the south across the glass: thin, quiet, with a
number tattooed on the inside of the wrist. They do not talk about it. They do not stay long.

## How they live

Happily. Fed, well, at peace, and numbered: [[the-count]] decides everything, including when they
are taken.

## Threads

- Are the Counted Lands what Harth would be, if the knot gave?

the-grass-sea.name: The Grass Sea
the-grass-sea.summary: The endless grassland east of the mountains, where the Hoofborn ride; once a generation it pours west over Crownhold and Harrowmere like a flood, and then goes home.
the-grass-sea.body:
## The land

East of the eastern hills the trees stop and the grass begins, and it does not stop. A sea of it,
to the height of a horse's chest, moving under the wind for a thousand miles. The [[the-hoofborn]]
live on it, and nothing else does that the Hoofborn have not decided to leave alive.

the-greywood.name: The Greywood
the-greywood.summary: The forest of the west Mark that died in the Ashfall and never fell; grey trunks to the horizon, no leaves, no birds, outlaws in the hollows and worse things in the deep of it.
the-greywood.body:
## The wood

West of [[hookford]] the old forest of the Mark stood in the path of the ash. It died standing.
Thirty years on, the trunks are still there, grey and bare, hard as bone, and the wind goes
through them with a sound like breathing. Nothing grows under them. Nothing nests in them.

## Who lives there

Outlaws, because the [[greycloaks]] do not go in. Charcoal-burners, because grey wood burns hot.
And in the deep of it, past where the outlaws go, things the outlaws do not name.

## Threads

- Why has nobody ever found the far side of the deep wood?

the-halberd-march.name: The Halberd March
the-halberd-march.summary: The soldier-kingdom of the north road, founded by Marcus Halberd and the Unmourned between Crownhold and Gallowmark; its kings are captains, its law is the company contract, and it holds Grimwatch.
the-halberd-march.body:
## The realm

The army crowned [[marcus-halberd]], and the army is what he kept: the north road, the border
houses, and [[grimwatch]], which he took from the Greycloaks by paying them more. His successors
are the captains of [[the-unmourned]], each chosen by the company, each sworn on the rope.

## In the year 150

Poor, hard, and the best soldiers in Harth. The March fights Solmerine and the See for the
heartland, and sends companies south to the Ossar front for pay. It worships [[nevermourn]] above
the sun, and its kings do not weep.

the-iron-hall.name: The Iron Hall
aliases: the King's Hall, the Hall under the Roof
the-iron-hall.summary: The hall of the last king of Kell under its roof of iron plates, where the king still sits in the empty crown, his guard still stands in its ranks, the ledger lies open, and the floor is warm.
the-iron-hall.body:
## The hall

The iron roof is the only part of [[kell]] the coast can see, and since [[the-ebb]] it stands
clear of the salt a little longer every low water. Under it the king sits with the
[[iron-crown-of-kell]] on his head and three empty sockets in it. The iron is warm.

## The guard

The king's household guard drowned at their posts in full iron, and [[the-standing]] are
what is left of them: two ranks down the length of the hall, salt-white, facing the door.
They do not move while the king sits. Reach for what is his and they do.

## The floor

The flagstones are warm under the silt, warmer the nearer the throne. In the middle of the
floor is the grate of the great cistern, and the water that goes down it comes back up as
steam on a cold day. [[the-heave]] is under the hall, and closest here.

## The ledger

[[linelord]] lies open on its stand at the king's right hand. The last line in it is not the
king's. [[corve]] sits beside it and has not moved in years. Behind the throne, the
[[kings-way]] goes up.

## Threads

- Is one of the three rubies still in this room, as Sarn has never quite denied?
- What did [[gorvek]] take out of here in a sack?

the-saddle-throne.name: The Saddle Throne
the-saddle-throne.summary: The khanate the Hoofborn founded in the east of old Crownhold under Sorgan Windbreaker in year ten; its khans still hold court on horseback, and the old Marcheast is grassland again.
the-saddle-throne.body:
## The coming

In the tenth winter, while the three crowns fought each other and the south was burning,
[[sorgan-windbreaker]] came west over the hills with every tribe of [[the-hoofborn]]. [[the-iron-hundred]]
rode out to meet him and died to the last knight. He did not go home. He took [[marcheast]] and
let it go back to grass.

## In the year 150

The khans of the Saddle Throne hold court in tents in the ruins of the eastern towns, and sit on
their horses to give judgment. The khanate trades horses to all three realms of Crownhold, raids
all three, and is the only power in Harth that has fought the Ossar on open ground and won. They
know now what pushed them west.

the-sleepers-wall.name: The Sleepers' Wall
the-sleepers-wall.summary: The cliffs of ancient ice in the far north of the Rimewold, taller than any tower, in which shapes stand frozen; the clans say they are not dead, they are sleeping.
the-sleepers-wall.body:
## The wall

Far north, past the last valley anyone has farmed, the ice stands up in a wall: blue-white,
miles long, higher than the towers of [[crownhold]]. In it, deep, there are shapes. Tall ones,
too tall, standing upright with their arms at their sides, the way the [[ossar]] were drawn on
the walls of their temples. Behind them, deeper, larger ones that are not shaped like anything.

## The sleep

The [[rimeclans]] say the shapes are sleeping, not dead, and that the cold is what keeps them
asleep. Since [[brandfell]] split, the north has been warmer. Water runs down the face of the Wall
in summer now. [[clan-skoll]] went there and came back changed.

## Threads

- How much warmer does the north have to get?

the-sunward-see.name: The Sunward See
the-sunward-see.summary: The church-realm of the Sunward Faith in Granaria and the old heartland, which crowned Seraphine, burned her when she broke the ring, and kept her throne; ruled by its Exarchs, at war with the dark below and with everyone else.
the-sunward-see.body:
## The realm

The chapel crowned [[seraphine-vasthorne]]. When she broke the ring, the chapel burned her, and the
Exarch [[hadrian-mournevale]] took the throne in the name of [[helion-castor]], for safekeeping.
Nobody has given it back. The See is the grain heartland of old [[crownhold]], ruled from the
cathedral by Exarchs of the [[the-sunward-faith]].

## In the year 150

The See is the shield against the dark: its armies march south to the Ossar front every summer
under the sun-banner. It is also the realm that burns the most heretics, sells the most offices,
and has the most silver-eyed bishops.

the-teeth.name: The Teeth
the-teeth.summary: A chain of black volcanic islands off the Feverfen coast, where the reaver fleets winter, the slave ships of Harrowmere are taken, and no law in Harth reaches.
the-teeth.body:
## The islands

Forty black islands in a curve like a broken jaw, steep, hot, with good harbours in their
lee and nothing growing on their windward side. The reaver fleets winter here and raid from
here: the Harrowmere slave galleys, the Crownhold grain ships, the coast towns of the fen.

## The law

There is none but the Captain's Oath: a captain's word, once given, is kept, because a
captain who breaks it is hanged from the mast on Hask's pattern by their own crew. The reavers have
never heard of [[the-first-knot]]. They keep it anyway.

## Who is here

- [[oruana-blackwake]], the reaver queen, and [[blackwakes-own]].
- [[smokemouth]], the island that breathes.

## Threads

- Why does a second island smoke, since Brandfell split?

the-tenth-palace.name: The Tenth Palace
the-tenth-palace.summary: The palace on the Grand Canal of Harrowmere with no doors and no windows, where the Tenth Prince lives; the nine houses of the Gilded pay it something every year, and none of them will say what.
the-tenth-palace.body:
## The house

Between the palaces of Salt and Tallow stands one more, as fine as either, built of the same
pale stone, and it has no doors. No windows. No water-gate. The canal runs along its walls and
nothing goes in. The people of [[harrowmere]] call whatever lives there the Tenth Prince.

## The payment

Once a year, on the night of [[the-hiring-of-the-wise]], each of [[the-gilded]] sends a sealed
chest by barge, and the barge is tied against the blank wall, and in the morning the chest is
gone. Each house keeps the contents in its own ledger. No house has ever shown another.

## Threads

- What did the Gilded buy, when they bought Vahr's debts, that came with a house?

the-underhollow.name: The Underhollow
the-underhollow.summary: What lies at the bottom of Greyhollow under the smoke and the ash: the northernmost Ossar temple, built in a ring around a crack that goes down to the fire under the Mark, so that its priests could kneel at the edge of it.
the-underhollow.body:
## The bottom

Under three men's depth of ash and the smoke that stands on it, the floor of [[greyhollow]] is
black stone, and on the stone stands a temple: a ring of [[ossar]] columns, too tall, around a
crack in the ground a hundred paces long. The crack goes down. Heat comes up out of it, and the
smoke, and a sound like breath.

## Why it was built

The Ossar built their temples near their masters. This one is the nearest any of them came to
the surface in the north: the place where [[the-unborn]] could be heard best. When the knot was
tied it was buried and forgotten. The ash of [[the-ashfall]] filled the hollow over it. The
smoke is what comes up through the ash.

## Who has been there

[[mardra]]. Some [[smokewalkers]]. Nobody else who came back.

## Threads

- Is the crack getting wider?

ush-kaddah.name: Ush-Kaddah
aliases: the Well That Does Not Count
ush-kaddah.summary: The only living city of the Glassands, built around a well no one has found the bottom of; neutral ground for every Hadd tribe, Well-King and caravan, where blood spilled is paid for in water.
ush-kaddah.body:
## The city

A circle of white walls around a hole in the glass. The well at the heart of Ush-Kaddah is
wide as a market square and goes down past the reach of any rope. The water is cold and never
fails. Around it, the only city in the [[glassands]]: markets, caravanserais, Hadd tents, the
counting-houses of [[harrowmere]], and a small grey chapterhouse of the [[greycloaks]].

## The peace

The name means *the water that does not count*: here no tribe, king or caravan owes anything
for drinking. Blood spilled inside the walls is paid for in water, weighed against the dead, and
the killer goes thirsty for the debt. Even [[the-well-kings]] keep the peace here.

## Threads

- What is at the bottom of the well, that keeps the water cold?

vinalis.name: Vinalis
vinalis.summary: Vinalis: the wine province of the southern hills, terraced, sun-drunk and owned by absent lords in Solmerine.
vinalis.body:
## The province

Vinalis is the wine province of the southern hills, terraced, sun-drunk and owned by absent lords in Solmerine.

wallgate.name: Wallgate
wallgate.summary: The one pass through the Wallmountains, a throat of black rock with a Greycloak toll-house in it; the only gate into Gallowmark from the north, and the one nobody can close.
wallgate.body:
## The pass

The Wallmountains have one gap, and the Mark calls it the Wallgate because nobody in the
Mark wastes a second word. It is a throat of black rock a day's walk long, with the first of
the grey rivers coming down through it cold enough to stop a heart. North of it is [[brandfell]], still smoking, and whatever is past that. South of it is [[bonereach]].

## The toll-house

The [[greycloaks]] hold the Wallgate the way they hold everything: one house, one captain,
one open door. [[tolm]] sits in it. Nobody has ever taken the Wallgate by force, because
nobody has ever needed to. It is a gate that cannot be shut, and the order likes those.

## What comes through

Since the grey lifted, things come down out of the north through the Wallgate that did not
before. The toll-house tithes them like anyone else.

## Threads

- What is north of the Wallgate?
- Why does the first river run warm for one night each winter?

wrackhead.name: Wrackhead
wrackhead.summary: The headland over the drowned city, where the Greycloaks' first fort stands, the coast folk keep the salt-pile for Vorr, and the wreckers dive Old Kell for what the sea has not kept.
wrackhead.body:
## The head

A black headland shaped like a fist, with Old [[kell]] under the water at its knuckles. The
[[greycloaks]] built their first fort here, forty years ago, to guard the drowned quays. It
is the smallest fort they hold and the only one they have never left.

## The salt-pile

Below the fort, on the shingle, the coast folk keep a pile of wreck-wood and salt for
[[vorr]]. A plank from every wreck, a handful from every net. The Greycloaks tithe
everything on the coast and have never touched the pile.

## The wreckers

The people of Wrackhead dive. On a still day at low water you can see the iron roof of
Kell's hall, and once a year somebody goes down to it. [[rauk]] has gone down more than
anyone, come up with less each time, and stopped talking about it.

## Since the Ebb

The water is going out. The quays are showing. Since [[the-ebb]] the fort has doubled its
garrison and the salt-pile has doubled in height, and neither side has said why.

## Threads

- What is the fort really guarding: Kell, or the pile?

ysveld.name: Ysveld
ysveld.summary: The land across the western sea whose tall, courteous people trade with Harrowmere under white sails, and never say where on it they come from or why they come.
ysveld.body:
## The land

Nobody in Harth has been there and come back to say so. The ships come from the west, a few each
summer, white-sailed and too fast, into [[harrowmere]], and their people call it Ysveld.

## The people

Tall, fair, soft-voiced, with names like Ilvar, Saelith and Corvanne. They are unfailingly
courteous. They buy iron, salt, Ossar bones and, once, a [[the-hungry-books]], and pay in silver
that does not tarnish. They do not drink, do not marry, and do not answer questions about home.

## What they are

Ysveld serves [[aelarion]], the Watcher Between the Stars, which is to what is above what
[[the-unborn]] are to what is below. Ysveld is preparing for war against the below, and Harth is
where the front line is.

## Threads

- Why do the Ysveldings buy Ossar bones?
- Have they ever bought one of [[the-nine-irons]]?

argentine-houses.name: The Argentine Houses
argentine-houses.summary: The noble houses scattered through Harth whose children are born with pale silver eyes and who claim the blood of the emperors of Vahr; some whisper the blood is older and colder than that.
argentine-houses.body:
## Who they are

A dozen houses, more or less: three in [[crownhold]], two in [[harrowmere]], one with a ruin in
the [[glassands]], one in Gallowmark that does not admit it. Every few generations a child is
born to them with eyes like new silver, and that child inherits, whatever the order of birth.
They say the eyes are the blood of [[old-vahr]].

## The whisper

The emperors of Vahr learned their sorcery from the [[ossar]], and the Ossar's eyes were pale.
The Argentine Houses are fond of the cold, slow to warm, and very good at sorcery. They marry
each other. They do not let physicians bleed them.

## Threads

- Is the Vasthorne line one of them?
- What do the silver-eyed children dream about?

blackwakes-own.name: Blackwake's Own
blackwakes-own.summary: The reaver crews of Oruana Blackwake, freed rowers to a man, who take Harrowmere's slave galleys and send their people to Saltgrave; heroes on every coast Harrowmere does not own, and the first target of every fleet it hires.
blackwakes-own.body:
## The crews

Every one of them has rowed in chains. They wear the scar of the oar-iron on the ankle and do
not hide it. They take only slave ships, or ships that owe [[the-gilded]], which is all of them.

## Custom

They leave a galley drifting with its hold open and its masters chained to the oars. The
[[the-saltless]] of [[saltgrave]] send them salt every year, which in Saltgrave is the
greatest honour there is.

clan-skoll.name: Clan Skoll-Without-Fire
clan-skoll.summary: One of the three clans that walked north into the far ice after Brandfell split, and the only one to come back; they no longer light fires, and they do not feel the cold.
clan-skoll.body:
## Who they were

Clan Skoll was a small, hard clan of the far north, sixty spears and a longhouse. When
[[brandfell]] split and the winters went strange, Skoll and two other clans walked north into
the ice toward [[the-sleepers-wall]], looking for land the fire could not reach.

## Who came back

Skoll came back. Fewer, thinner, and pale to the lips. They do not light fires, not for cooking,
not for warmth, and they sit in the snow at night without cloaks. They say they made a bargain
at the Wall. They will not say with whom. The other two clans did not come back at all.

## Threads

- What did Skoll promise, and to what?

greycloaks.name: The Greycloaks
greycloaks.summary: The grey-cloaked order that holds Gallowmark by taking villages through the one gate left open; tithe-collectors, hook-wielders, and the only law most of the Mark has seen.
greycloaks.body:
## What they are

The Greycloaks began as the men who guarded the drowned quays of [[kell]] so that nobody
would steal what the sea had not yet taken. Forty years on, they guard everything, and what
they guard they tithe. Their cloaks are grey because grey hides ash, and the order was born
in the [[the-ashfall]].

## How they take a village

Never by storm. A Greycloak captain rides in alone, finds the one gate left open, and sits
down inside it. By evening the village is paying tithe and thinks it decided to. Every siege
in Gallowmark has been lost this way, which is why the wise close every gate, including the
ones they cannot see.

## The books

What the order tithes it writes down. The tithe-books hang from the hooks on the bridge at
[[hookford]], in Captain [[drusk]]'s hand, and the hangmen say they are a poor copy of the
ledger [[linelord]]. Captain [[tolm]] keeps the [[wallgate]] and writes nothing down.

## Beyond the Mark

The order holds Gallowmark, and nothing else, and is everywhere. It keeps a chapterhouse in
every city of [[harth]]: on the Grand Canal in [[harrowmere]], under the palace walls of
[[crownhold]], at the wells of the [[glassands]]. It rules no kingdom and wants none. It is
hired: to farm a king's taxes, keep a city's gates, guard a prince's debtors, hold a pass.
It is paid a tenth, and it takes the tenth politely, and somewhere in every kingdom there is
a gate the order holds and the king has forgotten he gave it.

The order is older than it says. It is [[the-tenth-legion]] of Vahr, which kept its gates when
the empire burned and never stopped. Nobody knows who leads it. The captains say *the Lady*, and lower their
voices. That is [[ishara-grey]]. The captains answer to the books, and the books answer to
someone.

## Enemies


[[gorvek]] has a price on his head that the order raises every winter. [[sarn]] they have tried
to hire and to kill, and the order's own records disagree on which came first.

house-aldemar.name: House Aldemar
house-aldemar.summary: House Aldemar, the oldest house of Crownhold, holders of Granaria and the grain, who have married into the throne three times and never sat on it.
house-aldemar.body:
## The house

House Aldemar is one of the five great houses of [[crownhold]], the oldest house of Crownhold, holders of Granaria and the grain, who have married into the throne three times and never sat on it.

## In the Three Crowns

Every great house must choose in [[the-three-crowns]]. House Aldemar has chosen, or says it has, which in
[[solmerine]] is not the same thing.

house-corvaith.name: House Corvaith
house-corvaith.summary: House Corvaith, the soldier-house of the Eastmarch, which leads the Iron Hundred and has not forgiven the Hoofborn for sixty years.
house-corvaith.body:
## The house

House Corvaith is one of the five great houses of [[crownhold]], the soldier-house of the Eastmarch, which leads the Iron Hundred and has not forgiven the Hoofborn for sixty years.

## In the Three Crowns

Every great house must choose in [[the-three-crowns]]. House Corvaith has chosen, or says it has, which in
[[solmerine]] is not the same thing.

house-lucentis.name: House Lucentis
house-lucentis.summary: House Lucentis, the house of bishops and scholars, which fills half the high offices of the Sunward Faith and backs Seraphine in public.
house-lucentis.body:
## The house

House Lucentis is one of the five great houses of [[crownhold]], the house of bishops and scholars, which fills half the high offices of the Sunward Faith and backs Seraphine in public.

## In the Three Crowns

Every great house must choose in [[the-three-crowns]]. House Lucentis has chosen, or says it has, which in
[[solmerine]] is not the same thing.

house-sabinus.name: House Sabinus
house-sabinus.summary: House Sabinus, the money-house of the Saltcoast, deepest in debt to Harrowmere and deepest in its counting-houses, which backs Tiberian the Fair.
house-sabinus.body:
## The house

House Sabinus is one of the five great houses of [[crownhold]], the money-house of the Saltcoast, deepest in debt to Harrowmere and deepest in its counting-houses, which backs Tiberian the Fair.

## In the Three Crowns

Every great house must choose in [[the-three-crowns]]. House Sabinus has chosen, or says it has, which in
[[solmerine]] is not the same thing.

house-trevane.name: House Trevane
house-trevane.summary: House Trevane, the border house of the north road, holders of the march toward Gallowmark and Grimwatch, hard, poor and proud.
house-trevane.body:
## The house

House Trevane is one of the five great houses of [[crownhold]], the border house of the north road, holders of the march toward Gallowmark and Grimwatch, hard, poor and proud.

## In the Three Crowns

Every great house must choose in [[the-three-crowns]]. House Trevane has chosen, or says it has, which in
[[solmerine]] is not the same thing.

ossar.name: The Ossar
ossar.summary: The tall, pale, cold-blooded people who ruled Harth before men, as priests of the Unborn; men were their cattle, until men hanged a god to bind them under the earth.
ossar.body:
## What they were

Taller than a man by a head, white as a thing grown in a cellar, with eyes like wet stone
and blood that does not warm. The Ossar built the black temple-cities whose roots are still
under the [[feverfen]] and the [[glassands]], and in them they kept the [[the-unborn]]
company and kept men the way men keep pigs: fed, counted, and taken.

They taught men sorcery. It was the cruellest thing they did, because it worked.

## The fall

Men rose, once, and lost, many times. Then they tied the [[the-first-knot]] on a ridge in
the north, and the oath held, and the Ossar went down into the earth after their masters.
Not all of them. Not all the way.

## Now

Bones too long for any grave are dug up in the Glassands every year. The fen-folk of the
Feverfen say the Ossar never left their temples, only the daylight. The [[the-kneeling]] say
the Ossar are coming back, and that it will be good to be counted again.

## Threads

- How many of them are still awake under the Feverfen?
- Is anything in a human throne-room descended from them?

qarr-dhuun.name: Qarr-Dhuun
qarr-dhuun.summary: The guild of diggers who go down into the ruins of the Glassands for gold and Ossar bones, and sell both in Harrowmere; the Hadd name means those who take from the dead, and it is not a compliment.
qarr-dhuun.body:
## The guild

Rope, lamp, pick and a debt to a Harrowmere house: that is a digger. Qarr-Dhuun licenses them,
maps the ruins, sells the finds, and takes half. They go down through the sand into Vahr's
streets, and under the streets into the black foundations of the [[ossar]].

## What they bring up

Gold, glass, statues with melted faces, and bones too long for any grave, which sell in
[[harrowmere]] for more than gold to buyers who do not give names. About one digger in five
does not come up. The guild writes them off in its ledger the same day.

## Threads

- Who is buying the Ossar bones, and what is being built with them?

rimeclans.name: The Rimeclans
rimeclans.summary: The clans of the Rimewold, who have no king, fight the winter and each other, and come south through the Wallgate when the winters are bad; the Reach of Gallowmark is their nearest kin and their oldest grudge.
rimeclans.body:
## Who they are

Tall, pale-haired, cold-eyed, and loud, which is how the Reach can tell them from its own.
A clan is a longhouse, a chief, and the men and women who followed the chief home. They count
wealth in iron, horses and the skulls over the door.

## What they want

Warm land. There is none north of the Wallgate, and the [[greycloaks]] hold the gate, so
every bad winter the clans come down to the toll-house and [[tolm]] asks them politely for a
tenth, and every bad winter some of them pay and some of them do not.

## Custom

A clan-chief is chosen by the clan standing behind them. When nobody stands behind, there
is no chief. [[hrok]] has had the longest line behind him in living memory.

## Threads

- Why have three clans gone north into the ice since Brandfell split, and not come back?

river-priests.name: The River-Priests of Thurn
river-priests.summary: The barefoot priesthood of the river-god Thurn, keepers of the names, who alone dare call Sarn the Lord of Streams and who say all the grey rivers are one.
river-priests.body:
## Who they are

Barefoot, wet to the knee, and unwelcome at most tables, the river-priests walk the banks of
the grey rivers of [[gallowmark]] and keep the names of things. They hold that every stream
in the Mark is the same river, [[thurn]], pretending to be many, and that to name a thing
truly is to have a grip on it.

## The naming

It was the river-priests who named [[sarn]] the Lord of Streams, and they meant it as a
warning: here is the thing that goes where water goes and takes what water takes. They have
named every Greycloak captain and every gallows on [[hangmoot]], and once, to his face,
[[gorvek]].

## Custom

A river-priest will answer any question with a name, and never with a reason.

smokewalkers.name: Smokewalkers
smokewalkers.summary: People who have walked into the smoke of Greyhollow and walked out again, changed: some with gifts, a sense of fire, a voice that carries, hands that do not burn; some with a hunger that nothing in the Mark will feed.
smokewalkers.body:
## Who they are

Most who go into the smoke of [[greyhollow]] do not come out. Those who do are Smokewalkers. Their
eyes catch firelight a moment too long. They are warm to the touch in winter.

## What they come out with

A gift, sometimes: knowing where fire is under the ground, walking through flame unburned, being
believed. A hunger, sometimes: for heat, for meat, for the smoke itself, until they walk back in
and do not come out again. Nobody knows which they will get until they get it.

## In the world

- [[the-kneeling]] at [[lowfold]] send their own into the smoke on purpose.
- [[the-ashen]] do not count Smokewalkers among them, and will not say why.

the-ashen.name: The Ashen
the-ashen.summary: The people who stayed on the rim of Greyhollow through the Ashfall and never left; grey-skinned, tattooed in ash, and feared by half the Mark.
the-ashen.body:
## Who they are

When the ash came down, most of the east fled south. The Ashen did not. They stayed in their
villages on the rim of [[greyhollow]], ate what they could, breathed what they had to, and came
out of the generation grey to the bone. Their children are born grey. They tattoo themselves
with ash rubbed into cuts, a line for every winter they have outlasted.

## What the Mark thinks

That they eat their dead. That [[mardra]] is one of them. That they can walk into the smoke of
the Hollow and out again. Two of those are true.

## Threads

- What do the Ashen know about the warmth under the Hollow that nobody else does?

the-gilded.name: The Gilded
the-gilded.summary: The nine merchant princes of Harrowmere, who bought the debts of the fallen empire and have been collecting from the whole Sunder ever since; they hire armies, sorcerers and the Greycloaks, and own a share of every throne.
the-gilded.body:
## The houses

Nine houses, each with a palace on the Grand Canal, a fleet, a bank and a feud with the other
eight. A prince is whoever holds the house's ledger. Princes rarely die of old age. [[aleid-van-der-haalst]],
of the House of Salt, has held hers for thirty years, which is the record.

## The debt

When [[old-vahr]] burned, the Gilded bought its debts from the dead for a copper on the
crown. Every kingdom of Harth grew up owing Harrowmere for an empire it never saw. The
princes do not collect it all. They collect enough.

## Threads

- What did the Gilded pay for, that they keep in the Tenth Palace?

the-hadd.name: The Hadd
the-hadd.summary: The veiled night-walking nomads of the Glassands, who read the stars and the cracks in the glass, lead the caravans between the ruins, and trust nobody who walks by day.
the-hadd.body:
## Who they are

*Hadd* is their word for the border, and they are the people of it: the line between glass and
sand, between night and day, between the ruins and the living. They walk only at night, faces
veiled to the eyes, and sleep under black tents through the burning day. A Hadd guide is the
only way across the [[glassands]] that is not a way to die.

## Names

Their names come from a language with no cousin in Harth, hard and full of breaks: Qeth,
Ysh'ra, Torr-Halaq, Ummar-Seb. A child is not named until it has walked one night on the
glass.

## Custom

To walk by day is to be a *sun-fool*. To unveil before a stranger is to offer your life. The
Hadd will guide anyone across the glass for water, and will leave anyone on it who lies to
them.

## Threads

- Why will no Hadd go within sight of [[old-vahr]]?

the-holdfast-lords.name: The Holdfast Lords
the-holdfast-lords.summary: The petty lords of Gallowmark, each with a timber or stone holdfast and a few dozen swords, who fight each other for what the Greycloaks leave and hire Ashborn by the season.
the-holdfast-lords.body:
## The lords

After [[the-ashfall]] the Mark was empty of everything but the [[greycloaks]] and whoever could
hold a hill. The Holdfast Lords are whoever held one: a tower on a mound, a ditch, a palisade,
a hall full of hired swords. They call themselves lords. The Greycloaks call them that too,
politely, and take a tenth of whatever they take.

## Their wars

Small, endless and bloody. A holdfast changes hands every few winters. The lords hire Ashborn
out of [[bonereach]] for the fighting, and the Ashborn hire out to whoever is winning.

the-honest-company-of-takers.name: The Honest Company of Takers
the-honest-company-of-takers.summary: The thieves' guild of Harrowmere, chartered, sealed and paying dues, which says its first master was Sarn; it steals by contract, keeps a ledger as careful as any prince's, and is the only honest business in the city.
the-honest-company-of-takers.body:
## The company

A guildhall with a sign over the door, a charter with nine forged seals, a tariff of fees
painted on the wall: so much for a purse, so much for a ring, so much for a man's papers out
of a locked room. A member pays dues. A non-member who steals in Harrowmere is found in the
canal. The city watch is a member.

## Its founder

The Company says [[sarn]] wrote its charter, a long time before Kell, and left it unsigned.
The charter is in the guildhall under glass. The bottom of it is blank. Every master of the
Company has looked at that blank and decided not to fill it in.

## Threads

- Did Sarn steal the rubies on a Company contract, and who paid?

the-hoofborn.name: The Hoofborn
the-hoofborn.summary: The horse peoples of the Grass Sea, who ride west over the hills once a generation and take everything; they last came sixty years ago, the old men of Crownhold still remember the fires, and the calendars say they are due.
the-hoofborn.body:
## Who they are

Small, hard, bow-legged, born in the saddle, and named for it. They have no cities and want none.
A Hoofborn host is a nation on horseback: men, women, children, herds, and the gods in carts.

## The coming

Once a generation the grass fails, or something east of the grass pushes them, and they come
west over the hills into [[crownhold]] and up to the lake of [[harrowmere]]. They last came sixty
years ago. They burned forty towns, took a king's head, and went home. The old men of Crownhold
remember the fires. The calendars of the Gilded say they are due again, and [[the-gilded]] have
begun buying horses.

## Threads

- What pushes them west?

the-iron-hundred.name: The Iron Hundred
the-iron-hundred.summary: Crownhold's order of armoured knights, a thousand strong until the Hoofborn broke them sixty years ago; a hundred now, sworn on the rope to be a thousand again and to ride east.
the-iron-hundred.body:
## The order

They were the Iron Thousand once, the heaviest horse in Harth, and they rode out to meet
[[the-hoofborn]] sixty years ago in [[marcheast]] and were shot to pieces in a single afternoon by
riders who never let them close. A hundred came home. The order kept the number as its name and
swore a [[rope-oaths]] to be a thousand again before it dies.

## Now

They are a hundred still, led by [[house-corvaith]], heavy, proud and obsolete, and they are the
only part of Crownhold's army that wants [[sorgan-windbreaker]] to come.

the-kneeling.name: The Kneeling
the-kneeling.summary: The secret cult of the Unborn, spread through every city of Harth; they kneel to what is under the world, ask it for what they want, and say the Ossar are coming back and that it will be good to be counted again.
the-kneeling.body:
## What they are

Not one church. Cells: a cellar in [[crownhold]], a barge in [[harrowmere]], a ruin in the
[[glassands]], a farm at the edge of [[greyhollow]]. They meet at night, they kneel with
their foreheads on bare earth, and they ask. Sometimes they are answered.

## What they believe

That the [[the-first-knot]] was a crime. That men were happier counted. That the knot is
loosening, and that those who knelt first will be eaten last.

## How they work

They cut ropes. A gallows burned, a debt forgiven, an oath broken in public, an iron ring
stolen: the Kneeling do these things, because each one loosens the knot a little. The
hangmen of [[hangmoot]] hunt them, and hang them, and say each hanging pulls it tight again.

## Threads

- Did the Kneeling hire [[sarn]] to empty the crown?

the-leech-mothers.name: The Leech-Mothers
the-leech-mothers.summary: The healers of the Feverfen, women only, who fight the fever with leeches and poison and have gone into the Ossar temples further than anyone living; feared and loved in every drifthold.
the-leech-mothers.body:
## Who they are

Old women with leech-jars at their belts and black stains to the elbow. They draw the fever
out with leeches, kill the leeches, and burn them. They know every poison in the
[[feverfen]] and use most of them as medicine.

## What they know

The fever comes from the temples, they say. To learn to cure it they went in. Every Leech-Mother
has been inside [[the-black-step]] at least once, as her last lesson. Some do not come out.
Those who do know more about the [[ossar]] than any scholar of [[crownhold]], and say very
little.

## Threads

- What is the last lesson, inside the temple?

the-ninth-rope.name: The Ninth Rope
the-ninth-rope.summary: The order of hangmen of Hangmoot, who keep the knot tight: they hang the Mark's debtors on Hask's pattern, hunt the Kneeling across Harth, and burn the Paid.
the-ninth-rope.body:
## The order

The Reeve of [[hangmoot]] and the hangmen under him. Every one of them has been hanged, once, as
their oath, and cut down before the end; they wear the scar like a collar. They know what
[[the-first-knot]] is. That is their whole secret, and they keep it.

## The work

They hang, on the nine gallows and wherever else they are needed, because every debt paid at
the rope pulls the knot tight. They hunt [[the-kneeling]] from Gallowmark to [[harrowmere]], and
burn [[the-paid]], because a rope does not hold what has no breath.

## Threads

- What do they do when a king is the debtor?

the-saltless.name: The Saltless
the-saltless.summary: The escaped salt-slaves of Harrowmere and their children, who live free in the mountain city of Saltgrave under a law crueller than the one they fled; to be called saltless is an honour.
the-saltless.body:
## Who they are

Every slave sold in [[harrowmere]] is weighed against salt on the Stairs of Weighing, and the
salt is the price. The Saltless are the ones who ran, from galleys, mines and canal-houses, and
reached the mountains. They buried the salt they were bought for, and called the place
[[saltgrave]], and themselves the ones without a price.

## The law

No one in Saltgrave owns anyone. Anyone who tries is hanged in salt-sacks. Anyone who brings a
slaver's coin in is hanged beside them. Anyone who leaves and comes back is asked one question
at the gate, and nobody outside knows what it is.

## Threads

- Who is the gate-keeper, and what is the question?

the-sunward-faith.name: The Sunward Faith
the-sunward-faith.summary: The state church of Crownhold, sworn to Helion Castor against the dark below; gold domes, incense, tithes, a hierarchy for sale, and an Exarch who sits at the king's right hand.
the-sunward-faith.body:
## The church

Every town in [[crownhold]] has a sun-temple with a gilt dome, and every temple takes its tithe,
and the tithes go up to the cathedral in the capital, where the Exarch of the Sunward sits beside
the throne of [[aurelian-vasthorne]]. Offices in the church are bought the way offices at court
are. Many priests are believers. Few bishops are.

## Its enemies

The faith hates [[the-kneeling]] by doctrine: below against above. It also hates [[the-ninth-rope]],
because the hangmen say the sun is not what holds the dark down, a rope is. And it fears
[[quintus-ashhand]], who was one of its priests, and burned his arm in one of its chapels.

## Threads

- How many of its bishops kneel in the cellars at night?

the-tenth-legion.name: The Tenth Legion
the-tenth-legion.summary: The gate-legion of Vahr that held every gate, bridge and pass of the empire for a tenth of what went through; it outlived the empire, put on grey, and is the order the Mark calls the Greycloaks.
the-tenth-legion.body:
## The legion

Every gate of Vahr had a cohort of the Tenth, grey-cloaked, polite, taking a tenth. The legion
was never sent to war. It did not need to be: it held the gates, and an army that does not own
the gates is just a crowd.

## After the fall

When [[old-vahr]] burned, the Tenth did not. It had no emperor to obey and kept its gates anyway,
for whoever paid. In the [[the-broken-years]] it forgot its name, kept its cloaks and its tenth,
and became the order. The [[greycloaks]] say they began guarding the quays of [[kell]]. They began
there again. They are much older than that.

## Threads

- Who did the Tenth answer to, if not the emperor? And who do the books answer to now?

the-unmourned.name: The Unmourned
the-unmourned.summary: The free company of Marcus Halberd, the best-paid and least-loved swords in Crownhold; they give their dead to Nevermourn and weep for nobody, and nobody weeps for them.
the-unmourned.body:
## The company

Four thousand foot, six hundred horse, a baggage train like a town, and a black banner with a
white crow. The Unmourned have fought for Crownhold, against it, and for Harrowmere twice. Since
their captain stopped hiding his face, they fight for him.

## Custom

They do not bury their dead. They lay them out for the crows on the field, and sing over them
loudly and badly, and march on in the morning. A man of the Unmourned who weeps is fined a
month's pay. Most of them think it is cheap.

the-well-kings.name: The Well-Kings
the-well-kings.summary: The sorcerer-kings of the Glassands, each ruling a well, a ruined tower and a few hundred thirsty people, who war on each other with pacts the way other kings war with armies; Qeth-Ummar is the greatest of them.
the-well-kings.body:
## The kings

Water is power in the [[glassands]], and every well outside [[ush-kaddah]] has a king. They
live in the old Vahrish towers above their wells, with the people who need the water living
below. Each is a sorcerer. Each has paid [[the-unborn]] in at least one coin, and most in two.

## Their wars

A Well-King does not raise an army. He asks. Wells go bitter, caravans lose their way, a rival's
people wake up in the night unable to remember their names. [[qeth-ummar]] is the greatest of
them, and the others pay him in water to be left alone.

## Threads

- What happens to a well when its king pays the third coin?

aelarion.name: Aelarion
aelarion.summary: The god of Ysveld, a cold bright watcher between the stars, as old as the Unborn and no more human; Ysveld serves it, and is preparing a war against what is below.
aelarion.body:
## The god

The people of [[ysveld]] say there is something above as there is something below. [[the-unborn]]
were before birth, under the world. Aelarion is between the stars, over it: cold, bright, patient,
watching. It is not kind. It does not want what the Unborn want. That is the whole of its goodness.

## Its servants

Ysveld serves Aelarion as the [[ossar]] served the Unborn: utterly. Its envoys in Harth, like
[[saelith]], are its eyes. They buy Ossar bones to learn the enemy. They ask about [[the-nine-irons]]
because the knot is the front line, and Ysveld wants to know how long it will hold.

## Threads

- When the knot gives, will Ysveld come to save Harth, or to burn it clean?

hask.name: Hask
hask.summary: The hanged god of the gallows on the ridges; the first rulers of the Mark hanged him so the land would hold, and every debt in Gallowmark is still paid at his rope.
hask.body:
## The god

[[gallowmark]] is named for the gallows, and the gallows are for Hask. The first rulers of
the Mark, before [[kell]] had a quay, built nine gallows on a ridge and hanged their god on
the ninth so the land would hold. That is the story the hangmen tell, and they tell it with
the knot already tied. Hask did not die. A hanged god does not; he hangs. Everything owed in
the Mark is owed to the rope, and the rope is his.

## The debt

Hask is the god of what is owed. A tithe is a debt, an oath is a debt, a name given is a
debt. The [[greycloaks]] have never written Hask's name in a ledger, and they collect in his
shape: patiently, and once. Hask has no priests. He has hangmen, and the Reeve of
[[hangmoot]] is the first among them.

## The knot

What the hangmen do not tell strangers: the first men did not hang Hask so that the land would
hold. They hanged him so that something else would stay under it. That is [[the-first-knot]],
and the [[ossar]] and [[the-unborn]] are what it holds.

## The rope and the crown

The hangmen say the land is held in place by nine ropes and [[the-nine-irons]], and that the night
[[sarn]] emptied the [[iron-crown-of-kell]], the ninth ring, the ninth rope went slack.
Since [[the-ebb]] they have stopped saying nothing.

## Threads

- Is Hask the god the Greycloaks do not name, or the god they are afraid of?
- Whom did the first rulers hang, really?

helion-castor.name: Helion Castor
helion-castor.summary: The sun god of Crownhold's state church, the Sunward Faith; the bright father who stands against the dark below, worshipped in gold-domed temples by a church that is rich, corrupt and very powerful.
helion-castor.body:
## The god

Helion Castor is the sun, and the sun is above, and what is above stands against what is below.
That is the whole of the faith's teaching, and it is older than Crownhold: the priests say the
emperors of [[old-vahr]] prayed to him before they began to ask the other way.

## Whether he answers

The sun rises. The priests say that is the answer.

## Threads

- Did the emperors stop praying to him, or did he stop listening?

mother-murk.name: Mother Murk
mother-murk.summary: The hungry, fertile swamp-mother of the Feverfen; the fen-folk say they worship nothing, and feed her all the same.
mother-murk.body:
## The goddess

The outsiders call her Mother Murk. The fen-folk do not call her anything when she can hear.
She is the fen itself: the warm black water, the roots, the rot that makes the fen green. She
gives fish, reed, children and fever, and she takes what falls in.

## Feeding

The fen-folk say they worship nothing, because worship is what the [[ossar]] wanted. But every
village drops the first fish of the day back into the water, and the old people go into it
when they are done, without a boat, singing.

## Threads

- Is she older than the Ossar's temples, or did she grow in their shadow?

nevermourn.name: Nevermourn
nevermourn.summary: The crow goddess of battlefields and carrion, worshipped by the sellswords of all Harth; one does not weep for the fallen, one gives them to her.
nevermourn.body:
## The goddess

Nevermourn walks every field after the fighting, at dusk, in a cloak of black feathers, and
the crows come down where she points. She does not weep. That is the whole of her teaching:
the dead are not lost, they are given, and she takes them, and nothing given to her is ever
wasted.

## Her people

Sellswords, camp-followers, the gravediggers of every army, and the hangmen's crows. A free
company gives her one eye before a great battle, cut out of the head of the first enemy taken
alive. Soldiers do not say *he died*. They say *she has him*.

## Custom

To mourn openly for a soldier is to rob her. Free companies sing on the night after a battle,
loudly and badly, and anyone who weeps is put out of the firelight until they stop.

## Threads

- Does she take the dead of the [[the-paid]], who have nothing left to give?

the-old-smith-under-the-snow.name: The Old Smith Under the Snow
the-old-smith-under-the-snow.summary: The fire god of the Rimeclans, whose name is never said; they hold that Brandfell is his forge, that the ash was the sweepings of his work, and that he wants something burned every winter.
the-old-smith-under-the-snow.body:
## The god

The clans of the [[rimewold]] do not say his name. They are not sure he has one. They say
*the Old Smith*, and look south toward [[brandfell]] when they say it. Under the snow, under
the mountain, he works. The ring of his hammer is the ground shaking. The ash that came down
over the north was the sweepings of his floor.

## What he wants

Something burned every winter: a ship, a hall, a horse, a man. Smiths and charcoal-burners
pray to him, and every forge in the north has a hole in the back wall where the fire can see
out.

## In the world

- Since Brandfell split, the clans say, he has been forging something big. [[mardra]] says the
  clans are right that something is down there, and wrong about what.

## Threads

- Is the Old Smith one of [[the-unborn]], given a kinder face?

the-unborn.name: The Unborn
the-unborn.summary: The things that were before the gods and are under the world now, bound; every sorcery in Harth is borrowed from them, and every loan is paid back with interest.
the-unborn.body:
## What they are

Nobody living has seen one, and the [[ossar]], who served them, did not have a word for them
that a human mouth can make. They are older than [[thurn]], older than the sea [[vorr]]
keeps, older than the first rope. They were not born, so they do not die. They wait.

They are under the world: under the ice of the [[rimewold]], under the glass of the
[[glassands]], under the fens and the mountains and the drowned coast. The [[the-first-knot]]
put them there. It did not put them anywhere they cannot be heard.

## Sorcery

All sorcery is a pact with something below. A sorcerer asks, the Unborn give, and the
price is taken from the body, the memory or the soul, in that order, and the asking gets
easier each time. That is how every sorcerer in Harth ends: easier and easier, and then
not a person. [[mardra]] says she has paid only in the first two coins. Nobody believes her.

## Stirring

The knot is loosening. A rope went slack the night [[sarn]] emptied the
[[iron-crown-of-kell]], and ten years later [[brandfell]] split and burned. The fire under
the Mark, the warm iron, the rising coast: the river-priests have names for all of it. The
[[the-kneeling]] have one name for all of it, and they say it on their knees.

## Threads

- What do they want, if anything that was never born can want?
- Is the fire under the Mark one of them turning over in its sleep?

thurn.name: Thurn
thurn.summary: The river-god of Gallowmark, the one grey river that pretends to be many; cold, patient, and the only god whose priests are taken seriously by people who trust nothing.
thurn.body:
## The god

Thurn does not have a face, a temple, or a promise. Thurn has water, and water goes where it
goes. The people of [[gallowmark]] do not pray to Thurn; they keep out of the way. The
[[river-priests]] say this is the correct form of worship.

## The rivers

Three grey rivers come down out of the Wallmountains and meet the sea at [[kell]], and the
priests say they are one river pretending to be three. Thurn is in them the way cold is in
them: no voice, no wants, only weight and direction. In the dark years they ran grey with ash
from the north, and the priests say Thurn carried the north's dead to the sea and did not
complain.

## Threads

- Does Thurn mind that [[sarn]] has been called Lord of Streams?

vorr.name: Vorr
vorr.summary: The drowned god of the salt deep below the coast, who keeps what the sea takes and took Kell whole; the coast folk pay him in wreckage and do not ask for anything back.
vorr.body:
## The god

[[thurn]] is what flows. Vorr is where it stops. The [[river-priests]] say every grey river
is one river; the coast folk say yes, and it ends in Vorr's mouth. Vorr is the salt at the
bottom of things, the weight in a drowned man's boots, the god of what is kept. The people
of the drowned coast do not pray to Vorr. They pay. A plank from every wreck goes onto the
salt-pile at [[wrackhead]], and nobody says what for.

## Kell

Vorr took [[kell]] in one night and has been chewing since. The coast folk hold that the
crown never held the rivers; it held Vorr's mouth shut, and [[sarn]] opened it. The
river-priests call this a coast story. They have never gone down to the salt-pile to say so.

## The Ebb

Since [[the-ebb]] the sea has been going out from Old Kell. The coast folk say Vorr is
opening his mouth to give something back, and that a god who has kept for forty years does
not give back for nothing.

## Threads

- Does Vorr have the three rubies, or only the crown?
- What does the salt-pile buy?

hookbreaker.name: Hookbreaker
hookbreaker.summary: The long northern sword Gorvek took from a Greycloak captain and never named; the legends named it Hookbreaker for the hooks it broke, and it went north with him and was not seen again, though a hundred false ones hang in a hundred halls.
hookbreaker.body:
## The sword

A long, plain northern blade, black iron, a hand-and-a-half grip wrapped in horse-leather.
[[gorvek]] took it off a [[greycloaks]] captain on the coast road and never gave it a name,
because naming is river-priest work. The songs did it for him. It broke more Greycloak hooks than
anyone could count, and the songs count them anyway.

## After

It went north with him on [[gorveks-last-road]]. Every hall in the north and half the holdfasts of
the Mark have a Hookbreaker over the fire. None of them is it.

## Threads

- Would anyone know the real one if they saw it?

imryn.name: Imryn
imryn.summary: One of the three rubies of the Iron Crown of Kell, which held the third river, the one that runs through Fordham in its bed; taken by Sarn, and now, the stories say, with Sarn still.
imryn.body:
## The stone

Imryn held the third river, the one that runs shallow at [[fordham]]. Of the three, it is the one
everybody agrees about: [[sarn]] still has it. Where Sarn keeps it, nobody knows. The
[[the-honest-company-of-takers]] say it is the only thing their first master never sold.

## What it does

Set in one of [[the-nine-irons]], it holds the ring shut, and the ring holds a rope of
[[the-first-knot]]. Out of the iron, the stories disagree. Some say it gives the holder grip on
the river it held. Some say it gives the river grip on the holder.

## Threads

- What happens if it is set back?

iron-crown-of-kell.name: The Iron Crown of Kell
iron-crown-of-kell.summary: The iron crown of the kings of Kell, set with three rubies said to hold the three rivers in place; empty since Sarn took the stones in one night, and the city with them.
iron-crown-of-kell.body:
## The crown

Iron, not gold. The kings of [[kell]] wore iron because gold was for people with something
to prove. Three rubies were set in it, one for each of the grey rivers that met at the city,
and the river-priests of [[thurn]] said that while the stones sat in the iron, the rivers sat
in their beds.

## The ring

The crown is older than Kell. It is the ninth of [[the-nine-irons]] of [[the-first-knot]], carried
south and worn by the emperors of [[old-vahr]] before the kings of Kell had it, and the three
rubies, [[tharsk]], [[velloch]] and [[imryn]], were set in it to hold the ring shut. That is the part the river-priests leave out.

## The theft

[[sarn]] took all three in a single night. Nobody saw the face. The rivers left their beds.
Whether the crown held the water or only the belief in the crown did, Kell drowned either
way, and the empty iron is somewhere under it.

## Threads

- The three rubies are the three most valuable objects in Harth. Sarn, asked, changes the
  subject.

linelord.name: LineLord
linelord.summary: The king's ledger of Kell, which records every line of every wall in the Mark, who laid it, and who holds the ground behind it; named by the river-priests, read aloud by Vurn, listened to by Gorvek.
linelord.body:
## What it is

In the world, LineLord is a ledger: a big book bound in iron. Not of coin; of lines. Every
