wall in [[gallowmark]] is laid one line of stone at a time, and the king's clerks wrote down
who laid each line and how long it has stood, and nothing else. It does not say whether the wall was any good. It says who
held the ground, and for how long, and that is the whole of what it says. The last king of
[[kell]] kept it in the iron-roofed hall and read it the winter before the night, looking
for a wall that would hold. It is there still, open on its stand in [[the-iron-hall]], and
the last line in it is not the king's. The [[greycloaks]]' tithe-books are a poor copy of it. Brother
[[ruun]] named it, and then stopped talking about it, as the [[river-priests]] do.

[[vurn]] reads it aloud. [[gorvek]] says he does not need it, and listens to every line.

## The rule

The ledger counts lines and days. It is not a measure of worth, and the Reach has never
mistaken it for one: a wall nobody dares touch stands as long in the ledger as a wall that
earned its place.

Outside the world, LineLord is a command-line tool that reads `git blame` and reports who
holds which line of a codebase and for how long. This entry is where the world and the tool
meet. Its farewells are the sagas of the Reach in Vurn's cadence; its names are
Gallowmark's; its rule is the one above, and it stands on every screen.

## The holds

Under [[wrackhead]] the ledger names a holder for each of the four depths of [[kell]], by
who holds the most ground there and for how long, and calls them by the old titles: the
**Holder of the Quaysteps**, the **Lord of the Lowstreets**, the **Keeper of the
Brinevaults** and the **Sitter in the Iron Hall**. Above them is the **Linelord**, which goes
to whoever holds the most of the Mark in all; [[jarn]] holds it now. A title is won by
holding more and lost the same way. Old holders are not good ones. They are only the ones
nobody has moved yet.

## Threads

- Is the ledger in the hall the one the king read, or one of the copies the clerks made in
  the [[brinevaults]]?

streamlord.name: Streamlord
streamlord.summary: The name of a software development kit and of the grimoire that documents it; not a thing anyone in the Mark carries, only a book whose epigraphs borrow the Mark's voices.
streamlord.body:
## What it is

Streamlord is not a thing in [[gallowmark]]. Nobody in the Mark carries it, wields it, or
has heard of it. It is a software development kit, and its documentation is written as a
grimoire, and that grimoire borrows the Mark's voices for its epigraphs: [[sarn]] narrates
it, the creed on its first page is [[gorvek]]'s, and the names in it are Gallowmark's.

## The rule

What the grimoire says about streams is about the software. Nothing in the canon depends on
it, and no character in the Mark can make a river obey.

tharsk.name: Tharsk
tharsk.summary: One of the three rubies of the Iron Crown of Kell, which held the first river, the one that comes down through the Wallgate in its bed; taken by Sarn, and now, the stories say, with Harrowmere.
tharsk.body:
## The stone

Tharsk held the first river in its bed, the cold one that comes down out of the north through the
[[wallgate]]. The rumour of [[harrowmere]] is that it was sold there the year after Kell drowned, to
the House of Salt, and that it went by barge to [[the-tenth-palace]] and was never seen again.

## What it does

Set in one of [[the-nine-irons]], it holds the ring shut, and the ring holds a rope of
[[the-first-knot]]. Out of the iron, the stories disagree. Some say it gives the holder grip on
the river it held. Some say it gives the river grip on the holder.

## Threads

- What happens if it is set back?

the-hungry-books.name: The Hungry Books
the-hungry-books.summary: The grimoires of Vahr that teach the forms of the pacts; every copy wants to be read, finds its way to someone who will, and is never where it was left.
the-hungry-books.body:
## The books

The emperors of [[old-vahr]] wrote down how to ask, so that their heirs would not have to learn
it from the [[ossar]]. The books survived the fire. Nobody knows how many there are. Each one is
bound in pale leather, written in a hand no scribe of Harth can match, and opens most easily at
the page its reader most wants.

## The hunger

A Hungry Book does not stay where it is put. Locked in a chest, it is found in a market. Burned,
it is found in the ashes, a little scorched. It always ends in the hands of someone who will
read it, and the first asking in it is always small.

## In the world

- [[the-ninth-rope]] keeps eleven under the gallows at [[hangmoot]], in iron, and counts them
  every morning. Some mornings there are ten.
- [[the-kneeling]] copy them, which is a crime the books seem to enjoy.

the-last-asking.name: The Last Asking
aliases: the Emperor's Bill, the Glass Tablet
the-last-asking.summary: The tablet on which the last emperors of Vahr wrote what they asked of the Unborn on the night the empire burned; a contract, the Gilded say, and they own the debt.
the-last-asking.body:
## The tablet

A slab of black stone the height of a man, written on both sides in the emperors' hand, carried
out onto [[ahl-sereth]] on the last night and read aloud. When the fire came, the stone went white
and half of it ran into the glass. What is left stands in the throne-room of [[old-vahr]], before
[[qeth-ummar]], who reads it every night.

## The contract

[[the-gilded]] bought the debts of Vahr. They hold that the Last Asking is one of them: a contract,
with a price not yet paid in full. They have sent three expeditions to copy it. One came back.

## Threads

- What is written on the half that ran into the glass?

the-nine-irons.name: The Nine Irons
the-nine-irons.summary: The nine iron rings of the First Knot, one for each rope on Hangmoot; carried south and worn as crowns by the emperors of Vahr and the kings after them; the Iron Crown of Kell was the ninth, and the House of Salt buys every one that comes to market.
the-nine-irons.body:
## The rings

Nine ropes hang on [[hangmoot]] and nine iron rings were forged to hold them shut, one for each.
The first men gave them to their chiefs to wear, so that the oath would sit on the heads of those
who ruled. The emperors of [[old-vahr]] wore them as crowns, under the gold. When the empire broke,
the rings went with the provinces.

## Where they are

- The ninth was the [[iron-crown-of-kell]], set with [[tharsk]], [[velloch]] and [[imryn]]. It is
  empty.
- One is on the head of [[aurelian-vasthorne]], under the gold, and [[seraphine-vasthorne]] wants
  it.
- Some are in [[harrowmere]]: [[aleid-van-der-haalst]] buys every iron ring that comes to market,
  real or not.
- The rest are lost, or worn by people who do not know what they are.

## Threads

- Why does the House of Salt want them: to keep the knot, or to own it?

velloch.name: Velloch
velloch.summary: One of the three rubies of the Iron Crown of Kell, which held the second river, the one that runs through Hookford in its bed; taken by Sarn, and now, the stories say, with the Iron Hall.
velloch.body:
## The stone

Velloch held the second river, the one that meets the first at [[hookford]]. It is the ruby
[[sarn]] has never quite said is gone. The divers and the pickers believe it is still in
[[the-iron-hall]], somewhere the king could reach. [[corve]] is sitting beside something.

## What it does

Set in one of [[the-nine-irons]], it holds the ring shut, and the ring holds a rope of
[[the-first-knot]]. Out of the iron, the stories disagree. Some say it gives the holder grip on
the river it held. Some say it gives the river grip on the holder.

## Threads

- What happens if it is set back?

ash-breath.name: Ash-Breath
ash-breath.summary: What comes up out of the crack under Greyhollow with every breath it takes: hot, half-shaped, and gone back down on the out-breath if it has not found something to hold.
ash-breath.body:
## What

The crack in the [[the-underhollow]] breathes. On the in-breath the smoke goes down, and the ash
with it. On the out-breath something comes up that is not smoke: heat with a shape to it, closer
kin to the [[seepers]] than anything else, but it has not had time to cool. It burns what it
touches, and it wants to touch something before the crack breathes in again.

## In the world

- [[mardra]] says to count the breaths and walk between them. She does not say what happens to
  those who lose count.

fenmaws.name: Fenmaws
fenmaws.summary: Long, low, armoured things of the Feverfen channels with a human face on the tongue; they lie under the black water and call with the voices of people you have lost.
fenmaws.body:
## What

A Fenmaw is twice a boat's length, mostly jaw, and lies just under the surface of the
[[feverfen]]'s channels. When its mouth opens, there is a face on the tongue, soft and pale, and
it talks. It uses voices it has eaten. Fen-folk children are taught never to answer a voice
from the water, even their mother's.

## Threads

- Do Fenmaws grow the faces, or keep them?

firstcloaks.name: The Firstcloaks
firstcloaks.summary: The order's first men, who guarded the drowned quays of Kell in the grey and never came up; still on duty, still polite, still collecting.
firstcloaks.body:
## What

The [[greycloaks]] began as the men who guarded the drowned quays of [[kell]] in
[[the-ashfall]]. Not all of them were relieved. On the [[quaysteps]] they still stand their
posts, cloaked in grey silt, and they still tithe.

## Voice

"Pardon. A tenth." Pay, and they stand aside. Refuse, and the hook comes out.

## In the world

- The fort at [[wrackhead]] keeps no list of the men it lost in the grey. [[tolm]] has asked
  for one, politely, twice.

hill-knives.name: The Hill-Knives
hill-knives.summary: The drowned of the poor streets of Kell, who went up the hill with knives the night the crown went empty and met the sea coming the other way; they are still going up.
hill-knives.body:
## What

The streets that had nothing went up the hill to the streets that had something. The water
caught them on the way, in the lanes, knife in hand. They are thin and quick and they come in
packs, the way they came that night, and they still go for the door with the bar behind it. The
biggest of them carried the beams and the hammers. The pickers call those Doorbreakers, and run.

## In the world

- Every barred door in the [[lowstreets]] has scratches on the outside, low down. These are the
  hands that made them.

knotrats.name: Knotrats
knotrats.summary: Rats the Kneeling breed to gnaw gallows-ropes and gallows-wood; grey, big as cats, with teeth that never stop growing, and loosed in the night under any gallows the cult wants down.
knotrats.body:
## What

Grey, heavy, and bred for one thing: to chew. A knotrat's teeth grow a finger a month and it must
gnaw or die. [[the-kneeling]] feed them on hemp. Loosed under a gallows, a nest of them will have
the rope down by dawn and the beam by the end of the week.

## In the world

- [[the-ninth-rope]] keep terriers at every gallows of [[hangmoot]], and the terriers are the
  best-fed dogs in the Mark.

lockwardens.name: The Lockwardens
lockwardens.summary: The armoured men who kept the two keys and the two seals of each strongroom door in Kell, drowned at the doors they kept and still keeping them.
lockwardens.body:
## What

Every strongroom door had two locks and a seal on each, and a man to each lock. They were chosen
for not being able to count, so that they could not be bribed with a number. They stand at the
doors in [[strongrooms]] in iron gone white with salt, and when somebody comes through who is not
in the ledger, they put their shoulders down and go through them.

notchers.name: Notchers
notchers.summary: Thin grey shapes in the Brinevaults that cut one notch in the wall for every moment you stand in their sight; at nine, a rope finds your neck.
notchers.body:
## What

Everything owed in the Mark is owed to [[hask]]'s rope, and the [[brinevaults]] are where
Kell kept its accounts. The Notchers keep them still. They do not touch you. They watch, and
cut a notch in the salt for every moment you are in their sight, and they cut slowly, and
there are nine gallows on [[hangmoot]].

At the ninth notch the debt is called. A rope comes down out of the dark, and you are one of
[[the-drawn]].

pickers.name: The Pickers
pickers.summary: Coast folk who went down into Kell before you for what they could carry; the ones still down there have decided you are what they can carry.
pickers.body:
## Who

Since [[the-ebb]] everybody on the coast with a knife and a rope has been down the
[[quaysteps]]. Most come up. Some found a dry room below and stayed, and live off what they
find and what they take from whoever comes after.

## Voice

They do not talk to you. They talk about you, to each other, while you can hear.

qaddir.name: Qaddir
qaddir.summary: Desert reptiles of the Glassands with scales of fused glass, from the length of an arm to the length of a wagon; they hunt by heat, and a sleeping camp is a feast.
qaddir.body:
## What

The Hadd name means *those who listen for warmth*. Qaddir lie under the glass-crust in the
day, cool and still, and come up at night toward anything warm: a fire, a horse, a body. Their
scales are glass, grown from the sand they swallow, and a Qaddir hide is worth a season's water
in [[harrowmere]].

## In the world

- The [[the-hadd]] travel cold. No fires on the glass. The Qaddir are why.
- The big ones live near [[old-vahr]], where the glass is thickest, and are said to be very old.

rimehounds.name: Rimehounds
rimehounds.summary: White wolves of the Rimewold as big as horses, which hunt in packs on the longest night of the year and take whatever is outside a wall.
rimehounds.body:
## What

Rimehounds are wolves the way a glacier is a stream. White, silent, the size of a horse, they
den in the far ice and come south once a year, on the longest night, in packs of a dozen. What
is outside a wall that night is theirs. The [[rimeclans]] bring the herds in, bar the doors, and
sing loud enough not to hear.

## In the world

- A clan-chief's cloak is a Rimehound hide, or it is not a chief's cloak. [[hrok]] has two.
- Since [[brandfell]] split, the packs come further south each winter, and some have been seen
  in [[bonereach]].

sealed-clerks.name: The Sealed Clerks
aliases: the Keepers of the First Ledgers
sealed-clerks.summary: The clerks of Kell who were in the strongrooms when the doors were sealed and the water came; they are still keeping the first ledgers, and they write down whoever comes in.
sealed-clerks.body:
## What

The doors held. The clerks inside did not, but they did not stop working either. They sit at
their desks in the [[strongrooms]] with their pens wet with brine, and when you come in they look
up, and write. What they write down sticks: every line is a notch, as with the [[notchers]] in
the vaults above, only quicker, because the clerks are better at it.

## In the world

- The [[firstcloaks]] say the clerks of Kell were the first of their own kind. The Firstcloaks
  are polite about it.

seepers.name: Seepers
seepers.summary: Things with no fixed shape that seep up through the cracks of deep mines and warm vents like water, and become something on the way; the miners of Irondeep and the smiths of Emberstead hear them before they see them.
seepers.body:
## What

Not [[the-unborn]] themselves. Something that comes off them, the way steam comes off a pot. It
rises through the warm cracks that [[brandfell]] opened, slow as water, and somewhere between
the deep and the light it takes a shape: a hand, a mouth, something the size of a dog with too
many joints. The knocking in the deepest shafts of [[irondeep]] is them.

## In the world

- Fire drives them back. Cold stops them. They are coming up further every year.

the-barred.name: The Barred
the-barred.summary: The drowned of Kell who are still holding their doors shut from the inside; harmless until you open one, and then it is not them you have to worry about.
the-barred.body:
## What

Every door in the [[lowstreets]] is barred, and behind most of them somebody is still
leaning on it. The Barred drowned with their shoulders to the wood. They do not come out.
They do not want you to go in. Open a door anyway and they let go of it, all at once, and
whatever they were keeping out comes past them.

## In the world

- The coast folk say [[vorr]] keeps what the sea takes. The Barred are what he took. What is
  behind the doors he did not.

the-blindkin.name: The Blindkin
the-blindkin.summary: The pale, eyeless people the Ossar bred from men to serve in their temples; a few thousand still live in the dark under the Black Step and the Glassands, tending what sleeps.
the-blindkin.body:
## What

The [[ossar]] did not only eat men. They bred them: for size, for silence, for blindness, so that
servants in the temple would never see what they served. The Blindkin are the result. Pale,
smooth-faced where the eyes should be, hairless, quick in the dark and slow in the light.

## Now

They never left. In the deep of [[the-black-step]] and under the ruins of the [[glassands]] they
still sweep the floors, still tend [[the-stonesleepers]], still wait. [[qarr-dhuun]] diggers meet
them sometimes, and do not come up.

the-drawn.name: The Drawn
the-drawn.summary: The hanged, with the rope still on, pulled through the Brinevaults toward the iron hall by a rope drawn tight from the other end; they do not fight you, they take you with them.
the-drawn.body:
## What

The hangmen of [[hangmoot]] say a rope that went slack forty-one years ago is being drawn
tight. In the [[brinevaults]] you can see what is on the end of it: the hanged, each with a
rope at the neck running off toward the hall, each moving along it whether it wants to or
not, the way a debt moves toward the one it is owed.

They do not attack. They hold on. Whatever a Drawn takes hold of goes where the rope goes.

the-long-back.name: The Long Back
the-long-back.summary: The thing that has begun to surface in the shallows where the sea has gone out from the Gallowmark coast; only its back has been seen, black and barnacled and a mile long, and the coast says it is what Vorr kept down.
the-long-back.body:
## What

Since [[the-ebb]], on still mornings, the fishers of [[drownhaven]] and [[ebbmouth]] have seen a
black ridge in the shallows that was not there before: barnacled, ridged, a mile long. It is
there one day and gone the next, somewhere else. Twice it has moved while boats were near it, and
the boats did not come back.

## What the coast says

That [[vorr]] keeps what the sea takes, and he took this a long time ago and kept it down. That
the sea going out is letting it up. That it is waiting for the water to go out far enough.

the-paid.name: The Paid
the-paid.summary: Sorcerers and their victims who have paid all three coins to the Unborn, body, memory and soul; they still walk, they still obey, and what obeys is not them.
the-paid.body:
## What

Every pact with [[the-unborn]] is paid in three coins, in order: body, memory, soul. The Paid
have given the third. They look like people, mostly. They do not eat, sleep or remember. They
do what something below tells them, slowly and without stopping.

## In the world

- Sorcerer-kings of the [[glassands]] keep them as guards. [[qeth-ummar]] has a hall full.
- [[the-kneeling]] call them *the finished*, and envy them.
- Hangmen burn them, because a rope does not hold what has no breath to stop.

the-standing.name: The Standing
aliases: the King's Iron, the Salt Guard
the-standing.summary: The household guard of the last king of Kell, drowned at their posts in full iron and still standing in their ranks in the hall; they do not move while the king sits, and they move when you touch what is his.
the-standing.body:
## What

When the sea came in over [[kell]] the king did not leave his chair, and the men sworn to
stand by it did not leave their posts. They are still there: two ranks down the length of
[[the-iron-hall]], salt grown white over the iron, faces gone, spears grounded.

They do not stop you walking between them. They do not stop you looking. Lay a hand on the
crown, the coin under the throne, or anything else that was the king's, and every one of
them turns at once.

## In the world

- The divers of [[wrackhead]] say the coast's oldest oath was sworn by these men: *until the
  king stands*. He has not stood.
- [[gorvek]] went between them and came out with a sack. Nobody knows whether he touched the
  crown, or what he touched instead.

the-stonesleepers.name: The Stonesleepers
the-stonesleepers.summary: The Ossar who went into the stone instead of under the earth when the knot was tied, and sleep there under the Glassands and the Feverfen; they are waking one at a time, over centuries, and the Kneeling call them the Buried Masters.
the-stonesleepers.body:
## What

Not every [[ossar]] went under the earth with their masters. Some lay down in the stone of their
temples, in niches cut to fit, and slept. The knot holds them too, but less. They lie under
[[the-black-step]] and the black foundations of the [[glassands]], tended by [[the-blindkin]].

## The waking

Since [[brandfell]] split, the niches have begun to empty. One in the time of [[the-burning-of-ossery]].
Three in the last generation. [[the-kneeling]] have a word for each one that wakes. The
building on [[smokemouth]] is in their pattern.

the-taken-in-lieu.name: The Taken in Lieu
the-taken-in-lieu.summary: What the clerks of Kell took in lieu of payment and kept in the strongrooms: people, mostly, sons and daughters pledged against a debt; still kept, still pulling toward whoever holds the paper.
the-taken-in-lieu.body:
## What

When a debt could not be paid in coin the clerks of Kell took something else, and wrote it in
the ledger, and kept it in the [[strongrooms]] until the debt was paid. The debts were never paid.
They are thin and grey and still tied with the clerks' tape at the wrist, and they do not fight
so much as hold on, the way the [[the-drawn]] hold on, and pull you to the desk to be written down.

the-unasked.name: The Unasked
the-unasked.summary: The drowned of the Lowstreets who did not stay drowned, and ate the ones who did; nobody asked them what they ate, and they can smell hunger on you.
the-unasked.body:
## What

The elders of [[bonereach]] do not ask a returning warrior where he has been. Nobody asked
the drowned of the [[lowstreets]] either. They went under with their doors barred, and some
of them did not stay under. Forty years in the dark with nothing to eat but the others.
They are thin. They are quick. They come for the hungry first.

## In the world

- The pickers say they have met people they knew, who went down too often and too hungry.

the-walled.name: The Walled
the-walled.summary: The people of the Lowstreets who bricked themselves into their back rooms with what they meant to keep, and after forty years in the packing have begun to come out through the wall.
the-walled.body:
## What

The [[bricked-rooms]] were shut from the inside, and the packing filled every crack. Some of them
are open now. Not broken in: pushed out, a brick at a time, from the back. The ones who did it
are grey with mortar and still have the silver in their hands. They do not run. They wait in the
next room with their backs to the wall, the way they waited the first time, and when you come in
they close the door behind you.

## In the world

- The pickers of [[drykell]] mark a wall that has a fresh hole in it, and go round.

## Threads

- What did they eat, in there, for forty years?

wrack.name: Your Wrack
wrack.summary: What the sea gives back of those who went down into Kell and did not come up, yours among them; each holds the ground it fell on and what it carried, and does not remember losing it.
wrack.body:
## What

Wrack is what the sea throws back onto the shingle at [[wrackhead]]: weed, spars, a boot. In
[[kell]] the sea throws back the ones who went down and stayed. Each comes up again where it
fell, holding what it held, standing on the ground the ledger last counted for it.

Yours come up too. Every time you went down and did not come back, something with your name
and your gear stayed on the floor where you fell, and it holds that ground now. It does not
know you. It is old ground, and it is yours, and it is still not good.

## Threads

- Does the ledger count your wrack as you, or as someone else who held the same ground?

ashday.name: Ashday
aliases: the Day the Sky Came Back
ashday.summary: The day the Mark keeps for the clearing of the Ashfall, year zero of every calendar; an ash cross on the forehead, silence until noon, and drink until there is none.
ashday.body:
## The day

At dawn on Ashday every household in [[gallowmark]] takes a handful of old ash and marks a cross on
each forehead. Nobody speaks until noon. At noon someone says the names of the dead of the grey,
as many as anyone remembers, and then the drinking starts, and lasts.

## Custom

The Ashborn do not mark their foreheads. They say they carry enough.

food-and-drink.name: Food and Drink of Harth
food-and-drink.summary: What people eat and drink across Harth: ash-bread in the Mark, mulled wine in Crownhold, eel pie in Harrowmere, cactus spirit on the glass, fish and fever-bark in the fen, and blood-mead in the north.
food-and-drink.body:
## The Mark

Ash-bread, baked dark and heavy from rye grown in ash-soil; turnips, mutton, sour ale. On
[[ashday]], nothing until noon.

## The Rimewold

Smoked fish, seal fat, horse when a horse dies, and blood-mead, thick and red, drunk from horns at
[[the-icething]].

## Crownhold

Wheat bread, wine, mulled with spice at court and with nothing in the provinces. Peacock at
banquets, and poison at the same banquets, so the court eats slowly.

## Harrowmere

Eel pie from the black lake, pickled herring, gin. The princes eat plainly and drink nothing.

## The Glassands

Dates, goat, flatbread baked on hot stone, and qasr, a clear spirit pressed from the glass-cactus,
that the [[the-hadd]] drink only at dawn when the walking is over.

## The Feverfen

Fish, reed-root, and fever-bark tea from [[the-leech-mothers]], bitter enough to stop the shakes.

helions-crown.name: Helion's Crown
helions-crown.summary: The great feast of the Sunward Faith on the longest day, when Helion Castor stands highest and the church says the dark below is weakest; gold, processions, and the year's tithes carried to the cathedral.
helions-crown.body:
## The feast

On the longest day of the year the domes of [[crownhold]] are uncovered to the sun, the Exarch
[[hadrian-mournevale]] crowns the king anew in light, and every temple carries its tithe in
procession to the capital. It is the richest day of the church's year by a wide margin.

knotnight.name: Knotnight
knotnight.summary: The night each year when the hangmen of Hangmoot tighten the ropes and the north keeps the gallows-feast; the south has forgotten why, and celebrates it anyway.
knotnight.body:
## The night

On the anniversary the hangmen keep for [[the-first-knot]], [[the-ninth-rope]] climbs all nine
gallows of [[hangmoot]] and tightens every knot by hand. In the Mark, every village with a gallows
does the same, and then drinks under it until dawn. Debts are paid on Knotnight, oaths sworn, and
the last unpaid debt of the year is hanged.

## Elsewhere

In [[crownhold]] and [[harrowmere]] Knotnight is a night of masks and rope-games whose meaning nobody
remembers. [[the-kneeling]] remember. They cut a rope somewhere every Knotnight.

law-in-harth.name: Law in Harth
law-in-harth.summary: How justice is done across Harth: the gallows and the rope-oath in the Mark, the king's courts and the poison-cup in Crownhold, Stillwater and the schuldbrief in Harrowmere, water-debts on the glass, and the captain's mast in the Teeth.
law-in-harth.body:
## The Mark

The [[the-ninth-rope]] and the Reeve's moot at [[hangmoot]]: what can be paid is paid, what cannot
is hanged or forgiven. The [[greycloaks]] tithe in between, and call it law.

## Crownhold

The king's courts, for those who can pay the judges. For those who cannot, the magistrates. For
nobles, the poison-cup, offered politely and drunk the same way.

## Harrowmere

Everything is a debt. A crime is a debt to the injured, written as a [[schuldbrieven]] and sold.
Those who cannot pay go to [[stillwater]].

## The Glassands

Blood is paid in water, weighed against the dead, as in [[ush-kaddah]]. Outside the city, a
[[the-well-kings]] judges, and the judgment is usually thirst.

## The Teeth

The Captain's Oath, and the mast.

pactmarks.name: Pactmarks
pactmarks.summary: The marks every pact with the Unborn leaves on the body that paid for it: black veins, glass in the skin, an eye that does not blink; anyone who knows how can read what a sorcerer has paid.
pactmarks.body:
## What they are

The first coin of every pact is the body, and the body keeps the receipt. A small asking leaves
a small mark: a vein gone black under the wrist, a nail turned to horn. A great one leaves a
great one: skin that is glass in patches, like [[qeth-ummar]]'s; a voice that comes from slightly
behind the mouth; an eye that no longer blinks or weeps.

## Reading them

Physicians, [[the-leech-mothers]] and [[the-ninth-rope]] can read pactmarks the way a clerk reads
a ledger: how many askings, how large, and how close the second coin is. Sorcerers cover them
with gloves, veils and paint. [[mardra]] does not, and her marks are fewer than they should be.

## Threads

- Can a pactmark be cut out, and does the debt go with it?

rope-oaths.name: Rope-oaths
rope-oaths.summary: Oaths sworn with a hand on one of Hask's ropes, which bind in earnest: the oath-breaker does not die at once, but begins to, and goes on dying until the oath is kept or the rope is done.
rope-oaths.body:
## The oath

Put your hand on a hangman's rope, say what you will do, and the [[the-ninth-rope]] will tie a
knot in it and keep it. That is a rope-oath. It is the oldest law in Harth and the only one
nobody can buy out of, not even in [[harrowmere]].

## Breaking it

The oath-breaker feels the rope at once: a tightness at the throat that does not go away. Each day
it is worse. Breath shortens, the face darkens, the voice goes. Keep the oath, late, and it
loosens. Do not, and in a season or a year the rope finishes what it began.

## Custom

Kings swear rope-oaths at their crowning, captains at their hiring, reavers on [[the-teeth]] by
the Captain's Oath, which is the same thing with a mast for a gallows.

sayings-of-harth.name: Sayings of Harth
sayings-of-harth.summary: The oaths, curses and sayings of the lands of Harth, from By the Ashfall in the Mark to She has him among the free companies.
sayings-of-harth.body:
## Gallowmark

- *By the Ashfall.* The oath of the Ashborn, never by a god.
- *The rope remembers.* A debt is never forgotten.
- *What do you want?* The question the Reach asks instead of where you have been.

## The free companies

- *She has him.* Said of the dead, for [[nevermourn]].
- *Weep later, and pay the fine.*

## Crownhold

- *Under the gold, the iron.* Everything fine hides something hard.
- *Helion sees.* Said piously, and as a threat.

## Harrowmere

- *Clasped hands, open purse.*
- *Everyone owes. The question is whom.*

## The Glassands

- *Walk at night, drink at dawn.*
- *Sun-fool.* The worst thing a Hadd can call you.

## The Rimewold

- *Behind me stand —* followed by a number. A boast, and an argument.
- *Bar the door.* Goodbye, on the Longnight.

schuldbrieven.name: Schuldbrieven
schuldbrieven.summary: The debt-letters of Harrowmere, traded like coin, inherited like land and sworn on Hask's rope; the whole of Harth runs on them, and a man can be hanged on one he never signed.
schuldbrieven.body:
## The letters

A schuldbrief is a debt written down: who owes, whom, how much, by when, sealed by a Harrowmere
house and sworn with a hand on a hangman's rope. Once written it can be sold, and most are, many
times. The debtor owes whoever holds the paper. Most debtors do not know who that is.

## Inheriting

Debts pass to heirs in Harth, and so do schuldbrieven. A child can be born owing. [[stillwater]]
is full of people who never signed what put them there.

## The rope

Because they are sworn as [[rope-oaths]], a schuldbrief that goes unpaid tightens. The hangmen
say every one paid pulls the knot of [[the-first-knot]] a little tighter, which is why
[[the-ninth-rope]] defends Harrowmere's debts and despises Harrowmere. The [[the-burning-of-the-rolls]]
burns schuldbrieven, and the hangmen are afraid of what that does.

the-count.name: The Count
the-count.summary: The system of the Counted Lands: every person has a number from birth, tattooed on the wrist; the number decides their work, their marriage, and the year they are taken, and the people are grateful for it.
the-count.body:
## The number

In [[the-counted-lands]] every child is numbered at birth, the number pricked into the inside of
the wrist. The number decides what work you do, whom you may marry, and when your number comes up.
When it does, you are taken, quietly, in the night, and your house is given to the next number.

## The happiness

Nobody starves in the Counted Lands. Nobody is sick, nobody is at war, nobody is afraid of anything
but their number, and most are not afraid of that. They say the [[ossar]] care for them. The
[[the-numbered-man]] said that was the worst of it.

the-harrowmere-mark.name: The Harrowmere Mark
the-harrowmere-mark.summary: The silver coin of Harrowmere, struck by the House of Salt with a handshake on the reverse; the only coin taken everywhere in Harth, and trusted nowhere.
the-harrowmere-mark.body:
## The coin

A thin silver disc, a ship on the face, two hands clasped on the back, and the mint-mark of the
House of Salt on the rim. Every kingdom of Harth strikes its own coin. Every kingdom of Harth
prices in marks.

## The trust

Nobody trusts it. Each house of [[the-gilded]] shaves the silver a little when it suits them, and
the weight of a mark has fallen every generation since [[the-fall-of-vahr]]. People take it
anyway, because the alternative is to be paid in something worse, and in Harth the something worse
is [[schuldbrieven]].

## Sayings

- *Clasped hands, open purse.*
- *A mark is a promise from a liar, and the liar is rich.*

the-longnight.name: The Longnight
the-longnight.summary: The longest night of the year: in the north the Rimehounds hunt and every clan bars its doors and sings; in the cities of the south the Kneeling keep their highest night in secret.
the-longnight.body:
## In the north

The [[rimehounds]] come south out of the ice on the Longnight, and what is outside a wall is
theirs. The clans bring in the herds, bar the doors, and sing as loud as they can until dawn. In
[[bonereach]] and lately in the rest of the Mark, they do the same.

## In the south

The [[the-kneeling]] hold that the Longnight is when the dark below is nearest, and kneel all
night, every cell in Harth at once. The Sunward call it the night of the enemy. The hangmen hunt.

the-low-imperial.name: The Low Imperial
the-low-imperial.summary: The common tongue of Harth, descended from the speech of Vahr along its roads; everyone speaks some of it, and only priests and sorcerers can read the High Imperial it came from.
the-low-imperial.body:
## The tongue

When [[old-vahr]] fell its language broke like everything else, but its roads kept a version of it
alive: the Low Imperial, the speech of milestones, markets and armies. It is the tongue of trade in
[[harrowmere]], of law in [[crownhold]], and of every free company.

## The others

Every land keeps its own tongue beside it: the hard northern speech of the Mark and the Rimewold,
the courtly Low Imperial of Crownhold, the merchant-speech of Harrowmere, the Hadd tongue of the
glass, the water-speech of the fen. The High Imperial survives only in temples and in
[[the-hungry-books]].

truenaming.name: Truenaming
truenaming.summary: The river-priests' art, older than pacts: to name a thing truly is to take a grip on it; it costs no soul, only a piece of the namer's own name, and an old river-priest has almost none left.
truenaming.body:
## The art

The [[river-priests]] hold that every thing has a true name, under the one people call it, and
that the true name is a handle. Say it, and you have hold. A flood named truly goes down a
finger, as the river went down under [[vell]]'s feet. A man named truly does what he was going
to do anyway, but cannot stop.

## The cost

Truenaming is not a pact. Nothing below is asked. The price is paid in the namer's own name: each
true name given takes a little of the giver's. Young priests have long names. Brother [[ruun]] is
called by one syllable, and some days he does not answer to it.

## Threads

- What happens to a priest who gives the last of their name?

war-in-harth.name: War in Harth
war-in-harth.summary: How Harth fights: free companies hired by the season, holdfasts and gates that decide everything, sorcerers bought at the Hiring who poison both sides, and armoured horse against the riders of the Grass Sea.
war-in-harth.body:
## Free companies

No king of Harth can afford an army. They keep a guard and buy the rest: free companies like
[[the-unmourned]], hired at [[fordham]], [[harrowmere]] or the camp-fairs of [[crownhold]], paid
in [[the-harrowmere-mark]] or in plunder. A company fights for its contract, swears a
[[rope-oaths]] on it, and worships [[nevermourn]].

## Gates and walls

Harth is a land of walls: Vahrish fortresses, river cities, the holdfasts of the Mark. Battles are
rare. Sieges are not. Whoever holds the gates holds the land, which is why every side wants the
[[greycloaks]] and nobody trusts them.

## Sorcerers in war

A sorcerer bought at [[the-hiring-of-the-wise]] can sour a well, send a fever, turn a river, make
an army forget its orders. Every asking costs the sorcerer, and it costs the land: a field
poisoned by sorcery stays poisoned. Captains hire them anyway, and hang them after if they can.

## Horse

Crownhold's armoured knights are the heaviest horse in Harth and were built for one enemy: the
[[the-hoofborn]] of [[the-grass-sea]], who fight from the saddle with the bow and never charge.
Sixty years ago the knights lost.

gorveks-last-road.name: Gorvek's Last Road
gorveks-last-road.summary: The winter Gorvek of Bonereach rode north through the Wallgate and past Brandfell into the Rimewold, with two horses from Hrok's hall and the sack from Kell, and was never seen again.
gorveks-last-road.body:
## The road

Thirty-one years after the ash cleared, [[gorvek]] came through the [[wallgate]] going north.
[[tolm]] was in the door, old, and asked him for a tenth, and Gorvek put something in his
hand, and Tolm let him through and never said what it was. He came to [[hrok]]'s hall, asked
for a horse, got two, and rode north past [[brandfell]] into the white.

He had the sack from [[kell]] with him. Nobody saw what was in it.

## After

Nobody saw him again. That has not stopped anyone. The Reach says he went to finish
something. The [[rimeclans]] say he walked into the ice. The [[the-kneeling]] say he went to
cut Hask down. Every bastard line in the north says it is his, and some of them may be right.

## Threads

- What was in the sack?
- Is he still out there?

the-ashfall.name: The Ashfall
the-ashfall.summary: The ash that came down over the north of Gallowmark when Brandfell split open, and darkened the sky for a generation; the year it cleared is year zero of every calendar in the Mark.
the-ashfall.body:
## What fell

Ten years after [[kell]] went under, [[brandfell]] split open in the Wallmountains, and the
fire in it came out. The sky over the north of [[gallowmark]] went black. Then the ash came
down: hot at first, burning thatch and birch and the people who could not get under stone,
then cold and grey and endless, a finger deep, a hand deep, to the knee. It fell on
[[bonereach]] first and hardest, and it stayed a generation. The sun was a coin behind it.
Nothing grew. Inside the dark people did what people do when nobody can see them.

The rivers carried it south. For thirty years the grey rivers ran grey in earnest, and laid
the ash down on the sea floor over drowned Kell, which is why the silt on the
[[quaysteps]] is not sand.

## What came out

When the sky cleared, the ones who walked out of the north were called the Ashborn.
[[gorvek]] is one. The [[greycloaks]] are, in a sense, another: the order was born guarding
the drowned quays of [[kell]], took the north in the dark years while nobody could see it
happen, and never took the cloak off.

## The calendar

The Mark counts its years from the clearing. Everything before is *in the grey*, and nobody
is precise about it.

## Threads

- Why did Brandfell split, ten years to the season after the stones were taken?

the-broken-years.name: The Broken Years
the-broken-years.summary: The thousand years after the fall of Vahr, when kingdoms rose and fell across Harth, plagues walked the roads, peoples wandered, and the Greycloaks learned to be everywhere without ruling anywhere.
the-broken-years.body:
## What happened

Everything, and none of it for long. A hundred kingdoms claimed the empire and ninety-eight
fell. [[crownhold]] lasted. [[harrowmere]] bought the debts. The Red Cough emptied the river
cities twice. The [[the-hoofborn]] came off [[the-grass-sea]] four times. [[the-kneeling]] took
a city and the hangmen burned it: [[the-burning-of-ossery]].

## What it made

The Harth of now: kingdoms that remember an empire, an order in grey that holds every gate, a
city that owns everyone's debt, and a knot that nobody but the hangmen remembers is there.

the-burning-of-ossery.name: The Burning of Ossery
the-burning-of-ossery.summary: The war in which the Kneeling took the city of Ossery and opened something under it, and the hangmen and the kings of the Broken Years burned the city with everyone in it to close it again.
the-burning-of-ossery.body:
## The war

For a generation the Kneeling had been in Ossery's cellars. Then they were in its council, and then
its gates closed. What happened inside for the next year nobody wrote down. The river below the city
ran warm.

## The burning

[[the-ninth-rope]] came south with every hangman in Harth, and three kings came with their armies,
and they did not besiege Ossery. They burned it, all of it, with everyone inside, and hanged anyone
who came out. The hangmen say the knot was tighter afterward. The kings did not ask how.

the-burning-of-the-rolls.name: The Burning of the Rolls
the-burning-of-the-rolls.summary: The peasant rising of Crownhold's hungry provinces under the one-armed prophet Quintus Ashhand, who burn the tax-rolls and the Greycloak houses and refuse the tenth.
the-burning-of-the-rolls.body:
## The rising

It started in a single village, when [[quintus-ashhand]] put the tax-rolls into the chapel
fire. Now it is nine provinces. The rebels march from village to village, open the granaries,
burn every list of who owes what, and pull down the [[greycloaks]]' chapterhouses stone by
stone.

## Why it frightens everyone

Not the peasants. The lists. In Harth a debt is a rope, and a rope is the knot, and the
hangmen of [[hangmoot]] have sent word south that every roll burned loosens it. The
[[the-kneeling]] have sent word too. They are delighted.

## Threads

- Who is paying for the rebels' iron?

the-drowning-of-kell.name: The Drowning of Kell
the-drowning-of-kell.summary: The night Sarn took the three rubies from the Iron Crown and Kell went under by morning; forty years before the Ashfall lifted, and the reason there are Greycloaks.
the-drowning-of-kell.body:
## The night

[[sarn]] entered the iron-roofed hall of [[kell]], took the three rubies from the
[[iron-crown-of-kell]], and was gone. Nobody saw a face. By morning the grey rivers had left
their beds and the quays were under water.

## What it made

The guards of the drowned quays became the [[greycloaks]]. The river-priests of [[thurn]]
gave Sarn the name Lord of Streams that same year, as a warning. And the Mark learned the
lesson it has lived by since: a thing held in place by belief is held in place by nothing.

the-ebb.name: The Ebb
the-ebb.summary: The first winter after the grey lifted, the sea began to go out from Old Kell and has not come back; the drowned quays are showing, every power in the Mark is moving toward the coast, and three gods have been given the credit.
the-ebb.body:
## What is happening

In the first winter after the grey lifted, the sea went out from Old [[kell]] on the low
tide and did not come all the way back. Every month since, it has gone a little further. The
quay-stones of the drowned city are showing below [[wrackhead]]. On a still day the iron
roof of the hall stands clear of the water for an hour. Nobody has walked to it yet.
Everybody is going to.

## Three gods, one name

[[vell]] named it the Ebb before the coast had noticed, and the [[river-priests]] say
[[thurn]] is calling the rivers home to their beds. The coast folk say [[vorr]] is opening
his mouth to give something back. The hangmen of [[hangmoot]] say a rope that went slack
forty-one years ago is being drawn tight from the other end, and that [[hask]] does not draw
a rope for nothing. All three are pointing at the same iron hall and the three empty sockets
in it.

## Who is moving

- The [[greycloaks]] said for forty years they would raise Kell. The sea is doing it for
  them. They have doubled the fort at Wrackhead and sent [[tolm]] south from the
  [[wallgate]] for the first time since the grey.
- [[gorvek]] was on the coast before anyone, and went down first, for the crown.
- [[mardra]] has begun selling things she says came up out of Kell, and says the floor of
  the hall is warm.
- [[rauk]] has stopped diving, and [[brim]] walks to the waterline every morning.
- [[sarn]] narrates. Sarn always did. Sarn has started narrating this.

## What it binds

Every gallows, every river, every fort and every debt in the Mark is drawn tight toward one
iron hall standing up out of the salt. The [[iron-crown-of-kell]] held the world together by
being believed in. The sea is about to show everyone whether it is still there.

## Threads

- How far out does the sea go?
- What is at the low-water mark when it stops?
- Why is the shingle at Wrackhead warm to bare feet, this winter, for the first time?

the-fall-of-vahr.name: The Fall of Vahr
the-fall-of-vahr.summary: The end of the empire of Vahr a thousand years before Kell drowned, when its sorcerer-emperors asked the Unborn for one thing too many; the heartland burned to glass, and the empire broke into the kingdoms of Harth.
the-fall-of-vahr.body:
## The empire

Vahr was the first thing men built that the [[ossar]] had not. It ran from the ice to the
fens, it wore iron crowns because iron was the metal of the knot, and for a thousand years it
kept the oath and hanged its debtors on Hask's pattern. Then it began to use what the Ossar
had taught.

## The asking

The emperors of [[old-vahr]] asked [[the-unborn]] for victories, and got them; for long
lives, and got them; and at the last, for an empire that would never end. Something gave
it to them. The heartland burned in one night, white, and the sand around the capital ran
like water and set like glass. That is the [[glassands]].

## What was left

The provinces woke up without an emperor and became kingdoms: [[crownhold]], which says it
is Vahr's heir; [[harrowmere]], which bought the empire's debts and calls that the same
thing; the cities of the coast, of which [[kell]] kept the ninth of [[the-nine-irons]]. The rest of the
[[harth]] is what happens when nobody holds a land for a thousand years.

## Threads

- Did the emperors die, or did they get what they asked for?

the-first-knot.name: The First Knot
the-first-knot.summary: The oath by which the first men bound the Ossar and the Unborn under the earth: they hanged their own god on the ninth gallows of a northern ridge, so that the rope would hold for as long as a god can hang.
the-first-knot.body:
## The rope

The first men had one god of their own, the god of oaths, and they had lost every war
against the [[ossar]]. So they swore the one oath that could not be broken, and they made a
god hold it: they built nine gallows on the ridge that is now [[hangmoot]] and hanged
[[hask]] on the ninth. A hanged god does not die. He hangs, and the oath hangs with him, and
what it binds stays bound. The Ossar and their masters went under.

## The ropes and the ring

The hangmen say the binding is nine ropes and nine iron rings, [[the-nine-irons]], one to hold each
rope shut, and that the rings were carried south and worn by emperors and kings. The ninth was set
with stones and became the [[iron-crown-of-kell]]. The
crown held the rivers in their beds because it held a great deal more than rivers.

## What it is held with

- [[rope-oaths]], sworn on the ropes, which bind in earnest.
- [[the-nine-irons]], the rings.
- [[the-ninth-rope]], the hangmen who keep it.

## Why the Mark is the Mark

Everything owed in [[gallowmark]] is owed to the rope, because every debt paid at Hask's
gallows pulls the knot a little tighter. The Mark is not a borderland by accident. It is
the place where the world is tied shut.

## Threads

- What did the first men promise Hask for hanging?
- Who is meant to cut him down, and when?

the-fraying.name: The Fraying
the-fraying.summary: The age that began in year nine, when Seraphine Vasthorne broke her dead father's iron ring and a rope snapped on Hangmoot; the Ossar woke in the Feverfen and the south of the Glassands, those lands were lost, and Harth has been fighting to hold the rest ever since.
the-fraying.body:
## The night

[[aurelian-vasthorne]] died in the sixth winter after the ash cleared, and [[the-three-crowns]]
were crowned in three cities. In the ninth, [[seraphine-vasthorne]], crowned by the chapel, took
her father's circlet, one of [[the-nine-irons]], down into the cellars of [[solmerine]] and broke it
on the floor where she knelt. On [[hangmoot]], that same night, a rope snapped. [[haldis-graymane]]
heard it from her bed.

## What woke

In the [[feverfen]] the lights on [[the-black-step]] burned all night, and in the morning the
[[the-stonesleepers]] were walking. In the south of the [[glassands]] the foundations under the
ruins opened. Within a year both lands were lost: their people fled, were taken, or were counted.
[[smokemouth]] finished what was being built on it.

## After

The Sunward church that crowned Seraphine burned her in the cathedral square of what became
[[the-sunward-see]], and kept her throne. The other ropes held. They have held, barely, for a
hundred and forty years.

## A hundred and fifty years on

This is the Harth of the year 150:

- Crownhold is three kingdoms at war with each other: [[realm-of-solmerine]], [[the-sunward-see]]
  and [[the-halberd-march]]. Its east is [[the-saddle-throne]] of the Hoofborn.
- The Feverfen and the south of the Glassands are Ossar country. The front is a line of forts,
  ruins and burned villages, and nobody holds it for long.
- [[the-ninth-rope]] holds Hangmoot with eight ropes, and hunts.
- The [[greycloaks]] hold every gate, still, politely. They have never shut one.
- [[harrowmere]] is richer than ever. Everyone owes it for the war.
- The Brink runs along the edge of what was lost: [[the-brink]].
- The Mark is still a borderland, forgotten and hard: the Greycloaks rule, the Holdfast Lords fight,
  and few beyond the hangmen know how much it matters.
- Kell is dry, and [[drykell]] has grown up in it. Brim is alive, they say, somewhere on the coast,
  and anyone might be the salt-king.
- The Rimewold is as it was: clans, ice, and war.
- [[the-tenth-palace]] has a door, and [[the-tenth-prince]] sits openly with the Gilded.
- Ishara Grey still reads the books. Nobody knows what she is.
- Gorvek is a legend. Hookbreakers hang in every hall.

## Threads

- How long can eight ropes hold what nine held?
- Who will try to cut the next one, and who will try to tie the ninth again?

the-going-home.name: The Going Home
the-going-home.summary: What the descent shows and nobody in the Mark says: the grey came up out of Kell, and it is going back down, and it is drawing the sea after it.
the-going-home.body:
## Retired

This was the truth behind the descent until the canon was repaired: the grey as something
that came up out of Kell and went home down a drain. The Ashfall is fire and ash from
[[brandfell]], and the Ebb is [[the-heave]]. Kept so the old lines can be traced; do not
write from it.

## What was written

This entry is the truth behind the descent, for the people who write it. No character in
the Mark says it, and no line in the game states it. The player reads it in what they find.

When [[sarn]] took the stones, the three rivers left their beds, the sea came in over
[[kell]], and the place under the iron hall where the one river ends was opened. The grey
came up out of it, through the water, and climbed the rivers against the current to where
they rise beyond the [[wallgate]]. It came down over the north from there, and so the north
has always believed it came from the north. That was [[the-ashfall]].

When it lifted it did not go away. It went home, down the rivers, into the drain under the
hall, and it is drawing the sea after it. That is [[the-ebb]]. [[thurn]] calling the rivers
home, [[vorr]] opening his mouth, [[hask]]'s rope drawn tight: all three are right, and none
of them is the reason. [[greyhollow]] is the part that never made it home, and it rises when
the sea goes out because it is the same body.

[[vell]] told [[gorvek]] what he carries: the one thing that can tell a stream to stop. He
went down before anyone, and he is standing in the drain with [[streamlord]], holding it.

## What the player learns, tier by tier

1. [[quaysteps]]: ash in the silt; the order's first men, dead in the grey, still on duty.
2. [[lowstreets]]: the doors were barred against the grey, not the water.
3. [[brinevaults]]: the clerks counted the days of the grey; a fall of water stands still.
4. [[the-iron-hall]]: the grey at home, and Gorvek in the drain, and his line in the ledger.

## Threads

- How long can he hold it?
- When the sea is all the way out, does the grey come up again?

the-heave.name: The Heave
the-heave.summary: What the descent shows and nobody in the Mark says: the fire that broke Brandfell and made the Ashfall is still under the Mark, and it is lifting the land; the sea is not going out, the coast is coming up.
the-heave.body:
## What is true

This entry is the truth behind the descent, for the people who write it. No character in
the Mark says it plainly, and no line in the game states it. The player reads it in what
they find.

Ten years after [[sarn]] took the stones and [[kell]] went under, the mountain the Reach
calls [[brandfell]] split open north of the [[wallgate]], and ash came down over the north
for a generation. That was [[the-ashfall]]. It was fire, and fire does not go away when the
sky clears. It went under.

It runs under the whole Mark now, from Brandfell to the coast, close under [[greyhollow]]
where the ash never cooled, and closest of all under [[kell]]. It is lifting the ground the
way a loaf lifts in the oven. The sea is not going out. The coast is coming up out of it.
That is [[the-ebb]]. [[thurn]] calling the rivers home, [[vorr]] opening his mouth, [[hask]]'s
rope drawn tight: all three are given the credit, and none of them is the reason.

## What the fire is

[[mardra]] says the fire under the Mark is not a fire. It is [[the-unborn]], turning over in
their sleep, because the knot is looser than it was. She charges a great deal for saying so,
and she does not ask anyone to believe her.

## Why the iron is warm

[[rauk]] touched the crown and said the iron was warm. The first river runs warm one night
each winter at the Wallgate. The floor of [[the-iron-hall]] is warm under the salt. Every
one of them is the same fire, nearer the top than anyone has guessed.

## Why everyone goes down

Not for the truth. For what Kell had: the coin in the [[brinevaults]], the goods in the
[[bonded-stores]], the silver in the [[bricked-rooms]], the empty [[iron-crown-of-kell]] on
a dead king's head, and the rumour, which Sarn has never denied, that one of the three rubies
never left the hall. The ledger names whoever holds the most of it. That is the whole
descent: a drowned city, uncovered, and everyone in the Mark with a rope and a knife.

## What the player learns, tier by tier

1. [[quaysteps]]: ash in the silt that the rivers carried down; the order's first men, dead
   at their posts, still on duty.
2. [[lowstreets]]: the doors were barred against the city, not the water.
3. [[brinevaults]]: the clerks shut themselves in with the coin and counted the days.
4. [[the-iron-hall]]: the king, his guard still standing, a warm floor, and the stair he
   walled up behind him.

## Threads

- When the coast is all the way up, does the fire come up with it?
- Did Sarn know about the mountain when Sarn took the stones?

the-hiring-of-the-wise.name: The Hiring of the Wise
the-hiring-of-the-wise.summary: The yearly auction in Harrowmere where sorcerers are hired out for a year to the highest bidder; the greatest festival in the city, with masks, fire on the water, and everyone knowing exactly what is being sold.
the-hiring-of-the-wise.body:
## The auction

Once a year, at midwinter, the sorcerers of Harth who will work for coin come to
[[harrowmere]] and stand on the Stairs of Weighing in white masks, and the princes, kings and
captains of Harth bid for a year of each. The bidding is in the open. The contracts are not.

## The festival

The whole city goes masked. There is fire on the canals and music on every bridge, and the
[[the-honest-company-of-takers]] work all night with the city's blessing. It is also the night
the barges go to [[the-tenth-palace]].

## Threads

- Which sorcerer has never been outbid, and who keeps hiring them?

the-icething.name: The Icething
the-icething.summary: The gathering of every clan of the Rimewold on a frozen lake once in seven years, to fight, marry, divorce and settle feuds; the one place in the north where no clan kills another.
the-icething.body:
## The moot

Every seventh winter the [[rimeclans]] walk out onto the great frozen lake of the middle
Rimewold and pitch their tents on the ice. For nine days nobody may draw blood except in the
ring. Feuds are fought out with fists and axe-hafts, marriages made, marriages broken, chiefs
counted by who stands behind them. [[hrok]] has been counted the longest line at five
Icethings running.

## The law of the ice

Blood on the ice outside the ring breaks the truce, and the clan that broke it is put off the
lake into the night with the [[rimehounds]]. It has happened twice in living memory.

## Threads

- Will [[clan-skoll]] come to the next Icething, and will anyone let them onto the ice?

the-long-peace-of-vahr.name: The Long Peace of Vahr
the-long-peace-of-vahr.summary: The thousand years when the empire of Vahr held Harth from the ice to the fens: roads, iron law, the Tenth Legion at every gate, and the emperors keeping the knot until they began to ask.
the-long-peace-of-vahr.body:
## The peace

Not peace: quiet. The emperors of [[old-vahr]] held Harth with roads, law and iron. Every debt was
written, every oath sworn on the rope, every gate held by [[the-tenth-legion]]. The roads are still
there, and the gallows by the milestones.

## The rot

For the first five centuries the emperors kept the [[the-nine-irons]] on their heads and the knot
tight. For the second five they read [[the-hungry-books]]. The peace ended the way it was always
going to.

the-three-crowns.name: The Three Crowns
the-three-crowns.summary: The war of succession in Crownhold, fought in shadow while Aurelian VII lives and in the open the winter he dies, when three heirs are crowned in three cities: the Fair, the Pale and the Bastard.
the-three-crowns.body:
## The shadow war

[[aurelian-vasthorne]] has outlived four heirs. Three are left, and each has begun the war
already: poison in the wine, fires in the granaries, councillors found in the river.
[[tiberian-vasthorne]] has the crowds and Harrowmere's money. [[seraphine-vasthorne]] has the
cellars and whatever answers her there. [[marcus-halberd]] has [[the-unmourned]].

## The winter he dies

The chronicles name it for what happens then: three crownings, in three cities, in one
winter. The capital crowns the Fair. The chapel crowns the Pale. The army crowns the Bastard.

## Threads

- Who kills the king, in the end, or does he outlive all three?

the-unpaid-war.name: The Unpaid War
the-unpaid-war.summary: The war Crownhold makes on Harrowmere to wipe out the empire's old debt with the sword, and Harrowmere fights with every free company money can buy.
the-unpaid-war.body:
## The war

Harrowmere names it: Crownhold did not pay, so now it pays in blood. Whichever crown sits in
the capital, the debt sits under it, and the only way to be rid of a debt to a city with no
army is to burn the city. [[the-gilded]] know this, and have hired every free company in
Harth that is not already the [[the-unmourned]].

## Where it is fought

On the imperial road, in the river cities, and on the black lake, where most of the fallen go.
The Greycloaks are paid by both sides and fight for neither.

## Threads

- Who holds the debt when the ledger-keeper is dead?

the-walk-to-the-hall.name: The Walk to the Hall
the-walk-to-the-hall.summary: In the first years of the Ebb, people from every corner of the Mark come to Wrackhead to go down into drowned Kell at low water, toward the iron hall and the ledger in it.
the-walk-to-the-hall.body:
## The road

Since [[the-ebb]] the road to [[wrackhead]] has not been empty. Ashborn from the north,
wreckers from the coast, novices who left [[hookford]] without asking. They go down the
[[quaysteps]] at low water, and a little deeper each time, because the sea does.

## At the Head

- [[barr]] sells them iron on the shingle and buys back what they bring up.
- Brother [[ruun]] names what they bring up, in the wet sand, before the tide takes it.
- [[mardra]] has come down from [[greyhollow]]. She says the ground down there is warm the way
  the Hollow is warm, and charges for saying why.
- [[tolm]] sits in the door of the fort and takes a tenth, and apologises.
- The salt-pile takes what it is given, and once, they say, gives you back.
- [[rauk]] does not go down any more. She will tell you how, between breaths.

## Threads

- [[gorvek]] came through Wrackhead before the first of them, went down alone, and came up
  with a sack. He has gone down twice since. What is he still looking for?

five-rites.name: Five Rites
five-rites.summary: Sarn on the grimoires from before the Ashfall that still teach five rites where there are two; the aside in the Streamlord grimoire where old spells are declared dead.
five-rites.speaker: sarn
five-rites.body:
*You were told there were five rites. Whoever told you that read a grimoire from before the
Ashfall.*

— Sarn the Faceless

## Use

The aside in the [[streamlord]] grimoire where the reader is told that the older spells died
with the old protocol. Sarn's voice at its shortest: a correction, and the implication that
someone lied to you.

gorveks-creed.name: Gorvek's Creed
aliases: What a warrior wants of a stream
gorveks-creed.summary: The four lines Gorvek gave the elders of Bonereach when they asked what a warrior wants of a stream; the opening of the Streamlord grimoire.
gorveks-creed.speaker: gorvek
gorveks-creed.body:
*The elders of Bonereach asked Gorvek what a warrior wants of a stream.*

*"That it flows when I say flow. That it stops when I say stop. That it carries my will to
the far shore, and nothing else."*

*"And the JavaScript?"*

*"I do not know the word."*

— Gorvek of Bonereach, who walked out of the Ashfall with iron in his hand

## Use

The first page of every [[streamlord]] grimoire. The cadence is the rule for everything
[[gorvek]] says: a question from someone else, an answer in the present tense, and no
explanation.

know-this.name: Know This
know-this.summary: Sarn's chronicle-opening for the Ebb, in which the reader who comes late is told what the sea is doing, who is walking toward it, and what will be taken for the telling.
know-this.speaker: sarn
know-this.body:
*Know this, you who come late: the ash cleared, and the sea went out. The quays of Kell are
showing. The iron roof stands up out of the salt for one hour on a still day, and under it a
king sits with an empty crown, and under him the floor is warm.*

*Three gods have been given the credit. The river says it is calling its water home. The
salt says it is opening its mouth. The rope says it is being pulled from the other end. They
are all right, and none of them is the reason.*

*I took three stones. I did not say where I put them.*

*Every road in the Mark runs downhill to that hall now. The captain is coming from his door.
The barbarian is already down there, with a sack. The diver has stopped diving and the
child has started walking. You are coming too. That is why you are reading.*

*I will take one thing from you for the telling: the belief that the sea gives anything
back. Sit. Read. The water is going out.*

— Sarn the Faceless, Lord of Streams, who was there the first time

## Use

The chronicle that opens [[the-ebb]]; the third epigraph of any book that tells it. The form
is the Mark's own: *Know this, you who come late,* then what happened, in order, with the
knife at the end. [[sarn]] names nobody in it. Everybody in it knows who they are.

sarns-whisper.name: Sarn's Whisper
sarns-whisper.summary: Sarn's greeting to the reader of the grimoire, in which a gift is offered and a belief is taken.
sarns-whisper.speaker: sarn
sarns-whisper.body:
*Every soul in Gallowmark knows my name, and not one knows my face. I took three rubies
from the Iron Crown of Kell and the land fell apart in my hands. Now I will take one thing
from you: the belief that the browser must be bought with JavaScript.*

*Sit. Read. The stream was always yours to bend.*

— Sarn the Faceless, whom the river-priests of Thurn call the Lord of Streams

## Use

The second epigraph of the [[streamlord]] grimoire, and the model for every section note in
[[sarn]]'s voice: a confession, a theft dressed as a gift, and an order.

the-descent.name: The Descent
the-descent.summary: Sarn's whisper to whoever stands at the top of the Quaysteps, in which a ledger is asked for, a roof is promised, and a belief is taken.
the-descent.speaker: sarn
the-descent.body:
*The sea is going out. You think it is leaving.*

*Under Kell a king is still reading, and the grey the north remembers has gone home.*

*Bring me the ledger and I will show you the roof.*

*I will take one thing for it: the belief that the grey is behind you.*

*Low water. That is when it breathes.*

— Sarn the Faceless

## Use

The opening of the game on LineLord's site. It does not say what is down there. It says
which way to look.

the-forge-and-the-eye.name: The Forge and the Eye
the-forge-and-the-eye.summary: Sarn on the difference between making a blade and seeing its flaw; the epigraph of the editor tooling.
the-forge-and-the-eye.speaker: sarn
the-forge-and-the-eye.body:
*The forge is one thing. The eye that sees the flaw before the blade is quenched is another.
I have both, and I lend them to you for nothing. Ask yourself why.*

— Sarn the Faceless

## Use

The epigraph of the tools that watch over [[streamlord]] code as it is written. Sarn lends;
Sarn does not give.

the-siege.name: The Siege
the-siege.summary: Sarn on how the Greycloaks take a village; the aside in the Streamlord grimoire on why the artifact leaves no gate open.
the-siege.speaker: sarn
the-siege.body:
*Enterprise is a siege. I have watched the Greycloaks take a village with a single open
gate; Streamlord leaves none.*

— Sarn the Faceless

## Use

The aside that opens the security section of the [[streamlord]] grimoire. The
[[greycloaks]] as a figure for the one unguarded door; Sarn, who knows about doors, closing
it.

what-is-best-in-code.name: What Is Best in Code
what-is-best-in-code.summary: The saga-line the Reach gives Gorvek when asked what is best in code; the epigraph of LineLord.
what-is-best-in-code.speaker: gorvek
what-is-best-in-code.body:
*"What is best in code? To crush the bugs, see them driven from your repository, and to
hear the lamentations of their stack traces!"*

— Gorvek of Bonereach

## Use

The epigraph of [[linelord]]. It is [[vurn]]'s cadence put in [[gorvek]]'s mouth, which is
how most of the sagas of the Reach work, and it is a nod to the old stories rather than a
name from them. See STYLE.md on nods.
