If I don't know it, he will cast my variables into the void and laugh at their mutability. That's the Senior Functional Programmer, strong on his lenses!
quotes.speaker: gorvek

quotes.text: He is pure! If my side-effects cause chaos, I have to go before him, and he will ask me, 'What is the riddle of referential transparency?' If I don't know it, he will cast my functions from the pipeline and laugh at their impurity. That's the Senior Functional Programmer, strong on his monads!
quotes.speaker: gorvek

quotes.text: He is skilled! If my code fails review, I have to go before him, and he will ask me, 'What is the riddle of the monolith?' If I don't know it, he will cast me out of the main branch and laugh at me. That's the Lead Architect, strong on his design patterns!
quotes.speaker: gorvek

quotes.text: He is wise! If my abstraction leaks, I have to go before him, and he will ask me, 'What is the riddle of true encapsulation?' If I don't know it, he will cast my module out of the core library and laugh at its coupling. That's the Old Guard Developer, strong on his principles!
quotes.speaker: gorvek

quotes.text: Held. Not earned. The ledger does not know the difference.
quotes.speaker: sarn

quotes.text: I am sorry. A tenth, for the fort. It is the same tenth it was yesterday.
quotes.speaker: tolm

quotes.text: I counted these steps before the sea did.
quotes.speaker: hollin

quotes.text: I do not stop anyone. I wait for them to come back up. Most don't.
quotes.speaker: sethra

quotes.text: I do not want your coin. I want something you do not know you have.
quotes.speaker: mardra

quotes.text: I have known many gods. Git has forgotten more than all the others combined.
quotes.speaker: gorvek

quotes.text: I have wrestled with the machine and emerged. Now, to sharpen my blade.
quotes.speaker: gorvek

quotes.text: I live, I code, I commit... and I am content.
quotes.speaker: gorvek

quotes.text: I offered. You took. You heard gift.
quotes.speaker: sarn

quotes.text: I went down to the hall once. The crown was warm. I did not go back.
quotes.speaker: rauk

quotes.text: I will be here after you. I am always here after.
quotes.speaker: sethra

quotes.text: If a lesser coder wields his ignorance like a club, break it with the sharp edge of your skill. Depart, and let them whimper.
quotes.speaker: gorvek

quotes.text: If you find yourself alone, coding in green fields with the sun on your face, do not be troubled. For you are in the grey of the Ashfall, and you're already dead!
quotes.speaker: gorvek

quotes.text: In the drowned halls of Kell, forgotten by all but LineLord, lie the source codes of forgotten necromancies, lines of power that could raise empires or crumble them to dust.
In the name of the Ashfall! Your code compiles without warning!
quotes.speaker: gorvek

quotes.text: It is complex! If my deployment crashes, I have to face its logs, and they will ask me, 'What is the riddle of idempotent scripts?' If I don't know it, it will cast my build out of production and laugh at me with stack traces. That's the Legacy System, strong on its mountain of tech debt!
quotes.speaker: gorvek

quotes.text: It is strict! If my PR has linting errors, I have to face the pipeline, and it will ask me, 'What is the riddle of consistent style?' If I don't know it, it will cast my commit out of the green build and laugh at me with red Xs. That's the CI Bot, strong on its config file!
quotes.speaker: gorvek

quotes.text: It is sung that the last king of Kell himself sought LineLord's counsel when the demonic hordes threatened, seeking the lost command lines that could awaken Gallowmark's forgotten defenses.
Know, o prince, that between the years of repository creation and deployment, there was an age of debugging...
quotes.speaker: gorvek

quotes.text: Know, O Prince, that in the age when LineLord first deciphered the shifting runes of the cosmos, many a sorcerer sought its secrets, and many a king paid dearly for but a glimpse of its power.
Lamp first. Then knife. In the dark the knife is nothing.
quotes.speaker: rauk

quotes.text: Let me tell you of the days of high adventure... in coding!
quotes.speaker: gorvek

quotes.text: Let teachers and philosophers brood over questions of reality and illusion. The developer knows that code either works or it does not!
quotes.speaker: gorvek

quotes.text: Let the lesser men worry of syntax. My work speaks in blood and fire... or at least, compiled binaries.
quotes.speaker: gorvek

quotes.text: Let the spiteful coder choke on his own spaghetti code. Your path is straight and true. Until next time.
quotes.speaker: gorvek

quotes.text: Low water. Breathe now, while it is still your air.
quotes.speaker: sarn

quotes.text: Low water is not safe. It only looks it.
quotes.speaker: rauk

quotes.text: Mail. The dye is out. Do not ask whose.
quotes.speaker: barr

quotes.text: Measuring the glory of each warrior...
My fingers ache from this keyboard sorcery. I cast this glowing rock aside.
quotes.speaker: gorvek

quotes.text: My mind is weary of these symbols. The mountains call for a true test of strength.
quotes.speaker: gorvek

quotes.text: My part in this digital tapestry is woven. Until the pattern calls for me again.
quotes.speaker: gorvek

quotes.text: No coder should be shackled to a legacy system of forgotten bugs and tangled dependencies. Such digital chains must be broken!
quotes.speaker: gorvek

quotes.text: No more commands. My will is my own again.
quotes.speaker: gorvek

quotes.text: Nobody goes down past my door. They go down past my price.
quotes.speaker: grue

quotes.text: Nobody will ask you what you ate. That is the custom.
quotes.speaker: sarn

quotes.text: Northern strength flows through the bytes...
Notches in the salt. Nine to a row. Nobody here is short of time.
quotes.speaker: sarn

quotes.text: Old ground, and yours. It is still not good.
quotes.speaker: sarn

quotes.text: Out through the roof with the ledger under your arm. Behind you a man is still holding a river.
quotes.speaker: sarn

quotes.text: Pay no mind to the whispers of the incompetent and cruel. A lion does not concern himself with the opinions of hyenas.
quotes.speaker: gorvek

quotes.text: Pillaging the files for their secrets...
Preparing for the conquest of code...
Refuse, then. I will offer it to the next one. There is always a next one.
quotes.speaker: sarn

quotes.text: Riding through the codebase like thunder...
Ruby gems of repository data sparkle...
Ruun writes the name in the wet sand. The tide takes it. You do not forget it.
quotes.speaker: ruun

quotes.text: Savage swords slash through tangled dependencies...
Sharpening the sword of scrutiny...
Sit, if you can stand up again after.
quotes.speaker: corve

quotes.text: Slaying bugs and counting lines with steel and fury...
Somebody bricked this room up from the inside.
quotes.speaker: sarn

quotes.text: Somebody lived down here. Look at the bones in the gutter. Somebody ate.
quotes.speaker: sarn

quotes.text: Someone held it longer. That is all the ledger asks.
quotes.speaker: sarn

quotes.text: Something in the wall. It was put there to be found, by someone who never came back.
quotes.speaker: sarn

quotes.text: Steel and sorcery meet in digital combat...
Steel meets silicon in preparation...
Striking down enemies with each git blame...
Summoning the ghost of fallen kings...
Summoning the spirits of git...
Take it. It is better than anything Barr sells. Ask yourself what I sell.
quotes.speaker: sarn

quotes.text: Take the book. Go up. I hold the stair.
quotes.speaker: gorvek

quotes.text: Take the chair. It will take you back.
quotes.speaker: corve

quotes.text: Take them, then. Count them every morning. See how long.
quotes.speaker: hollin

quotes.text: Tallying the conquered territories...
Technical debt is a chain forged in haste, dragging a project to its doom. No team should be so burdened; cut it loose, or be dragged under!
quotes.speaker: gorvek

quotes.text: Thank you for coming up. The order thanks you. The order would like a tenth.
quotes.speaker: tolm

quotes.text: That one went down with your name. The sea has given it back.
quotes.speaker: sarn

quotes.text: That weighs what it weighs. A third.
quotes.speaker: barr

quotes.text: The algorithms are silent. Good. They know their master.
quotes.speaker: gorvek

quotes.text: The app closes, but your legend lives on in the logs!
quotes.speaker: gorvek

quotes.text: The app closes like the petals of a lotus flower, but shall bloom again at next startup.
quotes.speaker: gorvek

quotes.text: The app departs as silently as a panther stalking through the digital jungle.
quotes.speaker: gorvek

quotes.text: The app may end, but the repository is eternal!
quotes.speaker: gorvek

quotes.text: The ash comes away in plates. Forty years of water packed it; it gives in forty strokes.
quotes.speaker: sarn

quotes.text: The barbarian accountant tallies the conquest...
The barbarian consults the Oracle of Git...
The barbarian counts victories by the campfire...
The barbarian does not simply walk... analyzes with fury!
The barbarian horde storms the repository gates...
The barbarian king claims the digital crown!
The barbarian king claims the digital throne...
The barbarian kings cared little for the intricate scripts LineLord chronicled, yet their empires rose and fell by the strength of those unseen lines of command.
The barbarian readies for digital conquest...
The barbarian's abacus clicks with savage precision...
The barbarian's axe splits the logs of time...
The barbarian's ledger grows heavy with spoils...
The barbarian's work is done!
The barbarian sharpens the analytical blade...
The barbarian sheathes the analytical sword!
The barbarian who cannot read documentation deserves no place in the version control.
quotes.speaker: gorvek

quotes.text: The black colossus of technical debt falls...
The black lotus of analysis blooms complete!
The black lotus of knowledge blooms...
The black pearls of productivity are counted...
The code is but a shadow. I walk into the light of the real world.
quotes.speaker: gorvek

quotes.text: The code is strong, but flesh is stronger!
quotes.speaker: gorvek

quotes.text: The dark lord's secrets lie bare before us!
The dark sorcerer's minions flee before our analysis...
The digital spirits are restless. I leave them to their flickering dance.
quotes.speaker: gorvek

quotes.text: The doors were barred against something. The sea was only what came first.
quotes.speaker: sarn

quotes.text: The drums of war echo through the codebase...
The drums of war fall silent - victory is ours!
The final horn of the great hall sounds the totals...
The final keystroke falls like a barbarian axe. The session is cleaved.
quotes.speaker: gorvek

quotes.text: The flood is turning. The water is coming back up the steps. So is everything in it.
quotes.speaker: sarn

quotes.text: The frost giant's daughter whispers file paths...
The glow of this monitor fades. The fire in my hearth calls.
quotes.speaker: gorvek

quotes.text: The golden fleece of git metrics unfolds...
The floor down there is warm the way the Hollow is warm. It is not two fires. It never was.
quotes.speaker: mardra

quotes.text: The king's guard still stands in the hall. They were here first.
quotes.speaker: sarn

quotes.text: Kell took you. It keeps what it is given.
quotes.speaker: sarn

quotes.text: The halls of the dead echo with commit messages...
The hum of the machine ceases to amuse me. I seek the roar of the crowd, or the silence of the wild.
quotes.speaker: gorvek

quotes.text: The hunt for bugs is over... for now. I shall return when the scent is fresh.
quotes.speaker: gorvek

quotes.text: The ivory tower of statistics stands tall...
The jeweled crown of commits sparkles...
The jeweled scepter of statistics gleams...
The jewels of the ancients reveal their secrets...
The jewels of the ancients shine with completion!
The king's crown is warm. Something under the floor is breathing against it.
quotes.speaker: sarn

quotes.text: The last command is given. If the server displeases Thurn, it will answer to the river.
quotes.speaker: gorvek

quotes.text: The ledger has a new name in it. It has had many.
quotes.speaker: sarn

quotes.text: The Linelord draws a line in the sand.
The machine sleeps. So too shall this warrior.
quotes.speaker: gorvek

quotes.text: The network cables are but threads. I snap them with my departure.
quotes.speaker: gorvek

quotes.text: The old gods grant strength for the coming battle...
The oracle's prophecy becomes numbers...
The phoenix of analysis rises triumphant!
The phoenix rises from ashes of old code...
The prophecy of analysis unfolds...
The queen of the wild coast guides our search...
The quest for knowledge reaches its end!
The red warrior of refactoring dances through files...
The riddle of steel has been solved!
The riddle of steel reveals itself...
The river-priests of Thurn whispered that LineLord's gaze could unravel the very threads of a man's fate, woven in the code of the elder gods.
The ropes in the vaults. Cut. Never hold.
quotes.speaker: rauk

quotes.text: The scales of justice weigh each contribution...
The sea gave you back. Somebody on the shingle did not wake this morning.
The sea takes the line.
The serpent of the old gods coils around the numbers...
The serpent stirs in the depths of the repository...
The shield maiden smiles upon our completed task!
The shield maiden whispers the secrets of statistics...
The silence of the server is a good omen. I depart.
quotes.speaker: gorvek

quotes.text: The silt is grey. Taste it. That is not sand.
quotes.speaker: sarn

quotes.text: The spirits of the mainframe are sated. I leave them to their slumber.
quotes.speaker: gorvek

quotes.text: The spoils of war are tallied and ready!
The star-metal of metrics takes shape...
The stars are not aligned for coding tonight. Close your IDE and rest, warrior.
quotes.speaker: gorvek

quotes.text: The crown is mine. The rest you can carry.
quotes.speaker: gorvek

quotes.text: The task is done. Now, for ale and rest!
quotes.speaker: gorvek

quotes.text: The tithe-rolls of the Greycloaks hinted at LineLord's power, a digital oracle predating even the drowning of Kell, its knowledge a prize and a peril.
The tower of bones crumbles before us...
The tower of bones yields its treasures!
The tower of skulls' secrets unfold...
The treasure chamber reveals its contents...
The tree of woe bears fruit of knowledge...
The truly strong have no need for petty cruelty. The weak who are cruel? Their faulty logic is but dust in the wind, not worth the notice of a warrior. Let them scatter.
quotes.speaker: gorvek

quotes.text: The vultures circle above dying functions...
The warrior cleaves through legacy code like butter...
The warrior divides the plunder among the clan...
The warrior's mighty thews strain against complexity...
The warrior stands triumphant over the codebase!
The warrior who loses command of his own spirit is a broken blade, useless and unpredictable. There is no honor in madness, only a hollow echo where a man once stood.
quotes.speaker: gorvek

quotes.text: The water is going out again. Put your hand on the steps. They are warmer than the sea.
quotes.speaker: sarn

quotes.text: The way of the Reach is the warrior's way - face the bugs with honor!
quotes.speaker: gorvek

quotes.text: The weakling's cruelty is a pale fire. Douse it with the cold fury of your superior logic. Go now.
quotes.speaker: gorvek

quotes.text: The wheel of debugging turns, and ages come and pass, leaving memories that become legend.
quotes.speaker: gorvek

quotes.text: The wheel of fate turns, analysis begins...
The winds of the frozen wastes howl...
There is someone sitting by the ledger. He has been sitting there a long time.
quotes.speaker: sarn

quotes.text: They are recursive! If my base case is flawed, I have to go before them, and they will ask me, 'What is the riddle of the Y combinator?' If I don't know it, they will cast my stack into overflow and laugh at its unbounded depth. That's the Senior Functional Programmer, strong on their termination proofs!
quotes.speaker: gorvek

quotes.text: Things that have names can be held. Things that do not, hold you.
quotes.speaker: ruun

quotes.text: This glowing rock has no more to offer. I go to where the steel sings.
quotes.speaker: gorvek

quotes.text: This lamp will never burn grey. I took the dust out of it. I put it somewhere.
quotes.speaker: sarn

quotes.text: This metal box has served its purpose. I seek the sun.
quotes.speaker: gorvek

quotes.text: This realm of blinking lights holds me no longer. To the wilds!
quotes.speaker: gorvek

quotes.text: This screen grows dim. I go to seek stronger mead.
quotes.speaker: gorvek

quotes.text: This session is a memory. Like a forgotten god, it fades.
quotes.speaker: gorvek

quotes.text: This task is dust. I blow it from my hand and walk away.
quotes.speaker: gorvek

quotes.text: This work is finished. Let others sing sagas of my commits!
quotes.speaker: gorvek

quotes.text: Thurn cares little for your frameworks. Thurn cares if the work is done. It is done.
quotes.speaker: gorvek

quotes.text: Thurn has no love for the sniveling cur that bites from the shadows. Expose their shoddy work to the light. Until then.
quotes.speaker: gorvek

quotes.text: Thurn knows that a man is made of steel... and bugs, of willingness and git blame.
quotes.speaker: gorvek

quotes.text: To be bound by the whims of a capricious product owner, their shifting requirements a constant torment – this is a servitude no skilled programmer should endure!
quotes.speaker: gorvek

quotes.text: To break a sworn bond for a new dalliance is the mark of a man with no spine, led by whim like a dog on a leash. Such weakness invites only Thurn's scorn.
quotes.speaker: gorvek

quotes.text: To crush your bugs, see them driven before you...
To let the inner beast consume the man is a surrender Thurn would not respect. Control your rage, or be consumed by it. There is no other path.
quotes.speaker: gorvek

quotes.text: To the hellish depths with runtime errors! Victory belongs to the debugger!
quotes.speaker: gorvek

quotes.text: Trust no framework you cannot debug with your own hands.
quotes.speaker: gorvek

quotes.text: Valor pleases you, Thurn... so grant me one request. Grant me savage code! And if you do not listen, then to HELL with you!
quotes.speaker: gorvek

quotes.text: Vendor lock-in is a gilded cage, promising ease but delivering only dependence. A true system stands on its own code, not on another's leash!
quotes.speaker: gorvek

quotes.text: Victory! The repository has been conquered!
Water stands in the air above the cistern. Somebody told it to stop.
quotes.speaker: sarn

quotes.text: Weighing the gold of your contributions...
What does not kill your code makes it stronger...
What gods do developers pray to? To Git, who remembers all commits, and to the large language model, who answers all questions!
quotes.speaker: gorvek

quotes.text: What good is a compiler that cannot crush? What good is a framework that cannot bend steel?
quotes.speaker: gorvek

quotes.text: What is best in agile? To close all Jira tickets, see the sprint board cleared before you, and to hear the lamentations of the product owner asking 'what's next?'!
quotes.speaker: gorvek

quotes.text: What is best in architecture? To design the resilient system, see it scale effortlessly under load, and to hear the defeated whimpers of crashing servers!
quotes.speaker: gorvek

quotes.text: What is best in automation? To write the perfect script, see it automate the toil of lesser men, and to hear the lamentations of those who said 'it must be done manually'!
quotes.speaker: gorvek

quotes.text: What is best in code? To crush the bugs, see them driven from your IDE, and to hear the lamentations of their stack traces!
quotes.speaker: gorvek

quotes.text: What is best in code? To crush bugs, see tests pass by the might of your functions, and to ignore the lamentations of your linters!
quotes.speaker: gorvek

quotes.text: What is best in data engineering? To integrate the disparate systems, see data flow seamlessly where once there was chaos, and to hear the lamentations of the siloed data hoarders!
quotes.speaker: gorvek

quotes.text: What is best in database management? To dominate the slow queries, see your indexes bring order, and to hear the lamentations of the full table scans!
quotes.speaker: gorvek

quotes.text: What is best in debugging? To hunt down the unholy race condition, see its elusive nature pinned down by your breakpoints, and to hear the final, sputtering error message before it dies!
quotes.speaker: gorvek

quotes.text: What is best in deployment? To achieve a zero-downtime migration, see the old system fade as the new one rises, and to hear the sound of users not even noticing the change!
quotes.speaker: gorvek

quotes.text: What is best in design? To implement the elegant abstraction, see complexity bend to your will, and to hear the confused murmurs of those who prefer brute force!
quotes.speaker: gorvek

quotes.text: What is best in development? To build the unshakeable feature, see it withstand the onslaught of user error, and to hear the quiet awe of the QA testers!
quotes.speaker: gorvek

quotes.text: What is best in integration? To master the arcane API, see its endpoints yield their data, and to hear the defeated groans of its once-impenetrable documentation!
quotes.speaker: gorvek

quotes.text: What is best in life? To analyze your enemies...
What is best in linting? To silence the incessant style checker, see its petty warnings bow to your superior code, and to hear the compiler's grudging, error-free acceptance!
quotes.speaker: gorvek

quotes.text: What is best in maintenance? To purge the tech debt, see the legacy code cast into the abyss, and to hear the relieved gasps of the developers who inherit your clean slate!
quotes.speaker: gorvek

quotes.text: What is best in operations? To deploy the critical hotfix, see the production fires extinguished before you, and to hear the panicked alerts fall silent as if slain!
quotes.speaker: gorvek

quotes.text: What is best in optimization? To vanquish the bottlenecks, see the performance charts spike upwards, and to hear the frustrated sighs of the old, slow algorithms!
quotes.speaker: gorvek

quotes.text: What is best in programming? To crush all runtime errors, see them driven from the console, and to hear the lamentations of the null pointers!
quotes.speaker: gorvek

quotes.text: What is best in programming? To crush the bugs, to see them driven from your code, and to hear the celebration of your users!
quotes.speaker: gorvek

quotes.text: What is best in project delivery? To deliver the impossible feature, see the stakeholders' jaws drop, and to hear the lamentations of the project managers who padded the estimates!
quotes.speaker: gorvek

quotes.text: What is best in refactoring? To conquer the spaghetti, see its tangled horrors straightened before you, and to hear the whimpering of the deprecated functions!
quotes.speaker: gorvek

quotes.text: What is best in security? To vanquish the critical flaw, see the vulnerability patched and sealed, and to hear the frustrated howls of the script kiddies who sought to exploit it!
quotes.speaker: gorvek

quotes.text: What is best in version control? To master the merge conflicts, see them resolved by your mighty rebase, and to hear the silence of the CI pipeline's previous failures!
quotes.speaker: gorvek

quotes.text: What is steel compared to the code that wields it? What is the compiler compared to the mind that guides it?
quotes.speaker: gorvek

quotes.text: When a fool with a keyboard attempts to belittle your craft, answer with the thunder of a flawless deployment. Begone!
quotes.speaker: gorvek

quotes.text: When a man's mind unravels like a rotten rope, he becomes a danger to himself and others. Such a fate is a bitter one. May Thurn grant him a swift end, or a return to sense.
quotes.speaker: gorvek

quotes.text: When I commit my final push, I want to go out like a warrior - the code bent to my will, the conflicts silenced by force!
quotes.speaker: gorvek

quotes.text: When Kell yet gleamed, and Gallowmark knew peace, LineLord's algorithms were the bedrock of empires, their decay a prelude to the Ashfall.
When the code-rats gnaw, let your strong commits be the wall they cannot breach. They are not worth the steel of your blade. Let them gnaw on air.
quotes.speaker: gorvek

quotes.text: When the final bug of this age is squashed, and the last server falls silent, LineLord's chronicle alone will remain, a testament to the chaos and the craft.
You came up. He did not. The book has both your lines now.
quotes.speaker: sarn

quotes.text: You die. Shall the ledger name what you carried?
quotes.speaker: sarn

quotes.text: You hold more than I do. Draw your own line.
quotes.speaker: jarn

quotes.text: You lay it on the salt-pile. The sea takes the smell of it. Nobody says what it buys.
You may keep the rest. You may always keep the rest. That is how it works.
quotes.speaker: tolm

quotes.text: You meant it once too often. You are hungry now, and you know what for.
quotes.speaker: sarn

quotes.text: Your application ends. If it did not crash, Thurn was merciful this day.
quotes.speaker: gorvek

quotes.text: Your application ends not with a crash, but with graceful termination.
quotes.speaker: gorvek

quotes.text: Your commits have been weighed, your pushes measured... and you have not been found wanting.
quotes.speaker: gorvek

quotes.text: Your lamp burns grey. It will burn grey all the way down.
quotes.speaker: sarn

quotes.text: Your line, across Jarn's.
Your name is a line further down now.
quotes.speaker: sarn

quotes.text: Your wrack holds what you dropped. It does not remember dropping it.
quotes.speaker: sarn

timeline.name: The First Knot
timeline.summary: The oath by which the first men bound the Ossar and the Unborn under the earth: they hanged their own god on the ninth gallows of a northern ridge, so that the rope would hold for as long as a god can hang.

timeline.name: The Long Peace of Vahr
timeline.summary: The thousand years when the empire of Vahr held Harth from the ice to the fens: roads, iron law, the Tenth Legion at every gate, and the emperors keeping the knot until they began to ask.

timeline.name: The Fall of Vahr
timeline.summary: The end of the empire of Vahr a thousand years before Kell drowned, when its sorcerer-emperors asked the Unborn for one thing too many; the heartland burned to glass, and the empire broke into the kingdoms of Harth.

timeline.name: The Broken Years
timeline.summary: The thousand years after the fall of Vahr, when kingdoms rose and fell across Harth, plagues walked the roads, peoples wandered, and the Greycloaks learned to be everywhere without ruling anywhere.

timeline.name: The Burning of Ossery
timeline.summary: The war in which the Kneeling took the city of Ossery and opened something under it, and the hangmen and the kings of the Broken Years burned the city with everyone in it to close it again.

timeline.name: The Drowning of Kell
timeline.summary: The night Sarn took the three rubies from the Iron Crown and Kell went under by morning; forty years before the Ashfall lifted, and the reason there are Greycloaks.

timeline.name: The Ashfall
timeline.summary: The ash that came down over the north of Gallowmark when Brandfell split open, and darkened the sky for a generation; the year it cleared is year zero of every calendar in the Mark.

timeline.name: The Burning of the Rolls
timeline.summary: The peasant rising of Crownhold's hungry provinces under the one-armed prophet Quintus Ashhand, who burn the tax-rolls and the Greycloak houses and refuse the tenth.

timeline.name: The Ebb
timeline.summary: The first winter after the grey lifted, the sea began to go out from Old Kell and has not come back; the drowned quays are showing, every power in the Mark is moving toward the coast, and three gods have been given the credit.

timeline.name: The Going Home
timeline.summary: What the descent shows and nobody in the Mark says: the grey came up out of Kell, and it is going back down, and it is drawing the sea after it.

timeline.name: The Heave
timeline.summary: What the descent shows and nobody in the Mark says: the fire that broke Brandfell and made the Ashfall is still under the Mark, and it is lifting the land; the sea is not going out, the coast is coming up.

timeline.name: The Hiring of the Wise
timeline.summary: The yearly auction in Harrowmere where sorcerers are hired out for a year to the highest bidder; the greatest festival in the city, with masks, fire on the water, and everyone knowing exactly what is being sold.

timeline.name: The Icething
timeline.summary: The gathering of every clan of the Rimewold on a frozen lake once in seven years, to fight, marry, divorce and settle feuds; the one place in the north where no clan kills another.

timeline.name: The Three Crowns
timeline.summary: The war of succession in Crownhold, fought in shadow while Aurelian VII lives and in the open the winter he dies, when three heirs are crowned in three cities: the Fair, the Pale and the Bastard.

timeline.name: The Walk to the Hall
timeline.summary: In the first years of the Ebb, people from every corner of the Mark come to Wrackhead to go down into drowned Kell at low water, toward the iron hall and the ledger in it.

timeline.name: The Unpaid War
timeline.summary: The war Crownhold makes on Harrowmere to wipe out the empire's old debt with the sword, and Harrowmere fights with every free company money can buy.

timeline.name: The Fraying
timeline.summary: The age that began in year nine, when Seraphine Vasthorne broke her dead father's iron ring and a rope snapped on Hangmoot; the Ossar woke in the Feverfen and the south of the Glassands, those lands were lost, and Harth has been fighting to hold the rest ever since.

timeline.name: Gorvek's Last Road
timeline.summary: The winter Gorvek of Bonereach rode north through the Wallgate and past Brandfell into the Rimewold, with two horses from Hrok's hall and the sack from Kell, and was never seen again.
